title.en: Volume 306 Biographies 194: Eunuchs - Jiao Fang, Zhang Cai, Gu Bingqian, Cui Chengxiu, Liu Zhixuan, Cao Qincheng, Wang Shaohui, Huo Weihua, Yan Mingtai, Jia Jichun, Tian Ergeng
title.raw: 卷三百〇六 列傳第一百九十四 閹黨 焦芳 張綵 顧秉謙 崔呈秀 劉志選 曹欽程 王紹徽 霍維華 閻鳴泰 賈繼春 田爾耕 Volume 306 Biographies 194: Eunuchs - Jiao Fang, Zhang Cai, Gu Bingqian, Cui Chengxiu, Liu Zhixuan, Cao Qincheng, Wang Shaohui, Huo Weihua, Yan Mingtai, Jia Jichun, Tian Ergeng

sentences.zh: 明代閹宦之禍酷矣，然非諸黨人附麗之，羽翼之，張其勢而助之攻，虐焰不若是其烈也。

translations.literal: The calamity of eunuchs in the Ming dynasty was severe indeed; yet had not the various faction members clung to them, winged them, expanded their power and aided their attacks, the cruel flame would not have burned so fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The harm wrought by eunuchs in the Ming was dreadful enough, but without court factions clinging to them, lending them wings, inflating their power, and helping them strike down their foes, the tyranny would never have blazed so hot.

sentences.zh: 中葉以前，士大夫知重名節，雖以王振、汪直之橫，黨與未盛。

translations.literal: Before the mid-dynasty, scholar-officials knew to value reputation and integrity; although Wang Zhen and Wang Zhi were overbearing, factional followings had not yet flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mid-Ming, literati still prized honor and integrity; even when Wang Zhen and Wang Zhi ran rampant, factional networks had not yet taken hold.

sentences.zh: 至劉瑾竊權，焦芳以閣臣首與之比，於是列卿爭先獻媚，而司禮之權居內閣上。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin usurped power, Jiao Fang as chief Grand Secretary was the first to associate with him; thereupon the chief ministers vied to offer flattery, and the authority of the Directorate of Ceremonial stood above the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Jin seized power and Grand Secretary Jiao Fang led the cabinet in courting him, senior ministers scrambled to flatter the eunuchs, and the Directorate of Ceremonial came to outrank the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 迨神宗末年，訛言朋興，群相敵仇，門戶之爭固結而不可解。

translations.literal: By the late years of Emperor Shenzong, slander and factions arose together; groups became mutual enemies, and partisan strife hardened until it could not be undone.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Shenzong's reign, rumor and factionalism ran wild; rival camps treated one another as mortal foes, and partisan warfare had set like cement.

sentences.zh: 兇豎乘其沸潰，盜弄太阿，黠桀渠憸，竄身婦寺。

translations.literal: Vicious minions seized upon the boiling collapse, stole and wielded the imperial sword; cunning ruffians and crafty villains slipped into the women's quarters and eunuch offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked henchmen exploited the turmoil, usurped the sword of state, and cunning rogues hid themselves behind palace women and eunuch chambers.

sentences.zh: 淫刑痡毒，快其惡正醜直之私。

translations.literal: Licentious punishments festered with poison, gratifying their private hatred of the upright and their loathing of the straight.
translations.idiomatic: They inflicted cruel and corrupt punishments to satisfy their spite against honest men and their envy of the forthright.

sentences.zh: 衣冠填於狴犴，善類殞於刀鋸。

translations.literal: Officials in caps and robes filled the prisons; good men perished under blade and saw.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry crowded the jails, and worthy men fell to the executioner's blade.

sentences.zh: 迄乎惡貫滿盈，亟伸憲典，刑書所麗，跡穢簡編，而遺孽余燼，終以覆國。

translations.literal: When their evil reached its fullness, the penal code was swiftly applied; where the law books recorded them, their traces defiled the annals—yet the surviving spawn and lingering embers in the end overturned the state.
translations.idiomatic: When their crimes had run their course, justice was at last enforced and their names stained the legal records and the histories; yet the embers they left behind still brought down the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝之定逆案也，以其事付大學士韓爌等，因慨然太息曰：「忠賢不過一人耳，外廷諸臣附之，遂至於此，其罪何可勝誅！」

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie settled the treason cases, he entrusted the matter to Grand Secretary Han Kuang and others, and sighed deeply, saying: "Zhongxian was but one man; the outer-court ministers attached themselves to him and things came to this—how can their guilt be exhaustively punished!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor settled the treason cases, he handed the matter to Grand Secretary Han Kuang and his colleagues and sighed: "Wei Zhongxian was only one man; it was the outer-court ministers who rallied to him and brought matters to this pass—how could their guilt ever be fully punished!"

sentences.zh: 痛乎哉，患得患失之鄙夫，其流毒誠無所窮極也！

translations.literal: Alas! Petty men who fret over gain and loss—the poison they spread truly knows no limit!
translations.idiomatic: Alas for those petty men who clutch at gain and fear loss—the harm they spread truly has no end!

sentences.zh: 今錄自焦芳、張綵以下，迄天啟朝，為《閹黨列傳》，用垂鑒誡。

translations.literal: Now recording from Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai downward through the Tianqi reign, this is made the 《Biographies of the Eunuch Faction》, to serve as warning and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records from Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai down through the Tianqi reign as the 《Biographies of the Eunuch Faction》, set down as a lesson for posterity.

sentences.zh: 其以功名表見，或晚節自蓋，如王驥、王越、楊維垣、張捷之徒，則仍別見焉。

translations.literal: Those who achieved distinction through merit, or who covered themselves in their later years, such as Wang Ji, Wang Yue, Yang Weiyuan, Zhang Jie, and the like, are still treated in separate accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Men who won fame through genuine achievement, or who redeemed themselves late in life—such as Wang Ji, Wang Yue, Yang Weiyuan, and Zhang Jie—are given separate biographies elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 焦芳，泌陽人。

translations.literal: Jiao Fang was a native of Biyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang was from Biyang.

sentences.zh: 天順八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eighth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1464.

sentences.zh: 大學士李賢以同鄉故，引為庶吉士，授編修，進侍講。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Xian, being a fellow townsman, recommended him as a Hanlin bachelor; he was appointed Compiler, then promoted to Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Xian, a fellow native of Biyang, sponsored him as a Hanlin bachelor; Fang was made a compiler and later promoted to court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 滿九年考，當遷學士。

translations.literal: When his nine-year review was complete, he was due for promotion to Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years of service he was due for promotion to Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 或語大學士萬安：「不學如芳，亦學士乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Grand Secretary Wan An: "One so unlearned as Fang—should he also become a bachelor?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone remarked to Grand Secretary Wan An, "Should a man as ignorant as Fang become a bachelor?"

sentences.zh: 芳聞大恚曰：「是必彭華間我也。

translations.literal: Fang heard this and raged: "This must be Peng Hua slandering me.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang heard, he flew into a rage: "Peng Hua must have turned them against me.

sentences.zh: 我不學士，且刺華長安道中。」

translations.literal: If I am not made bachelor, I shall stab Hua on the Chang'an road."
translations.idiomatic: If I am not made bachelor, I will stab Hua on the road in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 華懼，言於安，乃進芳侍講學士。

translations.literal: Hua was afraid and spoke to An; Fang was then advanced to Lecturing Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was terrified and appealed to Wan An, who then had Fang promoted to lecturing bachelor.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔纂《文華大訓》，進講東宮，其書皆華等所為。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had ordered the compilation of the 《Great Instructions of Wenhua》 for lectures in the Eastern Palace; the book had all been written by Hua and others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the court had ordered the compilation of the 《Great Instructions of Wenhua》 for lectures in the crown prince's palace; Peng Hua and his colleagues had written the entire work.

sentences.zh: 芳恥不與，每進講，故摘其疵，揚言眾中。

translations.literal: Fang was ashamed not to have participated; whenever he lectured, he deliberately picked out flaws and proclaimed them before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to have been left out, Fang seized every lecture to pick flaws in the text and broadcast them before the court.

sentences.zh: 翰林尚文采，獨芳粗陋無學識，性陰很，動輒議訕，人鹹畏避之。

translations.literal: The Hanlin prized literary polish; Fang alone was crude and without learning, of a secretive and spiteful nature, always ready to mock and slander—everyone feared and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin valued literary polish, but Fang was coarse and ignorant, secretive and spiteful, always ready to mock and slander; everyone feared and shunned him.

sentences.zh: 尹旻之罷也，芳與其子龍相比，謫桂陽州同知。

translations.literal: When Yin Min was dismissed, Fang was compared with his son Long and demoted to Vice Magistrate of Guiyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Min was dismissed from office, Fang was lumped together with Yin's son Long and demoted to vice magistrate of Guiyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 芳知出華、安二人指，銜次骨。

translations.literal: Fang knew this came from the direction of Hua and An, and bore a grudge to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Fang knew Peng Hua and Wan An were behind his fall and nursed a grudge to the bone.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，移霍州知州，擢四川提學副使，調湖廣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, he was transferred to Magistrate of Huozhou, then promoted to Vice Commissioner of Education in Sichuan and transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he was moved to magistrate of Huozhou, then promoted to vice commissioner of education in Sichuan and transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷南京右通政，以憂歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Right Vice Commissioner in Nanjing, then returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made right vice commissioner in Nanjing, then went home to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授太常少卿兼侍講學士，尋擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and concurrent Lecturing Bachelor, and soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was appointed vice minister of rites and concurrent lecturing bachelor, and soon promoted to right vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 怨劉健尼己，日於眾中嫚罵。

translations.literal: Resenting Liu Jian for obstructing him, he daily hurled abuse in public gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: He resented Liu Jian for blocking his rise and daily hurled abuse at him in public.

sentences.zh: 健判牒不可意，即引筆抹去，不關白尚書。

translations.literal: When Jian's written decisions displeased him, he would take up the brush and strike them out without informing the Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he disliked a decision Liu Jian had drafted, he would strike it out with his own brush without telling the minister.

sentences.zh: 俄改吏部，轉左侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 馬文升為尚書，芳輒加姍侮，陰結言官，使抨擊素所不快及在己上者。

translations.literal: When Ma Wensheng became Minister, Fang constantly heaped insults upon him, secretly allied with censorial officials, and had them attack those he had long disliked and those above him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Wensheng became minister, Fang constantly insulted him, secretly enlisted censors, and set them on men he disliked and on anyone ranked above him.

sentences.zh: 又上言禦邊四事以希進用，為謝遷所抑，尤憾遷。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on four matters of frontier defense hoping for advancement, but was blocked by Xie Qian; he especially resented Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial on four frontier policies hoping for promotion, but Xie Qian blocked it, and he hated Qian all the more.

sentences.zh: 每言及余姚、江西人，以遷及華故，肆口詬詈。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of men from Yuyao or Jiangxi—because of Qian and Hua—he would open his mouth in curses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yuyao or Jiangxi men came up—because of Qian and Hua—he would break into open abuse.

sentences.zh: 芳既積忤廷臣，復銳進，乃深結閹宦以自固，日夜謀逐健、遷，代其位。

translations.literal: Fang having long offended court ministers yet still eager to advance, he deeply bonded with eunuchs to secure himself, day and night plotting to drive out Jian and Qian and take their places.
translations.idiomatic: Having long alienated the court yet still hungry for power, Fang threw in his lot with the eunuchs and plotted day and night to oust Liu Jian and Xie Qian and take their posts.

sentences.zh: 正德初，戶部尚書韓文言會計不足。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, Minister of Revenue Han Wen spoke of insufficient accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign, Minister of Revenue Han Wen reported that the treasury was short.

sentences.zh: 廷議謂理財無奇術，唯勸上節儉。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that managing finances had no special art—only to urge the emperor toward frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed there was no magic to balancing the books and that the emperor should simply spend less.

sentences.zh: 芳知左右有竊聽者，大言曰：「庶民家尚須用度，況縣官耶？

translations.literal: Fang knew there were eavesdroppers nearby and spoke loudly: "Even common households need expenditures—how much more the state?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor's attendants were listening in, Fang declared loudly, "Even common households need money to live—how much more the state?

sentences.zh: 諺雲『無錢揀故紙』。

translations.literal: As the proverb says, 'Without money, one picks over old paper.'
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, 'When you're broke, you sort through old paper.'

sentences.zh: 今天下逋租匿稅何限，不是檢索，而但雲損上何也？」

translations.literal: Today how limitless are delinquent rents and concealed taxes in the realm—not to search them out, but only to speak of cutting the sovereign's expenses—why is this?"
translations.idiomatic: How much delinquent rent and hidden tax is there under heaven? The answer is not to cut the emperor's spending but to collect what is owed—why talk only of austerity?

sentences.zh: 武宗聞之大喜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong heard this and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengde Emperor heard this and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 會文升去，遂擢為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Wensheng departed, Fang was then promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Wensheng left office, Fang was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 韓文將率九卿劾劉瑾，疏當首吏部，以告芳。

translations.literal: Han Wen was about to lead the Nine Ministers in impeaching Liu Jin; the memorial should have been headed by the Ministry of Personnel, and he told Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wen was preparing to lead the Nine Ministers in impeaching Liu Jin; as minister of personnel his name would head the memorial, and he confided in Fang.

sentences.zh: 芳陰泄其謀於瑾。

translations.literal: Fang secretly revealed the plot to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fang secretly tipped Jin off.

sentences.zh: 瑾遂逐文及健、遷輩，而芳以本官兼文淵閣大學士，入閣輔政，累加少師、華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: Jin then drove out Wen and Jian, Qian, and their fellows; Fang with his original office concurrently became Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, entered the cabinet to assist in government, and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Preceptor and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then purged Han Wen, Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and their allies; Fang kept his ministry post while joining the Grand Secretariat as a grand secretary of Wenyuan Pavilion, and was later made junior preceptor and grand secretary of Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 居內閣數年，瑾濁亂海內，變置成法，荼毒縉紳，皆芳導之。

translations.literal: During several years in the cabinet, Jin corrupted the realm, altered established laws, and poisoned the gentry—all guided by Fang.
translations.idiomatic: For years in the cabinet Fang guided Jin as he corrupted the realm, overturned established law, and ravaged the official class.

sentences.zh: 每過瑾，言必稱千歲，自稱曰門下。

translations.literal: Whenever he visited Jin, his words always addressed him as "Your Thousand Years"; he called himself "your follower."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he visited Jin he addressed him as "Your Thousand Years" and called himself "your follower."

sentences.zh: 裁閱章奏，一阿瑾意。

translations.literal: In reviewing memorials, he wholly followed Jin's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: In reviewing memorials he did nothing but echo Jin's will.

sentences.zh: 四方賂瑾者先賂芳。

translations.literal: Those from all quarters who bribed Jin first bribed Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who wished to bribe Jin had to bribe Fang first.

sentences.zh: 子黃中，亦傲很不學，廷試必欲得第一。

translations.literal: His son Huangzhong was also arrogant and unlearned; in the palace examination he insisted on taking first place.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huangzhong was equally arrogant and ignorant and demanded first place in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 李東陽、王鏊為置二甲首，芳不悅。

translations.literal: Li Dongyang and Wang Ao placed him at the head of the second rank; Fang was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang and Wang Ao ranked him at the top of the second class; Fang was furious.

sentences.zh: 言於瑾，徑授翰林檢討，俄進編修。

translations.literal: He spoke to Jin, and Huangzhong was directly appointed Hanlin Proofreader, soon advanced to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He complained to Jin, who had Huangzhong made a Hanlin proofreader and soon promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 芳以黃中故，時時詈東陽。

translations.literal: Because of Huangzhong, Fang constantly cursed Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Huangzhong, Fang constantly reviled Li Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 瑾聞之曰：「黃中昨在我家試石榴詩，甚拙，顧恨李耶？」

translations.literal: Jin heard this and said: "Huangzhong yesterday at my house tried a poem on pomegranates—very clumsy—yet he blames Li?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin heard this and remarked, "Huangzhong tried a pomegranate poem at my house yesterday and it was dreadful—yet he blames Li Dongyang?"

sentences.zh: 瑾怒翰林官傲己，欲盡出之外，為張綵勸沮。

translations.literal: Jin was angry that Hanlin officials looked down on him and wished to expel them all to the outer offices; Zhang Cai dissuaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin resented the Hanlin scholars' arrogance toward him and wanted to banish them all to outer posts, but Zhang Cai talked him out of it.

sentences.zh: 及修《孝宗實錄》成，瑾又持前議，綵復力沮。

translations.literal: When the 《Veritable Records of Xiaozong》 were completed, Jin again raised the former proposal; Cai again strongly dissuaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the 《Veritable Records of Xiaozong》 were finished, Jin revived the idea, and Zhang Cai again blocked it.

sentences.zh: 而芳父子與檢討段炅輩，教瑾以擴充政事為名，乃盡出編修顧清等二十余人於部曹。

translations.literal: But Fang, father and son, with Proofreader Duan Jiong and others taught Jin that under the name of expanding administrative affairs, more than twenty compilers including Gu Qing were all sent out to ministry posts.
translations.idiomatic: But Fang, his son, proofreader Duan Jiong, and others persuaded Jin to purge the Hanlin under the pretext of expanding government business, and more than twenty compilers including Gu Qing were banished to ministry posts.

sentences.zh: 有司應詔舉懷材抱德之士，以余姚人周禮、徐子元、許龍，上虞人徐文彪四人名上。

translations.literal: The authorities, responding to an edict recommending men of talent and virtue, submitted the names of four men: Zhou Li, Xu Ziyuan, and Xu Long of Yuyao, and Xu Wenbiao of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: When officials were ordered to recommend men of talent and virtue, they nominated four men from Yuyao and Shangyu: Zhou Li, Xu Ziyuan, Xu Long, and Xu Wenbiao.

sentences.zh: 瑾以禮等皆遷鄉人，而詔草出健，因下四人詔獄，欲並逮健、遷。

translations.literal: Jin, because Zhou Li and the others were all Qian's countrymen and the edict draft had come from Jian, therefore sent the four to the imperial prison and wished to arrest Jian and Qian as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jin noted that all four were from Xie Qian's home region and that Liu Jian had drafted the edict, so he threw them into prison and tried to arrest Jian and Qian as well.

sentences.zh: 東陽力解之。

translations.literal: Dongyang strenuously secured their release.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang intervened forcefully on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 芳厲聲曰：「縱貰其罪，不當除名耶？」

translations.literal: Fang said in a harsh voice: "Even if their crime is pardoned, should they not be stripped of office?"
translations.idiomatic: Fang shouted, "Even if you spare their lives, should they not be stripped of office?"

sentences.zh: 乃黜健、遷為民，而榜逐余姚人之為京官者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jian and Qian were demoted to commoners, and a proclamation drove out Yuyao men serving as capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Qian were demoted to commoners, and an edict expelled all Yuyao men from capital posts.

sentences.zh: 滿剌加使臣亞劉，本江西萬安人，名蕭明舉。

translations.literal: The Malacca envoy Ya Liu was originally Xiao Mingju of Wan'an in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The Malacca envoy Ya Liu was originally Xiao Mingju, a native of Wan'an in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 以罪叛入其國，與其國人端亞智等來朝。

translations.literal: Having committed a crime, he defected to that country; with his countryman Duan Yazhi and others he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: After committing a crime he fled to Malacca and came to court with his countryman Duan Yazhi and others.

sentences.zh: 既又謀入浡泥國索寶，且殺亞智等。

translations.literal: Later he also plotted to enter the state of Brunei to seize treasure, and moreover to kill Yazhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He later plotted to enter Brunei in search of treasure and to murder Yazhi and his companions.

sentences.zh: 事聞，方下所司勘奏。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the relevant offices were just ordered to investigate and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, the responsible offices were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 芳即署其尾曰：「江西土俗，故多玩法，如彭華、尹直、徐瓊、李孜省、黃景等，多被物議。

translations.literal: Fang immediately appended to the end: "The customs of Jiangxi have always been prone to bending rules; such men as Peng Hua, Yin Zhi, Xu Qiong, Li Zisheng, and Huang Jing have often drawn public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Fang immediately added a note at the end: "Jiangxi custom has always been lawless; men such as Peng Hua, Yin Zhi, Xu Qiong, Li Zisheng, and Huang Jing have drawn much public criticism.

sentences.zh: 宜裁減解額五十名，通籍者勿選京職，著為令。」

translations.literal: The quota of successful candidates should be cut by fifty; those who gain office should not be selected for capital posts—let this be made a regulation."
translations.idiomatic: The provincial quota should be cut by fifty places, and Jiangxi graduates should be barred from capital posts—let this be made law.

sentences.zh: 且言：「王安石禍宋，吳澄仕元，宜榜其罪，使他日毋得濫用江西人。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Wang Anshi brought calamity to Song; Wu Cheng served Yuan—their crimes should be posted so that in future Jiangxi men may not be indiscriminately employed."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Wang Anshi ruined the Song; Wu Cheng served the Yuan—their crimes should be posted so that Jiangxi men are never again employed without scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 楊廷和解之曰：「以一盜故，禍連一方，至裁解額矣。

translations.literal: Yang Tinghe rebutted: "Because of one thief, to bring calamity on an entire region—even to cut the examination quota!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tinghe objected: "Because of one thief you would punish an entire province—even cut the examination quota!

sentences.zh: 宋、元人物，亦欲並案耶？」

translations.literal: Men of Song and Yuan—you wish to indict them together as well?"
translations.idiomatic: And you would drag in men of the Song and Yuan as well?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The proposal was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 芳深惡南人，每退一南人，輒喜。

translations.literal: Fang deeply hated southerners; whenever a southerner was demoted, he rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Fang loathed southerners; every time one was demoted he rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 雖論古人，亦必詆南而譽北，嘗作《南人不可為相圖》進瑾。

translations.literal: Even when discussing ancients, he always had to slander the South and praise the North; he once composed the 《Chart on Why Southerners Cannot Serve as Chancellor》 and presented it to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Even when he discussed the ancients, he invariably denigrated the South and praised the North; he once composed and presented to Liu Jin the 《Chart on Why Southerners Cannot Serve as Chancellor》.

sentences.zh: 其總裁《孝宗實錄》，若何喬新、彭韶、謝遷皆肆誣詆，自喜曰：「今朝廷之上，誰如我直者。」

translations.literal: As chief compiler of the 《Veritable Records of Xiaozong》, he recklessly slandered men such as He Qiaoxin, Peng Shao, and Xie Qian, and said to himself with satisfaction: "Who at court today is as upright as I?"
translations.idiomatic: As chief compiler of the 《Veritable Records of Xiaozong》, he freely slandered figures such as He Qiaoxin, Peng Shao, and Xie Qian, and said with satisfaction, "Who at court today is as upright as I?"

sentences.zh: 始張綵為郎時，芳力薦以悅瑾，覬其為奸利。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cai was first a bureau secretary, Fang strongly recommended him to please Jin, hoping he would help with illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cai was first a bureau secretary, Jiao Fang strongly recommended him to please Liu Jin, hoping he would help with corrupt gains.

sentences.zh: 比綵為尚書，芳父子薦人無虛日，綵時有同異，遂有隙。

translations.literal: By the time Zhang Cai became minister, Fang father and son recommended people without a single idle day; Zhang Cai sometimes disagreed, and a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Cai became minister, Jiao Fang and his son recommended people every day without fail; Zhang Cai sometimes disagreed, and a rift developed between them.

sentences.zh: 而段炅見瑾匿綵，芳勢稍衰，轉附綵，盡發芳陰事於瑾。

translations.literal: When Duan Jiong saw that Jin was keeping Zhang Cai in reserve and Fang's influence had slightly waned, he turned to attach himself to Zhang Cai and fully disclosed Fang's secret affairs to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Jiong saw that Liu Jin was holding Zhang Cai in reserve and Jiao Fang's influence had begun to wane, he switched allegiance to Zhang Cai and fully exposed Jiao Fang's hidden misdeeds to Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾大怒，數於眾中斥芳父子。

translations.literal: Jin was greatly angered and repeatedly rebuked Fang father and son before the assembled officials.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin was furious and repeatedly rebuked Jiao Fang and his son in public.

sentences.zh: 芳不得已，乃乞歸。

translations.literal: Fang had no choice and requested to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang had no choice but to request permission to retire.

sentences.zh: 黃中頠閣蔭，以侍讀隨父還。

translations.literal: Huang Zhong received hereditary privilege for the Hanlin Academy and returned with his father as a reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Huangzhong received hereditary privilege for appointment to the Hanlin Academy and returned home with his father as a reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，給事、御史交劾，削其官，黜黃中為民。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, supervising secretaries and censors jointly impeached him; his office was stripped, and Huang Zhong was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin fell, supervising secretaries and censors jointly impeached Jiao Fang; his office was stripped, and Jiao Huangzhong was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之，芳使黃中賫金寶遺權貴，上章求湔雪復官，為吏科所駁。

translations.literal: After some time, Fang had Huang Zhong carry gold and treasures as gifts to powerful nobles and submit a memorial seeking exoneration and restoration to office; it was rejected by the Office of Personnel Supervision.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, Jiao Fang had Jiao Huangzhong carry gold and treasures as gifts to powerful nobles and submit a memorial asking to be cleared of blame and restored to office; the Office of Personnel Supervision rejected it.

sentences.zh: 於是吏部覆奏，請械系黃中法司，以彰天討。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Personnel memorialized again, requesting that Huang Zhong be shackled and handed over to the judicial authorities to manifest Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Ministry of Personnel memorialized again, asking that Jiao Huangzhong be shackled and handed over to the judicial authorities so that Heaven's judgment might be made manifest.

sentences.zh: 黃中狼狽遁走。

translations.literal: Huang Zhong fled in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Huangzhong fled in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 芳居第宏麗，治作勞數郡。

translations.literal: Fang's residence was grand and splendid, and his construction projects exhausted several commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang's residence was grand and splendid, and the labor of his building projects exhausted several commanderies.

sentences.zh: 大盜趙鐩入泌陽，火之，發窖多得其藏金，乃盡掘其先人冢墓，雜燒以牛馬骨。

translations.literal: The great bandit Zhao Si entered Biyang, set fire to it, opened vaults and found much of his hoarded gold; he then completely dug up his ancestors' tombs and burned a mixture of them with cattle and horse bones.
translations.idiomatic: The great bandit Zhao Si entered Biyang and set it ablaze; opening vaults, he found much of Jiao Fang's hoarded gold, then completely dug up his ancestors' tombs and burned them mixed with cattle and horse bones.

sentences.zh: 求芳父子不得，取芳衣冠被庭樹，拔劍斫其首，使群盜糜之，曰：「吾為天子誅此賊。」

translations.literal: Unable to find Fang father and son, they took Fang's hat and robes and hung them on the courtyard trees, drew swords and hacked at the head, had the bandits pulverize it, and said: "I execute this villain on behalf of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find Jiao Fang and his son, they took Jiao Fang's hat and robes and hung them on the courtyard trees, drew swords and hacked at the head, had the bandits grind it to pieces, and said, "I am executing this villain on behalf of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鐩後臨刑嘆曰：「吾不能手刃焦芳父子以謝天下，死有餘恨！」

translations.literal: Later, at his execution, Si sighed and said: "I could not personally slay Jiao Fang father and son to answer to the world; even in death I still have regrets!"
translations.idiomatic: Later, as he faced execution, Zhao Si sighed and said, "I could not personally slay Jiao Fang and his son to answer to the world; even in death I still have regrets!"

sentences.zh: 瑾從孫二漢當死，亦曰：「吾死固當，第吾家所為，皆焦芳與張綵耳。

translations.literal: Jin's grand-nephew Er Han, facing death, also said: "My death is certainly deserved, but what my family did was all the work of Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin's grand-nephew Er Han, facing death, also said, "My death is certainly deserved, but everything my family did was the work of Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai alone.

sentences.zh: 今綵與我處極刑，而芳獨晏然，豈非冤哉。」

translations.literal: Now Zhang Cai and I suffer the extreme penalty, yet Fang alone remains at ease—is this not unjust?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang Cai and I suffer the death penalty, yet Jiao Fang alone remains at ease—is this not unjust?"

sentences.zh: 芳父子竟良死。

translations.literal: Fang father and son in the end died a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang and his son in the end died natural deaths.

sentences.zh: 劉宇，字至大，鈞州人。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, courtesy name Zhi da, was a native of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, courtesy name Zhida, was a native of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 成化八年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi graduate in the eighth year of the Chenghua reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 由知縣入為御史，坐事謫，累遷山東按察使。

translations.literal: From magistrate he entered service as a censor; demoted for an offense, he was steadily promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a censor after serving as a magistrate; demoted for an offense, he was steadily promoted until he became surveillance commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，以大學士劉健薦，擢右僉都御史，巡撫大同，召為左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign, on the recommendation of Grand Secretary Liu Jian, he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Datong, then summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, on the recommendation of Grand Secretary Liu Jian, he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Datong, then summoned to serve as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，吏部尚書馬文升薦之，進右都御史，總督宣府、大同、山西軍務。

translations.literal: When the Zhengde era began, Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng recommended him; he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and made supreme commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde era began, Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng recommended him; he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and appointed supreme commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 宇初撫大同，私市善馬賂權要。

translations.literal: When Yu first served as grand coordinator of Datong, he privately bought fine horses to bribe powerful figures.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu first served as grand coordinator of Datong, he privately purchased fine horses to bribe powerful figures.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書劉大夏因孝宗召見，語及之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liu Daxia, when summoned by Emperor Xiaozong, spoke of this matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Liu Daxia was summoned by Emperor Xiaozong, he spoke of the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝密遣錦衣百戶邵琪往察，宇厚賂琪，為之抵諱。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly sent Jin Yi hundred-household officer Shao Qi to investigate; Yu heavily bribed Qi, who covered for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent Jin Yi hundred-household officer Shao Qi to investigate; Liu Yu heavily bribed Shao Qi, who covered for him.

sentences.zh: 後大夏再召對，帝曰：「健薦宇才堪大用，以朕觀之，此小人，豈可用哉？

translations.literal: Later, when Daxia was summoned again for an audience, the emperor said: "Jian recommended Yu as talent fit for great use, but in my view this man is a petty villain—how can he be used?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Liu Daxia was summoned again for an audience, the emperor said, "Liu Jian recommended Liu Yu as a man of talent fit for great use, but in my view he is a petty villain—how can he be used?

sentences.zh: 由是知內閣亦未可盡信也。」

translations.literal: From this one knew that the inner cabinet also could not be fully trusted.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knew that the inner cabinet also could not be fully trusted.

sentences.zh: 宇聞，以大夏不為己地，深憾之。

translations.literal: When Yu heard of this, he deeply resented Daxia for not speaking on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu heard of this, he deeply resented Liu Daxia for not speaking on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾用事，宇介焦芳以結瑾。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin held power, Yu used Jiao Fang as an intermediary to attach himself to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin held power, Liu Yu used Jiao Fang as an intermediary to attach himself to Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 二年正月入為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he entered office as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of the Zhengde reign, he entered office as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 瑾好摧折臺諫，宇緣其意，請敕箝制御史，有小過輒加笞辱，瑾以為賢。

translations.literal: Jin liked to break censorate remonstrators; Yu followed his intent, requested an edict to restrain censors, and for minor faults would add beating and humiliation; Jin considered him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin liked to break the censorate remonstrators; Liu Yu followed his intent, requested an edict to restrain the censors, and for minor faults would add beatings and humiliation; Liu Jin considered him worthy.

sentences.zh: 瑾初通賄，望不過數百金，宇首以萬金贄，瑾大喜曰：「劉先生何厚我。」

translations.literal: When Jin first accepted bribes, he hoped for no more than a few hundred taels of gold; Yu was the first to present ten thousand taels as a gift; Jin rejoiced greatly and said: "How generous of you, Mr. Liu!
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin first began accepting bribes, he expected no more than a few hundred taels of gold; Liu Yu was the first to present ten thousand taels as a gift; Liu Jin rejoiced greatly and said, "How generous of you, Mr. Liu!

sentences.zh: 尋轉兵部尚書，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Minister of War and given the additional title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Minister of War and given the additional title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子仁應殿試，求一甲不得。

translations.literal: His son Ren participated in the palace examination but could not attain first rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Ren took the palace examination but failed to attain first rank.

sentences.zh: 厚賄瑾，內批授庶吉士，逾年遷編修。

translations.literal: He heavily bribed Jin; by inner edict Ren was made a Hanlin bachelor, and the next year he was promoted to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He heavily bribed Liu Jin; by inner edict Liu Ren was appointed a Hanlin bachelor, and the following year he was promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 時許進為吏部尚書，宇讒於瑾，遂代其位，而曹元代宇為兵部。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Jin was Minister of Personnel; Yu slandered him to Jin and took his post, while Cao Yuan replaced Yu at the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Jin was Minister of Personnel; Liu Yu slandered him to Liu Jin and took his post, while Cao Yuan replaced Liu Yu at the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 宇在兵部時，賄賂狼籍。

translations.literal: While Yu was at the Ministry of War, bribes were everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Yu was at the Ministry of War, bribes were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 及為吏部，權歸選郎張綵，而文史贈遺又不若武弁，嘗悒悒嘆曰：「兵部自佳，何必吏部也。」

translations.literal: When he became Minister of Personnel, power passed to selection secretary Zhang Cai, and the gifts from civil officials were inferior to those from military officers; he once sighed in frustration and said: "The Ministry of War was fine enough—why the Ministry of Personnel?
translations.idiomatic: When he became Minister of Personnel, power passed to selection secretary Zhang Cai, and the gifts from civil officials were not as good as those from military officers; he once sighed in frustration and said, "The Ministry of War was fine enough—why bother with the Ministry of Personnel?

sentences.zh: 後瑾欲用綵代宇，乃令宇以原官兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: Later Jin wanted to use Zhang Cai to replace Yu, so he had Yu retain his original post while also serving as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Jin wanted to use Zhang Cai to replace Liu Yu, so he had Liu Yu retain his original post while also serving as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 宇宴瑾閣中，極歡，大喜過望。

translations.literal: Yu feasted Jin in the pavilion with supreme joy, exceeding all expectation in delight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu feasted Liu Jin in the pavilion with great joy, his delight exceeding all expectation.

sentences.zh: 明日將入閣辦事。

translations.literal: The next day he was about to enter the pavilion to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was about to enter the pavilion to handle affairs.

sentences.zh: 瑾曰：「爾真欲相耶？

translations.literal: Jin said: "Do you truly want to be chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin said, "Do you truly want to be chancellor?

sentences.zh: 此地豈可再入。」

translations.literal: This place cannot be entered again.
translations.idiomatic: This place cannot be entered again.

sentences.zh: 宇不得已，乃乞省墓去。

translations.literal: Yu had no choice and requested leave to visit his ancestral graves.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had no choice but to request leave to visit his ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 逾年瑾誅，科道交章劾奏，削官致仕，子仁黜為民。

translations.literal: A year later Jin was executed; censorate officials submitted joint impeachments; Yu's office was stripped and he retired, and son Ren was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Liu Jin was executed; censorate officials submitted joint impeachments; Liu Yu's office was stripped and he retired, and Liu Ren was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 曹元，字以貞，大寧前衛人。

translations.literal: Cao Yuan, courtesy name Yizhen, was a native of Daining Forward Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuan, courtesy name Yizhen, was a native of Daining Forward Guard.

sentences.zh: 柔佞滑稽，不修士行。

translations.literal: He was soft, sycophantic, and witty, and did not maintain proper conduct as a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He was soft, sycophantic, and witty, and did not maintain proper conduct as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 舉成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Chenghua reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 授工部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 正德二年累遷右副都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Zhengde reign he was steadily promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhengde reign he was steadily promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 分守中官張昭奉命捕虎豹，元以軍士出境搜捕，恐啟邊釁，上疏請止，不從。

translations.literal: The regional defending eunuch Zhang Zhao was ordered to capture tigers and leopards; Yuan, because troops crossed the border to search and hunt, feared provoking a border incident and memorialized to stop it, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The regional defending eunuch Zhang Zhao was ordered to capture tigers and leopards; Cao Yuan, fearing that sending troops across the border to search and hunt would provoke a border incident, memorialized asking that the order be stopped, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 改撫陜西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召為兵部右侍郎，轉左，尋代宇為尚書兼督團營，加太子少保。

translations.literal: A year later he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War, transferred to the left vice ministership, and soon replaced Yu as minister while also supervising the Tuan battalions; he was given the additional title Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War, transferred to the left vice ministership, and soon replaced Liu Yu as minister while also supervising the Tuan battalions; he was given the additional title Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 將校遷除，皆惟瑾命。

translations.literal: Promotions and transfers of officers all followed Jin's command alone.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions and transfers of officers all followed Liu Jin's command alone.

sentences.zh: 元所入亦不貲。

translations.literal: Yuan's income likewise was not insignificant.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuan's income was likewise enormous.

sentences.zh: 五年拜吏部尚書兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 元與劉瑾有連，自瑾侍東宮，即與相結。

translations.literal: Yuan had connections with Liu Jin; from the time Jin served the Eastern Palace they were allied.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuan had connections with Liu Jin; from the time Liu Jin served the Eastern Palace they were allied.

sentences.zh: 及瑾得誌，遂夤緣躐至卿相，然瑣刺無能，在閣中飲酒諧謔而已。

translations.literal: When Jin got his wish, Yuan climbed by connections straight to minister and chancellor rank, yet he was petty and incapable—in the pavilion he merely drank wine and bantered.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin got his wish, Cao Yuan climbed by connections straight to minister and chancellor rank, yet he was petty and incapable—in the Grand Secretariat he merely drank wine and bantered.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，元即日上疏請罪，詞極哀。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, Yuan that same day memorialized pleading guilty, in words extremely pathetic.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin fell, Cao Yuan that same day memorialized pleading guilty in words of extreme pathos.

sentences.zh: 詔許致仕，言官交劾，黜為民。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to retire; remonstrating officials jointly impeached him, and he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted him to retire, but remonstrating officials jointly impeached him, and he was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 元無子，病中自作墓誌，嘆曰：「我死，誰銘我者！」

translations.literal: Yuan had no son; while ill he wrote his own tomb inscription and sighed: "When I die, who will inscribe my epitaph!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuan had no son; while ill he wrote his own tomb inscription and sighed, "When I die, who will inscribe my epitaph!"

sentences.zh: 當劉瑾時，廷臣黨附者甚眾。

translations.literal: During Liu Jin's time, many court ministers factionally attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Jin's time, a great many court ministers factionally attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，言官交劾。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, remonstrating officials jointly impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin was executed, remonstrating officials jointly impeached them.

sentences.zh: 內閣則焦芳、劉宇、曹元。

translations.literal: In the Grand Secretariat there were Jiao Fang, Liu Yu, and Cao Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Secretariat there were Jiao Fang, Liu Yu, and Cao Yuan.

sentences.zh: 尚書則吏部張綵、戶部劉璣、兵部王敞、刑部劉璟、工部畢亨、南京戶部張澯、禮部朱恩、刑部劉纓、工部李善。

translations.literal: Among ministers there were Zhang Cai in Personnel, Liu Ji in Revenue, Wang Chang in War, Liu Jing in Justice, Bi Heng in Works, Zhang Can in Nanjing Revenue, Zhu En in Rites, Liu Ying in Justice, and Li Shan in Works.
translations.idiomatic: Among ministers there were Zhang Cai in the Ministry of Personnel, Liu Ji in the Ministry of Revenue, Wang Chang in the Ministry of War, Liu Jing in the Ministry of Justice, Bi Heng in the Ministry of Works, Zhang Can in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, Zhu En in the Ministry of Rites, Liu Ying in the Ministry of Justice, and Li Shan in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 侍郎則吏部柴升、李瀚，前戶部韓福，禮部李遜學，兵部陸完、陳震，刑部張子麟，工部崔巖、夏昂、胡諒，南京禮部常麟、工部張誌淳。

translations.literal: Among vice ministers there were Chai Sheng and Li Han in Personnel, former Revenue official Han Fu, Li Xunxue in Rites, Lu Wan and Chen Zhen in War, Zhang Zilin in Justice, Cui Yan, Xia Ang, and Hu Liang in Works, Chang Lin in Nanjing Rites, and Zhang Zhichun in Nanjing Works.
translations.idiomatic: Among vice ministers there were Chai Sheng and Li Han in the Ministry of Personnel, former Revenue official Han Fu, Li Xunxue in the Ministry of Rites, Lu Wan and Chen Zhen in the Ministry of War, Zhang Zilin in the Ministry of Justice, Cui Yan, Xia Ang, and Hu Liang in the Ministry of Works, Chang Lin in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, and Zhang Zhichun in the Nanjing Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 都察院則副都御史楊綸、僉都御史蕭選。

translations.literal: In the Censorate there were Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Lun and Assistant Censor-in-Chief Xiao Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Censorate there were Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Lun and Assistant Censor-in-Chief Xiao Xuan.

sentences.zh: 巡撫則順天劉聰、應天魏訥、宣府楊武、保定徐以貞、大同張禴、淮揚屈直、兩廣林廷選，操江王彥奇。

translations.literal: Among grand coordinators there were Liu Cong in Shuntian, Wei Ne in Yingtian, Yang Wu in Xuanfu, Xu Yizhen in Baoding, Zhang Fu in Datong, Qu Zhi in Huai-Yang, Lin Tingxuan in the Two Guangs, and Wang Yanqi commanding the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Among grand coordinators there were Liu Cong in Shuntian, Wei Ne in Yingtian, Yang Wu in Xuanfu, Xu Yizhen in Baoding, Zhang Fu in Datong, Qu Zhi in Huai-Yang, Lin Tingxuan in the Two Guangs, and Wang Yanqi commanding the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 前總督文貴、馬炳然。

translations.literal: Among former supreme commanders there were Wen Gui and Ma Bingran.
translations.idiomatic: Among former supreme commanders there were Wen Gui and Ma Bingran.

sentences.zh: 大理寺則卿張綸，少卿董恬，丞蔡中孚、張檜。

translations.literal: In the Court of Judicial Review there were Chief Zhang Lun, Vice Minister Dong Tian, and Assistant Ministers Cai Zhongfu and Zhang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Court of Judicial Review there were Chief Minister Zhang Lun, Vice Minister Dong Tian, and Assistant Ministers Cai Zhongfu and Zhang Hui.

sentences.zh: 通政司則通政吳釴、王雲鳳，參議張龍。

translations.literal: In the Directorate of Transmission there were Transmission Commissioners Wu Yi and Wang Yunfeng, and Assistant Commissioner Zhang Long.
translations.idiomatic: In the Directorate of Transmission there were Transmission Commissioners Wu Yi and Wang Yunfeng, and Assistant Commissioner Zhang Long.

sentences.zh: 太常則少卿楊廷儀、劉介。

translations.literal: In the Court of Imperial Sacrifices there were Vice Ministers Yang Tingyi and Liu Jie.
translations.idiomatic: In the Court of Imperial Sacrifices there were Vice Ministers Yang Tingyi and Liu Jie.

sentences.zh: 尚寶卿則吳世忠，丞屈銓。

translations.literal: In the Court of Imperial Seals there were Chief Wu Shizhong and Assistant Qu Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Court of Imperial Seals there were Chief Minister Wu Shizhong and Assistant Minister Qu Quan.

sentences.zh: 府尹則陳良器，府丞則石祿。

translations.literal: The prefectural intendant was Chen Liangqi, and the vice intendant was Shi Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural intendant was Chen Liangqi, and the vice intendant was Shi Lu.

sentences.zh: 翰林則侍讀焦黃中，修撰康海，編修劉仁，檢討段炅。

translations.literal: In the Hanlin Academy there were reader-in-waiting Jiao Huangzhong, compiler Kang Hai, reviser Liu Ren, and proofreader Duan Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hanlin Academy there were reader-in-waiting Jiao Huangzhong, compiler Kang Hai, reviser Liu Ren, and proofreader Duan Jiong.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎則王九思、王納誨。

translations.literal: Among bureau secretaries in the Ministry of Personnel there were Wang Jiusi and Wang Nahui.
translations.idiomatic: Among bureau secretaries in the Ministry of Personnel there were Wang Jiusi and Wang Nahui.

sentences.zh: 給事中則李憲、段豸。

translations.literal: Among supervising secretaries there were Li Xian and Duan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Among supervising secretaries there were Li Xian and Duan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 御史則薛鳳鳴、朱袞、秦昂、宇文鐘、崔哲、李紀、周琳。

translations.literal: Among censors there were Xue Fengming, Zhu Gun, Qin Ang, Yuwen Zhong, Cui Zhe, Li Ji, and Zhou Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Among censors there were Xue Fengming, Zhu Gun, Qin Ang, Yuwen Zhong, Cui Zhe, Li Ji, and Zhou Lin.

sentences.zh: 其他郎署監司又十餘人。

translations.literal: Other bureau secretaries and supervising commissioners numbered more than ten besides.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten other bureau secretaries and supervising commissioners were involved as well.

sentences.zh: 於是綵論死，福謫戍，元、恩、震、聰、訥、武、恬、介、黃中、海、仁、憲、鳳鳴、鐘除名，亨、昂閑住，善、巖、諒、志淳、綸、直、彥奇、良器、哲致仕，選、以貞、禴、中孚、龍、祿、銓、炅、豸、袞、紀、琳、九思，納誨謫外，朝署為清。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Cai was sentenced to death, Han Fu was banished to border garrison service, Cao Yuan, Zhu En, Chen Zhen, Liu Cong, Wei Ne, Yang Wu, Dong Tian, Liu Jie, Jiao Huangzhong, Kang Hai, Liu Ren, Li Xian, Xue Fengming, and Yuwen Zhong were struck from the rolls, Bi Heng and Xia Ang were suspended, Li Shan, Cui Yan, Hu Liang, Zhang Zhichun, Yang Lun, Qu Zhi, Wang Yanqi, Chen Liangqi, and Cui Zhe retired, and Xiao Xuan, Xu Yizhen, Zhang Fu, Cai Zhongfu, Zhang Long, Shi Lu, Qu Quan, Duan Jiong, Duan Zhi, Zhu Gun, Li Ji, Zhou Lin, Wang Jiusi, and Wang Nahui were demoted outside the capital—court offices were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhang Cai was sentenced to death and Han Fu was banished to border garrison service; Cao Yuan, Zhu En, Chen Zhen, Liu Cong, Wei Ne, Yang Wu, Dong Tian, Liu Jie, Jiao Huangzhong, Kang Hai, Liu Ren, Li Xian, Xue Fengming, and Yuwen Zhong were struck from the rolls; Bi Heng and Xia Ang were suspended from duty; Li Shan, Cui Yan, Hu Liang, Zhang Zhichun, Yang Lun, Qu Zhi, Wang Yanqi, Chen Liangqi, and Cui Zhe retired; and Xiao Xuan, Xu Yizhen, Zhang Fu, Cai Zhongfu, Zhang Long, Shi Lu, Qu Quan, Duan Jiong, Duan Zhi, Zhu Gun, Li Ji, Zhou Lin, Wang Jiusi, and Wang Nahui were demoted outside the capital—until the court offices were cleared.

sentences.zh: 張綵，安定人。

translations.literal: Zhang Cai was a native of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai was a native of Anding.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi graduate in the third year of the Hongzhi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 授吏部主事，歷文選司郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and served as bureau director in the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and served as bureau director in the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 綵議論便利，善伺權貴指。

translations.literal: Zhang Cai was sharp in discourse and good at reading the wishes of powerful men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai was sharp in discourse and good at reading the wishes of powerful men.

sentences.zh: 初矯飾徹聲譽，尚書馬文升等皆愛之。

translations.literal: At first he put on airs to build his reputation, and Minister Ma Wensheng and others all admired him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he cultivated an air of rectitude to build his reputation, and Minister Ma Wensheng and others all admired him.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉郤嘗劾其顛倒選法數事，文升悉為辯析，且譽其聰明剛正，為上下所推服。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Liu Xi once impeached him for several matters of perverting selection law; Wensheng fully argued in his defense and praised his intelligence and integrity, earning esteem above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Liu Xi once impeached him on several counts of perverting selection law; Ma Wensheng fully argued in his defense and praised his intelligence and integrity, winning esteem above and below.

sentences.zh: 詔令辦事如故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to carry on as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to carry on as before.

sentences.zh: 綵即五疏移疾去，文升固留不得，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Zhang Cai immediately submitted five memorials citing illness to leave; Wensheng firmly tried to retain him but could not, and contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai immediately submitted five memorials citing illness and asking to leave; Ma Wensheng firmly tried to retain him but could not, and contemporary opinion praised Zhang Cai for this.

sentences.zh: 越數日，給事中李貫薦綵有將略。

translations.literal: After several days, supervising secretary Li Guan recommended that Zhang Cai had military talent.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, supervising secretary Li Guan recommended Zhang Cai as a man of military talent.

sentences.zh: 楊一清總制三邊，亦薦綵自代。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing, supreme commander of the Three Frontiers, also recommended Zhang Cai to succeed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing, supreme commander of the Three Frontiers, also recommended Zhang Cai to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 而焦芳以綵與劉瑾同鄉，力薦於瑾。

translations.literal: But Jiao Fang, because Zhang Cai was a fellow townsman of Liu Jin, strongly recommended him to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: But Jiao Fang, because Zhang Cai was a fellow townsman of Liu Jin, strongly recommended him to Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾欲致之，因著令，病過期不赴者，斥為民。

translations.literal: Jin wanted to bring him in, and therefore issued a regulation that those who failed to report after illness leave expired would be dismissed as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin wanted to bring him in and therefore issued a regulation that anyone who failed to report after illness leave expired would be dismissed as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 綵乃就道。

translations.literal: Zhang Cai then set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai then set out on the road.

sentences.zh: 既見瑾，高冠鮮衣，貌白晳修偉，鬚眉蔚然，詞辯泉湧。

translations.literal: Once he met Jin, he wore a high cap and fresh clothes; his appearance was fair, tall, and imposing, his beard and brows luxuriant, and his eloquence poured forth like a spring.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met Liu Jin, he wore a high cap and fresh clothes; he was fair-skinned, tall, and imposing, with luxuriant beard and brows, and his eloquence poured forth like a spring.

sentences.zh: 瑾大敬愛，執手移時，曰：「子神人也，我何以得遇子！」

translations.literal: Jin greatly admired him, held his hand for a long time, and said: "You are a divine man—how did I merit meeting you!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin greatly admired him, held his hand for a long time, and said, "You are a divine man—how did I ever merit meeting you!

sentences.zh: 時文選郎劉永已遷通政，次當驗封郎石確。

translations.literal: At the time selection secretary Liu Yong had already transferred to the Directorate of Transmission; next in line was verification-and-seal secretary Shi Que.
translations.idiomatic: At the time selection secretary Liu Yong had already transferred to the Directorate of Transmission; next in line for promotion was verification-and-seal secretary Shi Que.

sentences.zh: 疏既入，瑾令尚書許進追原疏，以綵易之。

translations.literal: Once the memorial was submitted, Jin had Minister Xu Jin recall the original memorial and substitute Zhang Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial was submitted, Liu Jin had Minister Xu Jin recall the original memorial and substitute Zhang Cai in his place.

sentences.zh: 綵自是一意事瑾。

translations.literal: From then on Zhang Cai devoted himself entirely to serving Jin.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Zhang Cai devoted himself entirely to serving Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾惡進不附己，綵因媒孽去進，以劉宇代之。

translations.literal: Jin hated Xu Jin for not siding with him; Cai, by fabricating accusations, removed Xu Jin and replaced him with Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin resented Xu Jin for refusing to align with him; Zhang Cai, by sowing slander, had Xu Jin removed and Liu Yu put in his place.

sentences.zh: 宇雖為尚書，銓政率由綵，多不關白宇，即白宇，宇必溫言降接。

translations.literal: Though Yu was Minister, appointment policy was largely run by Cai; many matters were not reported to Yu at all, and even when they were reported, Yu always received him with gentle, deferential words.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Yu held the title of Minister, the power of appointment remained largely in Zhang Cai's hands; many matters never reached Liu Yu at all, and even when they did, Liu Yu always greeted him with warm, yielding courtesy.

sentences.zh: 綵抱案立語，宇俯僂不敢當。

translations.literal: Cai would hold documents and speak while standing; Yu would bow low and dare not presume to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai would stand clutching his papers as he spoke; Liu Yu would bow low before him and dare not hold himself as an equal.

sentences.zh: 居文選半載，擢左僉都御史，與戶部右侍郎韓鼎同廷謝。

translations.literal: After half a year in the Bureau of Appointments, he was promoted to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and, together with Han Ding, Vice Minister of Revenue, attended court to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year as Director of the Bureau of Appointments, he was promoted to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and, together with Han Ding, Vice Minister of Revenue, went before the throne to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 鼎老，拜起不如儀，為谷大用、張永輩所竊笑。

translations.literal: Ding was old; his bowing and rising did not conform to protocol, and he was secretly mocked by Gu Dayong, Zhang Yong, and their ilk.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ding was elderly; his bows and risings fell short of proper form, and Gu Dayong, Zhang Yong, and the rest secretly laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 瑾方慚，而綵丰采英毅，大用等皆稱羨，瑾乃喜。

translations.literal: Jin was thus shamed, but Cai's bearing was heroic and resolute; Dayong and the others all praised him with envy, and Jin was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin was mortified, but Zhang Cai's presence was bold and commanding; Gu Dayong and the others spoke of him with open envy, and Liu Jin's mood turned bright.

sentences.zh: 越二日罷鼎，而綵逾年超拜吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Two days later Ding was dismissed, and within a year Cai was promoted over the usual course to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Han Ding was dismissed, and within a year Zhang Cai was promoted out of turn to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 鼎，合水人。

translations.literal: Ding was a native of Heshui.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ding was a native of Heshui.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，為給事中，負直聲。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign he served as a supervising secretary and bore a reputation for upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongzhi era he had served as a supervising secretary and enjoyed a reputation for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 後遷右通政，治水安平有勞績，以通政使家居。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission; for meritorious service in managing waterways at Anping he was allowed to retire at home as Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission; for distinguished work in controlling the waters at Anping he retired home with the rank of Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 至是為瑾所引，復挫歸，遂失其素望。

translations.literal: Now, having been brought forward by Jin, he suffered setback upon return and thus lost the esteem he had long enjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Now, having been advanced by Liu Jin, he met with humiliation on his return and lost the standing he had long commanded.

sentences.zh: 瑾欲大貴綵，乃命劉宇入內閣，以綵代之。

translations.literal: Jin wished to greatly exalt Cai, so he ordered Liu Yu into the Grand Secretariat and had Cai replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin wished to raise Zhang Cai to great eminence, so he ordered Liu Yu into the Grand Secretariat and had Zhang Cai take his place.

sentences.zh: 一歲中，自郎署長六卿。

translations.literal: Within a single year he had risen from a bureau secretary to one of the Six Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year he had risen from a bureau secretary to one of the Six Ministers.

sentences.zh: 僚友守官如故，咸惴惴白事尚書前，綵厲色無所假借。

translations.literal: His colleagues continued in their posts as before; all trembled as they reported affairs before the Minister, and Cai would glower and grant no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues kept their posts as before, yet all approached the Minister's desk in fear; Zhang Cai would darken his face and show no leniency.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was additionally appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 每瑾出休沐，公卿往候，自辰至哺未得見。

translations.literal: Whenever Jin went out on his days of rest, the high officials would call on him; from dawn until the afternoon meal they could not obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liu Jin left the palace on his days of rest, the high officials would come to wait on him; from morning until the afternoon meal they could not gain an audience.

sentences.zh: 綵故徐徐來，直入瑾小閣，歡飲而出，始揖眾人。

translations.literal: Cai would deliberately arrive late, go straight into Jin's private pavilion, drink merrily, and only then emerge to bow to the assembled company.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai would deliberately arrive late, enter Liu Jin's private pavilion directly, drink merrily with him, and only then come out to bow to the waiting crowd.

sentences.zh: 眾以是益畏綵，見綵如瑾禮。

translations.literal: The others therefore feared Cai all the more and treated Cai with the same deference they showed Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The others therefore feared Zhang Cai all the more and accorded him the same deference they showed Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 綵與朝臣言，呼瑾為老者。

translations.literal: When Cai spoke with court officials, he addressed Jin as 'the old gentleman.'
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cai spoke with court officials, he called Liu Jin 'the old gentleman.'

sentences.zh: 凡所言，瑾無不從。

translations.literal: Whatever he said, Jin never failed to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he proposed, Liu Jin never refused.

sentences.zh: 因不時考察內外官，糾摘嚴急，間一用薄罰，而諸司臺諫謫辱日甚。

translations.literal: Consequently he conducted irregular inspections of officials within and without the capital, prosecuting and exposing them with severe urgency; occasionally he applied minor punishments, yet day by day the various bureaus, censorial offices, and remonstrating officials suffered demotion and humiliation all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He then began irregular inspections of officials within and outside the capital, prosecuting them with harsh urgency; though he sometimes imposed only light penalties, demotion and disgrace among the bureaus, censorial offices, and remonstrating officials grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 變亂舊格，賄賂肆行，海內金帛奇貨相望塗巷間。

translations.literal: He overturned established norms; bribery ran rampant, and across the realm gold, silk, and rare goods lined the roads and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: He overturned long-standing rules; bribery ran unchecked, and across the realm gold, silk, and rare goods crowded the roads and lanes.

sentences.zh: 性尤漁色。

translations.literal: He was especially given to seizing women for his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He was above all a predator of women.

sentences.zh: 撫州知府劉介，其鄉人也，娶妾美。

translations.literal: Liu Jie, prefect of Fuzhou, was a fellow townsman of his and had taken a beautiful concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie, prefect of Fuzhou, was his fellow townsman and had taken a beautiful concubine.

sentences.zh: 綵特擢介太常少卿，盛服往賀曰：「子何以報我？」

translations.literal: Cai specially promoted Jie to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, went in full ceremonial dress to congratulate him, and said: 'How will you repay me?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai specially promoted Liu Jie to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, went in full ceremonial dress to congratulate him, and asked, "How will you repay me?

sentences.zh: 介皇恐謝曰：「一身外，皆公物。」

translations.literal: Jie, in terror, apologized and said: 'Apart from my own person, all else is yours, my lord.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie, terrified, apologized and said, "Apart from my own body, everything I have is yours, my lord."

sentences.zh: 綵曰：「命之矣。」

translations.literal: Cai said: 'It is decided.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai said, "Then it is settled."

sentences.zh: 即使人直入內，牽其妾，輿載而去。

translations.literal: He then sent men straight into the inner quarters, seized the concubine, and carried her off in a sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent men straight into the inner quarters, seized the concubine, and carried her off in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 又聞平陽知府張恕妾美，索之不肯，令御史張禴按致其罪，擬戍。

translations.literal: He also heard that Zhang Shu, prefect of Pingyang, had a beautiful concubine; he demanded her but Shu refused, so he ordered Censor Zhang Fu to investigate and bring charges against him, recommending banishment to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard that Zhang Shu, prefect of Pingyang, had a beautiful concubine; when he demanded her and Shu refused, he ordered Censor Zhang Fu to investigate and bring charges against him, recommending banishment to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 恕獻妾，始得論減。

translations.literal: Shu presented the concubine, and only then was the sentence reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu surrendered the concubine, and only then was his sentence reduced.

sentences.zh: 綵既銜瑾恩，見瑾擅權久，貪冒無厭，天下怨之，因乘間說曰：「公亦知賄入所自乎？

translations.literal: Cai, having long owed Jin a debt of gratitude, saw that Jin had monopolized power for a long time and was insatiably greedy and corrupt, and that all under Heaven resented him; seizing an opportune moment he advised: 'Do you also know whence the bribes enter?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai, deeply indebted to Liu Jin, saw that Liu Jin had held power for years with insatiable greed and that the realm resented him; seizing a favorable moment he said, "Do you know where the bribes you receive really come from?

sentences.zh: 非盜官帑，即剝小民。

translations.literal: They are either stolen from the public treasury or wrung from the common people.
translations.idiomatic: They are either stolen from the public coffers or wrung from the common people.

sentences.zh: 彼借公名自厚，入公者未十一，而怨悉歸公，何以謝天下？」

translations.literal: They use your name to enrich themselves; of what comes to you, not one part in ten—yet all the resentment falls upon you. How can you answer to all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: They borrow your name to enrich themselves; of what reaches you, not one part in ten—and yet all the hatred settles on you. How can you answer to the realm?

sentences.zh: 瑾大然之。

translations.literal: Jin greatly agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 會御史胡節巡按山東還，厚遺瑾。

translations.literal: It happened that Censor Hu Jie, returning from an inspection tour of Shandong, presented Jin with lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Censor Hu Jie, returning from an inspection tour of Shandong, presented Liu Jin with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 瑾發之，捕節下獄。

translations.literal: Jin opened them and had Jie arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin opened the gifts and had Hu Jie arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 少監李宣、侍郎張鸞、指揮同知趙良按事福建還，饋瑾白金二萬。

translations.literal: Junior Director Li Xuan, Vice Minister Zhang Luan, and Assistant Commander Zhao Liang, returning from investigating affairs in Fujian, presented Jin with twenty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Director Li Xuan, Vice Minister Zhang Luan, and Assistant Commander Zhao Liang, returning from investigating affairs in Fujian, presented Liu Jin with twenty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 瑾疏納金於官，而按三人罪。

translations.literal: Jin memorialized surrendering the silver to the state and prosecuted the three men for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin memorialized surrendering the silver to the state and prosecuted the three men for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 其他因賄得禍者甚眾。

translations.literal: Many others likewise met disaster because of bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Many others likewise met ruin through bribery.

sentences.zh: 苛斂之害為少衰，中外或稱綵能導瑾為善矣。

translations.literal: The harm of harsh levies diminished somewhat, and within and without the court some praised Cai for being able to guide Jin toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The scourge of harsh exactions eased somewhat, and within and outside the court some praised Zhang Cai for steering Liu Jin toward better conduct.

sentences.zh: 及瑾伏誅，綵以交結近侍論死，遇赦當免。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Cai was sentenced to death on the charge of associating with close attendants, but when an amnesty was granted he should have been exempt.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin was executed, Zhang Cai was sentenced to death for associating with close attendants, a charge that should have been remitted when an amnesty was granted.

sentences.zh: 改擬同瑾謀反，瘐死獄中，仍剉屍於市，籍其家，妻子流海南。

translations.literal: The charge was changed to conspiracy with Jin to rebel; he died of illness in prison, yet his corpse was still dismembered in the marketplace, his household was confiscated, and his wife and children were exiled to Hainan.
translations.idiomatic: The charge was changed to conspiracy with Liu Jin to rebel; he died of illness in prison, yet his corpse was still dismembered in the marketplace, his household was confiscated, and his wife and children were exiled to Hainan.

sentences.zh: 韓福者，西安前衛人也。

translations.literal: Han Fu was a native of Xi'an Front Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu was a native of Xi'an Front Guard.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 為御史，按宣府、大同，數條奏軍民利病，邊人悅之。

translations.literal: As a censor he inspected Xuanfu and Datong, repeatedly memorializing on matters of benefit and harm to soldiers and civilians; the border people were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: As a censor he inspected Xuanfu and Datong, repeatedly memorializing on the hardships and needs of soldiers and civilians, and the border people were pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，遷大名知府，奸盜屏跡，道不拾遺，政績為畿輔冠。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period he was transferred to prefect of Daming; scoundrels and robbers vanished, and lost articles were not picked up off the roads—his administrative achievements ranked first in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongzhi era he was transferred to prefect of Daming; scoundrels and robbers vanished, and no one picked up lost goods left on the road—his record ranked first among the prefectures of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 以卓異舉，遷浙江左參政，病免。

translations.literal: Recommended for outstanding merit, he was transferred to Left Assistant Administrator of Zhejiang, then retired due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for outstanding merit, he was transferred to Left Assistant Administrator of Zhejiang, then retired due to illness.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，言官交薦，召為大理右少卿。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor acceded, remonstrating officials jointly recommended him, and he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong Emperor acceded, remonstrating officials jointly recommended him, and he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 正德二年以右僉都御史督蘇、松糧儲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to oversee grain storage in Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to oversee grain storage in Suzhou and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召入為右副都御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to serve as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to serve as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 坐累，下詔獄。

translations.literal: He was implicated and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was implicated in a case and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 獄上，劉瑾以同鄉故，立命出之。

translations.literal: When the case reached the throne, Jin, because they were from the same district, immediately ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: When the case reached the throne, Liu Jin, because they were from the same native district, immediately ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 召與語，大悅，即用為戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned to converse with him, Jin was greatly delighted and immediately appointed him Left Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to speak with him, Liu Jin was greatly delighted and immediately appointed him Left Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 福強結幹吏，所在著能聲。

translations.literal: Fu had always cultivated connections with capable clerks and everywhere built a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu had always cultivated ties with capable clerks and everywhere won a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 至是受挫，為瑾所拔擢，遂精心事瑾，為效力。

translations.literal: Now, having suffered setback, he was promoted by Jin and thereupon devoted himself wholeheartedly to serving Jin, exerting himself on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Now, having suffered a fall, he was raised up by Liu Jin and thereupon devoted himself wholeheartedly to Liu Jin's service, laboring on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 瑾亦時召與謀，委寄亞於綵。

translations.literal: Jin also summoned him from time to time for counsel, entrusting him with responsibilities second only to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin also summoned him from time to time for counsel, entrusting him with responsibilities second only to Zhang Cai.

sentences.zh: 會湖廣以缺餉告，命兼僉都御史往理之。

translations.literal: It happened that Huguang reported a shortage of provisions, and Fu was ordered additionally as Assistant Censor-in-Chief to go manage the matter.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Huguang reported a shortage of provisions, and Han Fu was additionally appointed Assistant Censor-in-Chief and sent to manage the matter.

sentences.zh: 瑾喜操切，福希指，益務為嚴苛。

translations.literal: Jin delighted in harsh, incisive measures; Fu, seeking to please him, strove all the more to be severe and exacting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin delighted in harsh, incisive measures; Han Fu, eager to please him, strove all the more to be severe and exacting.

sentences.zh: 湖廣民租自私弘治改元後，逋六百餘萬石，皆遇災蠲免。

translations.literal: Private land rents in Huguang, since the first year of Hongzhi's renewal of the reign title, had fallen overdue by more than six million shi—all exempted due to disasters encountered.
translations.idiomatic: Private land rents in Huguang, since the first year of the Hongzhi reign, had fallen overdue by more than six million shi—all of it exempted because of disasters encountered.

sentences.zh: 福欲追徵之，劾所司催科不力，自巡撫鄭時以下凡千二百人。

translations.literal: Fu wished to pursue collection of these arrears; he impeached the responsible offices for lax collection, implicating everyone from Grand Coordinator Zheng Shi downward—twelve hundred persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu wished to pursue collection of these arrears; he impeached the responsible offices for lax collection, implicating everyone from Grand Coordinator Zheng Shi downward—twelve hundred persons in all.

sentences.zh: 奏至，舉朝駭愕，戶部尚書劉璣等議如福言。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the whole court was shocked; Revenue Minister Liu Ji and others deliberated in accordance with Fu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the whole court was shocked; Revenue Minister Liu Ji and others deliberated in accordance with Han Fu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 瑾忽怒福，取詔旨報曰：「湖廣軍民困敝，朕甚憫之。

translations.literal: Jin suddenly grew angry at Fu and took the imperial edict in reply, saying: 'The soldiers and people of Huguang are weary and impoverished; We are deeply compassionate toward them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin suddenly turned on Han Fu and issued an imperial edict in reply: "The soldiers and people of Huguang are weary and impoverished; We are deeply compassionate toward them.

sentences.zh: 福任意苛斂，甚不稱朕意，令自劾，吏部舉堪代者以聞。」

translations.literal: Fu has arbitrarily imposed harsh levies, which greatly fails to accord with Our intent. Let him memorialize his own dismissal; the Ministry of Personnel is to nominate suitable replacements and report.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu has arbitrarily imposed harsh levies, which greatly fails to accord with Our intent. Let him memorialize his own dismissal; the Ministry of Personnel is to nominate suitable replacements and report.

sentences.zh: 福引罪求罷，乃召還。
