translations.literal: Fu acknowledged his guilt and requested dismissal, and was then recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu acknowledged his guilt and requested dismissal, and was then recalled.

sentences.zh: 四年復命核遼東屯田。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again ordered to audit military colonies in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was again ordered to audit military colonies in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 福性故刻深，所攜同知劉玉等又奉行過當。

translations.literal: Fu was by nature severe and deep; the Assistant Commander Liu Yu and others he brought with him also carried out orders to excess.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu was by nature harsh and unyielding; the Assistant Commander Liu Yu and others he brought with him also enforced his orders to excess.

sentences.zh: 軍士不能堪，焚掠將吏及諸大姓家。

translations.literal: The soldiers could not endure it; they burned and plundered the homes of commanders and officials and of great clans.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers could not endure it; they burned and plundered the homes of commanders, officials, and great clans.

sentences.zh: 守臣發帑撫慰之。

translations.literal: The defending officials opened the treasury to console and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The defending officials opened the treasury to console and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 亂始定。

translations.literal: Only then was the disturbance settled.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was the disturbance settled.

sentences.zh: 給事中徐仁等極論之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Xu Ren and others memorialized forcefully against this.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Xu Ren and others memorialized forcefully against this.

sentences.zh: 瑾迫公議，勒福致仕。

translations.literal: Jin, pressed by public opinion, compelled Fu to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin, pressed by public opinion, compelled Han Fu to retire.

sentences.zh: 明年瑾敗，籍其貲，則福在湖廣時所饋白金數十萬兩，封識宛然，遂遣戍固原。

translations.literal: The next year when Jin fell, his assets were confiscated—and there were several hundred thousand taels of silver that Fu had presented during his time in Huguang, the seals still intact; he was accordingly banished to Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Liu Jin fell, his confiscated assets included several hundred thousand taels of silver that Han Fu had presented during his time in Huguang, the seals still intact; Han Fu was accordingly banished to Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 李憲，岐山人。

translations.literal: Li Xian was a native of Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian was a native of Qishan.

sentences.zh: 為吏科給事中，諂事瑾，每率眾請事於瑾，盛氣獨前，自號六科都給事中。

translations.literal: As a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel, he flattered and served Jin; each time he would lead the crowd to petition Jin, striding forward with overbearing manner, styling himself Chief Supervising Secretary of the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: As a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel, he fawned on Liu Jin; each time he would lead the crowd to petition Liu Jin, striding forward with overbearing airs and styling himself Chief Supervising Secretary of the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 時袖白金示同列曰：「此劉公所遺也。」

translations.literal: He would at times pull silver from his sleeve to show his colleagues, saying: 'This was a gift from Lord Liu.
translations.idiomatic: He would sometimes draw silver from his sleeve to show his colleagues, saying, "This was a gift from Lord Liu.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，虞禍及，亦劾瑾六事。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, fearing calamity would reach him, he also memorialized six charges against Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin fell, fearing that retribution would reach him, he also memorialized six charges against Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾在獄，笑曰：「李憲亦劾我乎？」

translations.literal: Jin, in prison, laughed and said: 'Li Xian memorializes against me too?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin, in prison, laughed and said, "Li Xian memorializes against me too?

sentences.zh: 卒坐除名。

translations.literal: In the end he was sentenced to removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Li Xian was sentenced to removal from office.

sentences.zh: 張龍，順天人。

translations.literal: Zhang Long was a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Long was a native of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 官行人，邪媚無賴，與壽寧侯通譜系，因得交諸中人、貴戚，恃勢奪人田宅。

translations.literal: He held the post of Courier; sycophantic and worthless, he claimed kinship with the Marquis of Shouning and thereby gained acquaintance with various eunuchs and noble relatives, relying on their power to seize others' fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Courier; sycophantic and worthless, he claimed kinship with the Marquis of Shouning and thereby gained access to eunuchs and noble relatives, relying on their power to seize others' fields and houses.

sentences.zh: 正德三年夤緣為兵科給事中，出核遼東軍餉，得腐豆四石。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde, through pull he became a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War, went out to audit Liaodong military provisions, and discovered four shi of spoiled beans.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengde, through pull he became a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War, went out to audit Liaodong military provisions, and discovered four shi of spoiled beans.

sentences.zh: 請逮問監守諸臣，罰郎中徐璉以下米三百石有差。

translations.literal: He requested that supervising and guarding officials be arrested for questioning, and fined Registrar Xu Lian and others varying amounts of three hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that supervising and guarding officials be arrested for questioning, and fined Registrar Xu Lian and others, in varying amounts, three hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 瑾以為能，擢通政參議。

translations.literal: Jin considered him capable and promoted him to Participating Secretary of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin considered him capable and promoted him to Participating Secretary of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，謫知灤州。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, he was demoted to magistrate of Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin fell, he was demoted to magistrate of Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 後又結朱寧為父，起嘉興同知，遷登州知府。

translations.literal: Later he also formed a bond with Zhu Ning as his adoptive father, was restored as Vice Magistrate of Jiaxing, and was transferred to prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also took Zhu Ning as his adoptive father, was restored as Vice Magistrate of Jiaxing, and was transferred to prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 言官彈射無虛月。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials impeached him without a month passing idle.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials impeached him month after month without pause.

sentences.zh: 與山西左布政使倪天民、右布政使陳逵、右參議孫清並貪殘，天下目為「四害」。

translations.literal: Together with Left Provincial Administrator Ni Tianmin of Shanxi, Right Provincial Administrator Chen Kui, and Right Assistant Administrator Sun Qing, all were greedy and cruel—the world regarded them as the 'Four Scourges.'
translations.idiomatic: Together with Left Provincial Administrator Ni Tianmin of Shanxi, Right Provincial Administrator Chen Kui, and Right Assistant Administrator Sun Qing, all were greedy and cruel—the world regarded them as the "Four Scourges."

sentences.zh: 龍朝覲入都，中旨擢右通政，為寧通中外賄，所乾沒不貲。

translations.literal: When Long came to court for an audience, a secret edict promoted him to Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission, serving as Zhu Ning's conduit for bribes inside and outside; what he embezzled was beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Long came to court for an audience, a secret edict promoted him to Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission; he served as Zhu Ning's conduit for bribes inside and outside the court, and what he embezzled was beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 後以私取賄，為寧所覺，斥逐之。

translations.literal: Later, for privately taking bribes, he was discovered by Zhu Ning and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for privately taking bribes, he was discovered by Zhu Ning and driven out.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，下獄論死。

translations.literal: In the early Jiajing period he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jiajing period he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 顧秉謙

translations.literal: Gu Bingqian
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bingqian

sentences.zh: (魏廣微)

translations.literal: (Wei Guangwei)
translations.idiomatic: (with Wei Guangwei)

sentences.zh: 廣微，南樂人，侍郎允貞子也。

translations.literal: Guangwei was a native of Nanle, son of Vice Minister Yun Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangwei was a native of Nanle, son of Vice Minister Yun Zhen.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士歷南京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Academic Probationer he rose through ranks to Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin Academic Probationer he rose through the ranks to Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 忠賢用事，以同鄉同姓潛結之，遂召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian held power, through shared native place and surname he secretly allied with him, and was thereupon summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian held power, through shared native place and surname he secretly allied with him and was thereupon summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 至是，與秉謙俱以原官兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: At this time, both he and Bingqian were appointed Grand Secretaries while retaining their original posts, at the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At this time both he and Gu Bingqian were appointed Grand Secretaries while retaining their original posts, at the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 七月，秉謙晉太子太保，改文淵閣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Bingqian was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Gu Bingqian was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十一月晉少保、太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年正月晉少傅、太子太師、吏部尚書，改建極殿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, first month, he was promoted to Junior Preceptor, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel, and transferred to the Jidian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, first month, he was promoted to Junior Preceptor, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel, and transferred to the Jidian Hall.

sentences.zh: 九月晉少師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was promoted to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: That September he was promoted to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 秉謙為人，庸劣無恥，而廣微陰狡。

translations.literal: Bingqian as a man was mediocre, base, and shameless, whereas Guangwei was secretly cunning and treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bingqian was a mediocre, shameless man; Wei Guangwei was sly and treacherous beneath the surface.

sentences.zh: 趙南星與其父允貞友善，嘗嘆曰：「見泉無子。」

translations.literal: Zhao Nanxing was on friendly terms with his father Yunzhen and once sighed, saying, "Jianquan has no son."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nanxing was close to Wei Guangwei's father, Yunzhen, and once sighed and said, "Jianquan has no son."

sentences.zh: 見泉，允貞別號也。

translations.literal: Jianquan was Yunzhen's alternative style name.
translations.idiomatic: Jianquan was Yunzhen's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 廣微聞之，恨刺骨。

translations.literal: Guangwei heard of this and hated him to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwei heard this, his hatred cut to the bone.

sentences.zh: 既柄政，三及南星門，閽人辭不見。

translations.literal: Once he held power, he went three times to Nanxing's gate, but the gatekeeper declined and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power, he called three times at Nanxing's door, but the gatekeeper turned him away.

sentences.zh: 廣微怫然曰：「他人可拒，相公尊，不可拒也。」

translations.literal: Guangwei said angrily, "Others may be refused, but the exalted Chancellor cannot be refused."
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei said in a fury, "You may refuse others, but you cannot refuse the Chancellor himself."

sentences.zh: 益恨南星。

translations.literal: He hated Nanxing all the more.
translations.idiomatic: His hatred of Nanxing only deepened.

sentences.zh: 楊漣之劾忠賢二十四罪也，忠賢懼，屬廣微為調旨，一如忠賢意。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian impeached Zhongxian with twenty-four charges, Zhongxian was afraid and entrusted Guangwei to draft the rescript, exactly as Zhongxian wished.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian memorialized against Wei Zhongxian with twenty-four counts of misconduct, Zhongxian grew afraid and had Guangwei draft the imperial response—word for word as he wanted it.

sentences.zh: 而秉謙以漣疏有「門生宰相」語，怒甚。

translations.literal: Yet Bingqian was furious because Yang's memorial contained the phrase "student who became Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bingqian was enraged, for Yang's memorial had called him a "student who rose to be Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 會孟冬饗廟，且頒朔，廣微偃蹇後至，給事中魏大中、御史李應升連劾之。

translations.literal: On the occasion of the first-month winter temple sacrifice, when the new moon was also distributed, Guangwei arrived late and arrogant; Supervising Secretary Wei Dazhong and Censor Li Yingsheng jointly impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter temple sacrifice, when the court also issued the calendar for the new month, Guangwei arrived late and insolent; Supervising Secretary Wei Dazhong and Censor Li Yingsheng impeached him in succession.

sentences.zh: 廣微益憤，遂決意傾善類，與秉謙謀盡逐諸正人，點《縉紳便覽》一冊，若葉向高、韓爌、何如寵、成基命、繆昌期、姚希孟、陳子壯、侯恪、趙南星、高攀龍、喬允升、李邦華、鄭三俊、楊漣、左光鬥、魏大中、黃尊素、周宗建、李應升等百餘人，目為邪黨，而以黃克纘、王永光、徐大化、賈繼春、霍維華等六十餘人為正人，由閹人王朝用進之，俾據是為黜陟。

translations.literal: Guangwei grew angrier still, thereupon resolved to overturn the good, and with Bingqian plotted to drive out all upright men; marking off one volume of 《The Gentry Handbook》, more than a hundred men such as Ye Xianggao, Han Kuang, He Ruchong, Cheng Jiming, Miao Changqi, Yao Ximeng, Chen Zizhuang, Hou Ke, Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Qiao Yunsheng, Li Banghua, Zheng Sanjun, Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, Huang Zunsu, Zhou Zongjian, and Li Yingsheng were labeled an evil faction, while more than sixty men such as Huang Kezuan, Wang Yongguang, Xu Dahua, Jia Jichun, and Huo Weihua were deemed upright men; these lists were submitted through the eunuch Wang Chaoyong, so that appointments and dismissals might be made according to them.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Guangwei resolved to destroy the righteous. With Gu Bingqian he plotted to purge every upright official, compiling a list from 《The Gentry Handbook》: Ye Xianggao, Han Kuang, He Ruchong, Cheng Jiming, Miao Changqi, Yao Ximeng, Chen Zizhuang, Hou Ke, Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Qiao Yunsheng, Li Banghua, Zheng Sanjun, Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, Huang Zunsu, Zhou Zongjian, Li Yingsheng, and more than a hundred others were branded an evil faction; Huang Kezuan, Wang Yongguang, Xu Dahua, Jia Jichun, Huo Weihua, and sixty-odd others were declared the righteous. The eunuch Wang Chaoyong delivered the lists, and on their basis men were promoted or cast out.

sentences.zh: 忠賢得內閣為羽翼，勢益張。

translations.literal: Zhongxian gained the Grand Secretariat as wings, and his power grew yet greater.
translations.idiomatic: With the Grand Secretariat as his wings, Wei Zhongxian's power swelled still further.

sentences.zh: 秉謙、廣微亦曲奉忠賢，若奴役然。

translations.literal: Bingqian and Guangwei also bent obsequiously to serve Zhongxian, as if they were his slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bingqian and Wei Guangwei groveled before Zhongxian like bondsmen.

sentences.zh: 葉向高、韓爌相繼罷，何宗彥卒，秉謙遂為首輔。

translations.literal: Ye Xianggao and Han Kuang were dismissed in succession; He Zongyan died; and Bingqian thereupon became chief Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao and Han Kuang were removed one after another; He Zongyan died; and Gu Bingqian became chief Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 自四年十二月至六年九月，凡傾害忠直，皆秉謙票擬。

translations.literal: From the twelfth month of the fourth year to the ninth month of the sixth year, every injury to the loyal and upright was drafted on rescripts by Bingqian.
translations.idiomatic: From the twelfth month of the fourth year to the ninth month of the sixth, every blow struck against loyal and upright officials bore Gu Bingqian's draft rescript.

sentences.zh: 《三朝要典》之作，秉謙為總裁，復擬御制序冠其首，欲用是鉗天下口。

translations.literal: When 《The Essential Records of Three Reigns》 was compiled, Bingqian served as chief editor and also drafted an imperial preface to crown its opening, intending thereby to seal the mouths of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bingqian served as chief editor of 《The Essential Records of Three Reigns》 and drafted an imperial preface to stand at its head, hoping thereby to silence the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有一舉動，輒擬旨歸美忠賢，褒贊不已。

translations.literal: Whenever the court took any action, they would draft rescripts praising Zhongxian without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At the court's every move they drafted rescripts heaping praise on Wei Zhongxian, again and again.

sentences.zh: 廣微以劄通忠賢，簽其函曰「內閣家報」，時稱曰「外魏公」。

translations.literal: Guangwei communicated with Zhongxian by letter, inscribing the envelope "Grand Secretariat Family Dispatch"; at the time he was called "Lord Wei Without."
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei kept up a correspondence with Zhongxian, marking each envelope "Grand Secretariat Family Dispatch"; people called him "Lord Wei of the Outer Court."

sentences.zh: 先是，內閣調旨，惟出首輔一人，餘但參議論而已。

translations.literal: Previously, when the Grand Secretariat drafted rescripts, only the chief Grand Secretary issued them; the rest merely participated in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Grand Secretariat rescripts came from the chief Grand Secretary alone; the other members only joined in debate.

sentences.zh: 廣微欲擅柄，謀之忠賢，令眾輔分任，政權始分，後遂沿為故事。

translations.literal: Guangwei wished to monopolize power, consulted Zhongxian, and had all the Grand Secretaries share duties; political authority was first divided, and later this became established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei wanted sole control and consulted Zhongxian; the Grand Secretaries were made to divide the work, power was split for the first time, and the practice became fixed custom.

sentences.zh: 楊漣等六人之逮也，廣微實與其謀，秉謙調嚴旨，五日一追比。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian and the other five were arrested, Guangwei actually participated in the plot; Bingqian drafted a strict rescript requiring collection every five days.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian and five others were seized, Guangwei had in fact helped plan it; Gu Bingqian drafted a harsh rescript demanding payment under threat of punishment every five days.

sentences.zh: 尚書崔景榮懼其立死杖下，亟請廣微諫止。

translations.literal: Minister Cui Jingrong feared they would die immediately under the rods and urgently asked Guangwei to remonstrate and stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Cui Jingrong feared they would be beaten to death on the spot and urgently begged Guangwei to remonstrate and put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 廣微不自安，疏言：「漣等在今日，誠為有罪之人，在前日實為卿寺之佐。

translations.literal: Guangwei, ill at ease, memorialized, saying, "Yang Lian and the others are indeed guilty men today, but yesterday they were aides in the ministries and directorates.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his own mind, Guangwei submitted a memorial: "Yang Lian and the rest are guilty men today, but only yesterday they served as officials in the ministries and directorates.

sentences.zh: 縱使贓私果真，亦當輔付法司，據律論罪，豈可逐日嚴刑，令鎮撫追贓乎？

translations.literal: Even if their corruption were truly proven, they should still be handed over to the judicial authorities and sentenced according to law—how can they be subjected to daily severe punishments while the Brocade Guard is made to extort bribes?
translations.idiomatic: Even if their graft were proved beyond doubt, they ought to be handed to the judicial authorities and punished by law—how can they be tortured day after day while the Brocade Guard is sent to squeeze out bribes?

sentences.zh: 身非木石，重刑之下，就死直須臾耳。

translations.literal: One's body is not wood or stone; under heavy punishment, death comes in but a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Flesh and blood are not wood or stone; under savage beating, death is only a breath away.

sentences.zh: 以理刑之職，使之追贓，官守安在？

translations.literal: To assign the duty of judging crimes to men and then make them extort bribes—where is the integrity of office?
translations.idiomatic: To set men to judge crimes and then order them to hunt for bribes—what becomes of official duty?

sentences.zh: 勿論傷好生之仁，抑且違祖宗之制，將朝政日亂，與古之帝王大不相侔矣。」

translations.literal: Setting aside the harm to the virtue of sparing life, this also violates the institutions of our ancestors; the court will grow daily more chaotic and will greatly fail to resemble the emperors of old."
translations.idiomatic: Never mind the injury to the virtue of sparing life—it also breaks the institutions of the founding emperors; the court will sink deeper into disorder and bear no resemblance to the sage-kings of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 疏入，大忤忠賢意。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it greatly contravened Zhongxian's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial enraged Wei Zhongxian when it reached him.

sentences.zh: 廣微懼，急出景榮手書自明，而忠賢怒已不可解。

translations.literal: Guangwei was afraid and hastily produced Jingrong's handwritten letter to explain himself, but Zhongxian's anger could no longer be resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei panicked and quickly produced Jingrong's own letter to clear himself, but Zhongxian's wrath could no longer be appeased.

sentences.zh: 乃具疏乞休，不許。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial requesting retirement; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial begging to retire; it was refused.

sentences.zh: 居兩月，矯詔切責廷臣，中言「朕方率循舊章，而曰『朝政日亂』，朕方祖述堯、舜，而曰『大不相侔』」，蓋即指廣微疏語。

translations.literal: After two months, a forged edict severely rebuked the court officials, stating among other things, "I am just now following the old regulations, yet you say 'the court grows daily more chaotic'; I am just now emulating Yao and Shun, yet you say 'greatly unlike'"—clearly pointing to Guangwei's memorial words.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later a forged edict sharply rebuked the court, declaring, "I am just now following the old statutes, and you say 'the court grows daily more chaotic'; I am just now emulating Yao and Shun, and you say 'greatly unlike'"—plainly aimed at Guangwei's own words.

sentences.zh: 廣微益懼，丐秉謙為解，忠賢意少釋。

translations.literal: Guangwei grew more afraid, begged Bingqian to intercede, and Zhongxian's anger eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei grew still more afraid and begged Gu Bingqian to intercede; Zhongxian's anger eased a little.

sentences.zh: 然廣微卒不自安，復三疏乞休，五年八月許之去。

translations.literal: Yet Guangwei still could not be at ease, again submitted three memorials begging to retire, and in the eighth month of the fifth year was permitted to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Still unable to rest easy, Guangwei submitted three more memorials begging to leave office; in the eighth month of the fifth year he was at last allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 廣微先已加少保、太子太傅，改吏部尚書、建極殿大學士，至是復加少傅、太子太師，蔭子中書舍人，賜白金百、坐蟒一、彩幣四表裏，乘傳，行人護歸。

translations.literal: Guangwei had already been promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, transferred to Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Jianji Hall; now he was further made Junior Mentor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, his son granted the post of Secretariat Drafting Officer, given one hundred taels of white gold, one python robe, four sets of colored silks inside and out, transport by official relay, and an attendant to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei had already risen to Junior Guardian and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and been made Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Jianji Hall; now he was further promoted to Junior Mentor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, his son ennobled as a Secretariat Drafting Officer, and he was given a hundred taels of white silver, a python robe, four suits of colored silk, relay horses for the journey home, and an attendant to escort him.

sentences.zh: 典禮優渥，猶用前好故也。

translations.literal: The rites of honor were generous, still owing to their former good relations.
translations.idiomatic: The honors were lavish—a last courtesy to an old ally.

sentences.zh: 居二年，卒於家，贈太傅，恤典如制。

translations.literal: After two years at home he died; posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, with condolence rites per regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died at home; he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, with funeral rites according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 秉謙票擬，事事徇忠賢指。

translations.literal: In drafting rescripts, Bingqian carried out Zhongxian's wishes on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: In every rescript he drafted, Gu Bingqian did exactly as Wei Zhongxian wished.

sentences.zh: 初矯旨罪主考丁乾學，又調旨殺漣、光鬥等。

translations.literal: At first he forged an edict condemning chief examiner Ding Qianxue; he also drafted rescripts that led to the execution of Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He forged an edict condemning chief examiner Ding Qianxue and drafted rescripts that sent Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, and others to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 惟周順昌、李應升等下詔獄，秉謙請付法司，毋令死非其罪。

translations.literal: Only in the cases of Zhou Shunchang and Li Yingsheng, who were sent to the imperial prison, did Bingqian request that they be turned over to the judicial authorities so they would not die unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Zhou Shunchang and Li Yingsheng were sent to the imperial prison did Gu Bingqian ask that they be handed to the judicial authorities, lest they die for crimes they had not committed.

sentences.zh: 內臣出鎮，秉謙撰上諭，已復與丁紹軾請罷。

translations.literal: When inner eunuchs were dispatched to garrison posts, Bingqian drafted the imperial proclamation; yet he again joined Ding Shaoshi in requesting their abolition.
translations.idiomatic: When palace eunuchs were sent out to garrison commands, Gu Bingqian drafted the imperial proclamation—yet he also joined Ding Shaoshi in asking that the practice be abolished.

sentences.zh: 二事微有執爭。

translations.literal: In these two matters there was slight dissent.
translations.idiomatic: In these two matters he showed a trace of resistance.

sentences.zh: 馮銓既入閣，同黨中日夜交軋，群小亦各有所左右。

translations.literal: Once Feng Quan entered the Grand Secretariat, factions within the same party wrangled day and night, and lesser men each had their own backers.
translations.idiomatic: After Feng Quan entered the Grand Secretariat, allies turned on one another day and night, and every petty man had his own patron.

sentences.zh: 秉謙不自安，屢疏乞休，後廣微一年致仕去。

translations.literal: Bingqian could not feel secure, repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire, and retired one year after Guangwei.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bingqian could not feel secure; he memorialized again and again to retire, and left office a year after Guangwei.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，為言官祖重曄、徐尚勛、汪應元所糾，命削籍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, he was impeached by censorial officials Zu Chongye, Xu Shangxun, and Wang Yingyuan, and ordered stripped of his registry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen, censorial officials Zu Chongye, Xu Shangxun, and Wang Yingyuan impeached him, and he was ordered struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 已，坐交結近侍，入逆案中，論徒三年，贖為民。

translations.literal: Later, for associating with close attendants, he was included in the Treason Case, sentenced to three years' exile, and ransomed back to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for consorting with palace favorites, he was named in the Treason Case, sentenced to three years' banishment, and allowed to ransom his way back to commoner life.

sentences.zh: 二年，昆山民積怨秉謙，聚眾焚掠其家。

translations.literal: In the second year, the people of Kunshan, who had long nursed grievances against Bingqian, gathered and burned and plundered his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the people of Kunshan, who had long hated Gu Bingqian, rose up, burned his house, and looted it.

sentences.zh: 秉謙年八十，倉皇竄漁舟得免，乃獻窖藏銀四萬於朝，寄居他縣以死。

translations.literal: Bingqian was eighty years old; fleeing in panic, he escaped on a fishing boat, then presented forty thousand taels of silver from his cellar hoard to the court and lived out his days in another county.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bingqian was eighty; he fled in panic and escaped aboard a fishing boat, then surrendered forty thousand taels of silver from his cellar to the court and lived out his days in another county.

sentences.zh: 廣微亦追論削奪，列逆案遣戍中。

translations.literal: Guangwei was also retrospectively prosecuted and stripped of honors, listed in the Treason Case, and banished to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangwei was also prosecuted in retrospect, stripped of honors, named in the Treason Case, and sent into exile in the interior.

sentences.zh: 黃立極 施鳳來 張瑞圖 來宗道 楊景辰

translations.literal: Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, Zhang Ruitu, Lai Zongdao, Yang Jingchen
translations.idiomatic: Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, Zhang Ruitu, Lai Zongdao, Yang Jingchen

sentences.zh: 自秉謙、廣微當國，政歸忠賢。

translations.literal: From the time Bingqian and Guangwei held state power, government affairs passed to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gu Bingqian and Wei Guangwei held the reins, real power passed to Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 其後入閣者黃立極、施鳳來、張瑞圖之屬，皆依媚取容，名麗逆案。

translations.literal: Those who entered the Grand Secretariat afterward—Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, Zhang Ruitu, and their kind—all relied on flattery to win favor and were named in the Treason Case.
translations.idiomatic: Those who entered the Grand Secretariat after them—Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, Zhang Ruitu, and men like them—won favor through fawning and were all named in the Treason Case.

sentences.zh: 黃立極，字中五，元城人。

translations.literal: Huang Liji, styled Zhongwu, was a native of Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Liji, courtesy name Zhongwu, was a native of Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 累官少詹事、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose through the posts of Junior Mentor and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Junior Mentor and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年八月，忠賢以同鄉故，擢禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，與丁紹軾、周如磐、馮銓並參機務。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Tianqi, Zhongxian, on account of their being fellow-townsmen, promoted him to Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, and he joined Ding Shaoshi, Zhou Rupan, and Feng Quan in attending to state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Tianqi, Wei Zhongxian, citing their shared hometown, promoted him to Minister of Rites and Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary; he joined Ding Shaoshi, Zhou Rupan, and Feng Quan in directing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 時魏廣微、顧秉謙皆以附忠賢居政府。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Guangwei and Gu Bingqian both held government power by attaching themselves to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Guangwei and Gu Bingqian both held power in the government by clinging to Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 未幾廣微去，如磐卒。

translations.literal: Before long Guangwei left office, and Rupan died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guangwei left office, and Rupan died.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，紹軾亦卒，銓罷。

translations.literal: The next summer Shaoshi also died, and Quan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer Shaoshi died as well, and Feng Quan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 其秋，施鳳來、張瑞圖、李國𣚴入。

translations.literal: That autumn Shi Fenglai, Zhang Ruitu, and Li Guozhen entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Shi Fenglai, Zhang Ruitu, and Li Guozhen entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 已而秉謙乞歸，立極遂為首輔。

translations.literal: Before long Bingqian requested to retire, and Liji thereupon became chief Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gu Bingqian asked to retire, and Huang Liji became chief Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 宗道，蕭山人。

translations.literal: Zongdao was a native of Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zongdao was a native of Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 立極同年進士，累官太子太保、禮部尚書，以本官兼內閣大學士，預機務。

translations.literal: Liji, a jinshi of the same year, rose through the posts of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites, and served as Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat with his existing rank, participating in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Liji, a jinshi of the same year, rose to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites, then served as Grand Secretary with those ranks and took part in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 宗道官禮部時，為崔呈秀父請恤典，中有「在天之靈」語。

translations.literal: When Zongdao served in the Ministry of Rites, he requested funeral honors for Cui Chengxiu's father, using among other phrases "his spirit in heaven."
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Ministry of Rites, Lai Zongdao petitioned for funeral honors for Cui Chengxiu's father, writing among other things of "his spirit in heaven."

sentences.zh: 編修倪元璐屢疏爭時事，宗道笑曰：「渠何事多言，詞林故事，止香茗耳。」

translations.literal: Compiler Ni Yuanlu repeatedly memorialized on current affairs; Zongdao laughed and said, "What business has he airing so many words? The custom of the Hanlin Academy is nothing but tea and refreshments.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Ni Yuanlu memorialized again and again on affairs of the day; Zongdao laughed and said, "What does he have to talk so much about? In the Hanlin Academy the whole custom is tea and snacks.

sentences.zh: 時謂宗道清客宰相云。

translations.literal: At the time people called Zongdao the "tea-and-snacks Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: People called him the "tea-and-snacks Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 景辰，瑞圖同縣人。

translations.literal: Jingchen was a fellow-countryman of Ruitu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jingchen was a fellow townsman of Zhang Ruitu.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 積官吏部右侍郎，與宗道同入閣。

translations.literal: He accumulated the post of Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Personnel and entered the Grand Secretariat together with Zongdao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Personnel and entered the Grand Secretariat together with Lai Zongdao.

sentences.zh: 官翰林時，為《要典》副總裁，一徇奸黨指，又三疏頌忠賢。

translations.literal: When he served in the Hanlin Academy, he was deputy chief editor of 《The Essential Records》 and wholly followed the wicked faction's wishes; he also submitted three memorials extolling Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: As a Hanlin compiler he served as deputy chief editor of 《The Essential Records》, doing exactly as the wicked faction wished; he also submitted three memorials praising Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 及朝局已變，乃請毀《要典》，給事、御史交劾之，與宗道同日罷。

translations.literal: When the court situation had already changed, he requested the destruction of 《The Essential Records》; supervising secretaries and censors jointly impeached him, and he was dismissed on the same day as Zongdao.
translations.idiomatic: When the political tide had turned, he asked that 《The Essential Records》 be destroyed; supervising secretaries and censors impeached him in a body, and he was dismissed on the same day as Lai Zongdao.

sentences.zh: 其後定逆案，瑞圖、宗道初不與，莊烈帝詰之，韓爌等封無實狀。

translations.literal: Later when the Treason Case was settled, Ruitu and Zongdao were at first not included; Emperor Zhuanglie questioned this, and Han Kuang and others replied that there was no substantiated evidence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Treason Case was later settled, Zhang Ruitu and Lai Zongdao were at first left out; the Chongzhen Emperor questioned this, and Han Kuang and others answered that there was no solid evidence.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「瑞圖為忠賢書碑，宗道稱呈秀父『在天之靈』，非實狀耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Ruitu wrote a stele inscription for Zhongxian, and Zongdao spoke of Chengxiu's father's 'spirit in heaven'—is that not substantiated evidence?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhang Ruitu wrote an inscription for Wei Zhongxian's stele, and Lai Zongdao spoke of Cui Chengxiu's father's 'spirit in heaven'—are those not facts?

sentences.zh: 乃以瑞圖、宗道與顧秉謙、馮銓等坐贖徒為民，而立極、鳳來、景辰落職閑住。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruitu and Zongdao, together with Gu Bingqian, Feng Quan, and others, were sentenced to commute exile and become commoners; Liji, Fenglai, and Jingchen were removed from office and left idle.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhang Ruitu and Lai Zongdao, together with Gu Bingqian, Feng Quan, and others, were sentenced to banishment commutable to commoner status; Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, and Yang Jingchen were stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 崔呈秀

translations.literal: Cui Chengxiu
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chengxiu

sentences.zh: 崔呈秀，薊州人。

translations.literal: Cui Chengxiu was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chengxiu was a native of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed as a Palace Messenger.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Palace Messenger.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，擢御史，巡按淮、揚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was promoted to censor and sent on an inspection tour of Huai and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianqi reign he was promoted to censor and sent to inspect Huai and Yang.

sentences.zh: 卑汙狡獪，不修士行。

translations.literal: Base, filthy, cunning, and slippery, he did not maintain the conduct of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Vile, corrupt, cunning, and slippery, he kept none of a gentleman's standards.

sentences.zh: 見東林勢方盛，將出都，力薦李三才，求入其黨，東林拒不納。

translations.literal: Seeing that the Donglin faction's power was then flourishing, as he was about to leave the capital he vigorously recommended Li Sancai and sought to join their faction, but the Donglin refused to accept him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Donglin faction in the ascendant, he was about to leave the capital when he loudly recommended Li Sancai and tried to join their ranks; the Donglin would not have him.

sentences.zh: 在淮、揚，贓私狼籍。

translations.literal: In Huai and Yang his corruption was rampant.
translations.idiomatic: In Huai and Yang his corruption ran wild.

sentences.zh: 霍丘知縣鄭延祚貪，將劾之，以千金賄免。

translations.literal: Zheng Yanzuo, magistrate of Huoqiu, was greedy; Chengxiu was about to impeach him, but Yanzuo bribed him with a thousand taels of silver to escape prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yanzuo, magistrate of Huoqiu, was corrupt; Chengxiu was about to impeach him, but Yanzuo paid a thousand taels of silver and bought his way free.

sentences.zh: 延祚知其易與，再行千金，即薦之。

translations.literal: Yanzuo knew he was easy to deal with and offered another thousand taels, whereupon Chengxiu immediately recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzuo knew him for an easy mark and paid another thousand taels; Chengxiu at once recommended him for promotion.

sentences.zh: 其行事多類此。

translations.literal: Most of his conduct was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Most of what he did was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 四年九月還朝，高攀龍為都御史，盡發其貪汙狀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year he returned to court; Gao Panlong as Censor-in-Chief fully exposed his corrupt acts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year he returned to court; Censor-in-Chief Gao Panlong laid bare every detail of his corruption.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書趙南星議戍之，詔革職候勘。

translations.literal: Zhao Nanxing as Minister of Personnel proposed banishing him; an edict stripped him of office pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhao Nanxing proposed banishing him; an edict removed him from office pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 呈秀大窘，夜走魏忠賢所，叩頭乞哀，言攀龍、南星皆東林，挾私排陷，復叩頭涕泣，乞為養子。

translations.literal: Chengxiu was greatly distressed; by night he fled to Wei Zhongxian's residence, kowtowed and begged for mercy, saying Panlong and Nanxing were both Donglin men who persecuted him out of private spite; again he kowtowed and wept, begging to be adopted as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate, Cui Chengxiu fled by night to Wei Zhongxian's house, kowtowed and begged for pity, saying Panlong and Nanxing were both Donglin men who had framed him out of private spite; he kowtowed again, weeping, and begged to be taken as a son.

sentences.zh: 當是時，忠賢為廷臣交攻，憤甚，方思得外延為助。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongxian was under attack from court officials and was deeply angry, just then seeking outer-court allies.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Wei Zhongxian was under siege from court officials and burned with anger; he was looking for allies in the outer court.

sentences.zh: 涿州人馮銓，少年官侍從家居，與熊廷弼有隙，遺書魏良卿勸興大獄。

translations.literal: Feng Quan of Zhuozhou, who in youth had served as attendant and lived at home, had a feud with Xiong Tingbi and sent a letter to Wei Liangqing urging the launch of a major persecution.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan of Zhuozhou, who had served as a young attendant and then lived at home, bore a grudge against Xiong Tingbi and wrote to Wei Liangqing urging a great purge.

sentences.zh: 忠賢冀假事端傾陷諸害己者，得呈秀，恨相見晚，遂用為腹心，日與計畫。

translations.literal: Zhongxian hoped to use the occasion to destroy those who harmed him; gaining Chengxiu, he lamented they had not met sooner and thereupon made him his trusted confidant, meeting daily to plot.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian hoped to seize on the moment to ruin his enemies; finding Cui Chengxiu, he cried that they had met too late and made him his closest confidant, meeting daily to scheme.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，給事中李恒茂為呈秀訟冤。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Supervising Secretary Li Hengmao pleaded Chengxiu's case.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Supervising Secretary Li Hengmao memorialized in Cui Chengxiu's defense.

sentences.zh: 中旨即言呈秀被誣，復其官。

translations.literal: A palace rescript immediately stated that Chengxiu had been falsely accused and restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: A palace rescript at once declared that Cui Chengxiu had been slandered and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 呈秀乃首疏薦張鶴鳴、申用懋、王永光、商周祚、許弘綱等；

translations.literal: Chengxiu thereupon led with a memorial recommending Zhang Heming, Shen Yongmao, Wang Yongguang, Shang Zhouzuo, Xu Honggang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chengxiu then led with a memorial recommending Zhang Heming, Shen Yongmao, Wang Yongguang, Shang Zhouzuo, Xu Honggang, and others.

sentences.zh: 而再疏請令京官自陳，由是清流多屏斥。

translations.literal: In a second memorial he requested that capital officials be made to submit self-assessments, whereupon many of the upright were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In a second memorial he asked that capital officials be made to submit self-assessments, and many upright men were driven from office.

sentences.zh: 尋督三殿工，忠賢以閱工故，日至外朝。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised construction of the Three Halls; Zhongxian, on the pretext of inspecting the works, came daily to the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was put in charge of building the Three Halls; Wei Zhongxian, on the pretext of inspecting the work, came to the outer court every day.

sentences.zh: 呈秀必屏人密語，以間進《同志》諸錄，皆東林黨人。

translations.literal: Chengxiu always dismissed attendants for secret talk and gradually submitted 《Records of Comrades》 and other registers, listing Donglin faction members.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chengxiu always sent attendants away for secret talk and gradually submitted 《Records of Comrades》 and other registers naming Donglin men.

sentences.zh: 又進《天鑒錄》，皆不附東林者。

translations.literal: He also submitted 《The Mirror of Heaven》, listing those who did not attach themselves to the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted 《The Mirror of Heaven》, listing those who did not follow the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 令忠賢憑以黜陟，善類為一空。

translations.literal: He had Zhongxian rely on these for appointments and dismissals, until the ranks of good men were emptied out.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wei Zhongxian use these lists to decide appointments and dismissals until no good men remained at court.

sentences.zh: 暮夜乞憐者，莫不緣呈秀以進，繩集蟻附，其門如市。

translations.literal: Those who came by night begging favor all found their way to advancement through Chengxiu; they clustered like ropes and swarmed like ants, and his gate was like a marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Every man who came by night to beg for favor climbed to office through Cui Chengxiu; they roped themselves together and swarmed like ants until his gate was as crowded as a market.

sentences.zh: 累擢工部右侍郎並兼御史，督工如故。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works while also serving as censor; his supervision of construction continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Right Vice Minister of Works and concurrently censor, still supervising construction as before.

sentences.zh: 御史田景新言，侍郎兼御史非便，請改僉都御史，從之。

translations.literal: Censor Tian Jingxin said that a vice minister concurrently serving as censor was inconvenient; he requested changing the post to Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tian Jingxin argued that holding a vice ministership together with a censor's duties was awkward and asked that the post be changed to Assistant Censor-in-Chief; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 忠賢嘗修鄉縣肅寧城，呈秀首上疏稱美。

translations.literal: Zhongxian once repaired Suining city in his home county; Chengxiu was first to memorialize in praise.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian repaired Suining city in his home county, Cui Chengxiu was the first to memorialize in praise.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，復疏頌忠賢督工功，請賜敕獎諭，末言：「臣非行媚中官者，目前千譏萬罵，臣固甘之。」

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, he again memorialized praising Zhongxian's supervision of the works and requesting an imperial edict of commendation; at the end he said: "I am not one who fawns on palace eunuchs; though thousands revile and ten thousands curse me before my eyes, I am content with this.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year he memorialized again, praising Wei Zhongxian's supervision of the works and begging an edict of commendation; he closed with: "I am no sycophant of palace eunuchs; let thousands revile and ten thousands curse me—I am content.

sentences.zh: 疏出，朝野轟笑。

translations.literal: When the memorial was issued, court and country exploded in laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial appeared, and court and country erupted in laughter.

sentences.zh: 閣臣顧秉謙輩撰敕八百餘言，褒忠賢，極口揚詡，前代九錫文不能過也。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Gu Bingqian and others drafted a commendation of more than eight hundred words praising Zhongxian, extolling him to the utmost; even the nine-bestowals panegyrics of former dynasties could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Gu Bingqian and their colleagues drafted a commendation of more than eight hundred words, heaping praise on Wei Zhongxian with mouths opened wide—the nine-bestowals panegyrics of earlier ages could not have outdone it.

sentences.zh: 自是，中外章疏，無不頌忠賢功德者矣。

translations.literal: From this point, memorials within and without all praised Zhongxian's merits and virtues.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth memorials from every quarter sang only of Wei Zhongxian's merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 時方創《三朝要典》，呈秀疏陳耍典之源，追論並封、妖書、之藩三事，凡擁衛光宗者，悉加醜詆。

translations.literal: At the time 《The Essential Records of Three Reigns》 was being compiled; Chengxiu memorialized on the origins of the essential records, revisiting the three affairs of joint memorials, the demon book, and princes leaving the capital; all who had supported Guangzong were thoroughly slandered.
translations.idiomatic: While 《The Essential Records of Three Reigns》 was being compiled, Cui Chengxiu memorialized on the work's origins, rehashing the joint memorials, the demon book, and the princes' departure from the capital—all who had rallied to Guangzong he vilified without mercy.

sentences.zh: 忠賢悅，宣付史館。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was pleased and ordered it proclaimed and sent to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was pleased and had the memorial proclaimed and forwarded to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，進本部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year, he was promoted to Minister of his own ministry.
translations.idiomatic: That July he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十月，皇極殿成，加太子太保兼左都御史，仍督大工。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, when the Hall of Imperial Zenith was completed, he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Censor-in-Chief, still supervising the great works.
translations.idiomatic: In October, when the Hall of Imperial Zenith was completed, he was additionally made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Censor-in-Chief, still overseeing the great construction projects.

sentences.zh: 母死，不奔喪，奪情視事。

translations.literal: His mother died; he did not rush home for mourning but continued in office by imperial dispensation.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he did not leave office to mourn; granted leave from mourning, he continued in his duties.

sentences.zh: 呈秀負忠賢寵，嗜利彌甚。

translations.literal: Chengxiu relied on Zhongxian's favor and grew ever greedier for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in Wei Zhongxian's favor, Cui Chengxiu grew ever more rapacious.

sentences.zh: 朝士多拜為門下士，以通於忠賢。

translations.literal: Many court officials sought to become his followers in order to gain access to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials enrolled as his followers to reach Wei Zhongxian through him.

sentences.zh: 其不附己及勢位相軋者，輒使其黨排去之，時有「五虎」之目，以呈秀為魁。

translations.literal: Those who would not attach to him and those whose power clashed with his, he would have his faction drive out; at the time they were called the "Five Tigers," with Chengxiu as the chief.
translations.idiomatic: Those who refused to join him, or whose power rivaled his own, he had his faction hound from office; people called them the "Five Tigers," with Cui Chengxiu at their head.

sentences.zh: 諸所傾陷，不可悉數，雖其黨亦深畏之。

translations.literal: The men they ruined cannot all be counted; even their own faction deeply feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The men they brought down were beyond counting, and even their own allies feared them deeply.

sentences.zh: 子鐸不能文，屬考官孫之獬，獲鄉薦。

translations.literal: His son Duo could not write; he entrusted examiner Sun Zhixie, who obtained provincial recommendation for him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duo was no scholar; through examiner Sun Zhixie he secured provincial recommendation.

sentences.zh: 用其弟凝秀為浙江總兵官，女夫張元芳為吏部主事，妾弟優人蕭惟中為密雲參將，所司皆不敢違。

translations.literal: He appointed his brother Ningxiu as regional commander of Zhejiang, his daughter's husband Zhang Yuanfang as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, his concubine's younger brother the actor Xiao Weizhong as deputy regional commander of Miyun; none in those offices dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his brother Ningxiu as Zhejiang regional commander, his son-in-law Zhang Yuanfang as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, and his concubine's brother the actor Xiao Weizhong as Miyun deputy commander—and no one in those posts dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 明年八月冒寧、錦功，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year, claiming credit for Ningxia and Jinzhou, he was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following August he claimed credit for the Ningxia and Jinzhou campaigns and was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 俄敘三殿功，加少傅，世蔭錦衣指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward credit for the three halls was tallied; he was made Junior Tutor and his heirs granted the post of Assistant Commander of the Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, for the three halls he was made Junior Tutor and his heirs ennobled as assistant commanders in the Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 其月遷兵部尚書，仍兼左都御史，並綰兩篆，握兵權憲紀，出入烜赫，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: That month he was transferred to Minister of War, still concurrently Left Censor-in-Chief; holding both seals, he grasped military authority and censorial discipline; his coming and going were brilliant, his power eclipsed court and country.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was made Minister of War while retaining the Left Censor-in-Chiefship; with both seals in hand he held military power and censorial sway—his comings and goings blazed with glory, and his influence overshadowed court and realm.

sentences.zh: 無何，熹宗崩，廷臣入臨。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Xizong died and court ministers came to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Tianqi Emperor died, and court ministers came to the palace to mourn.

sentences.zh: 內使十餘人傳呼崔尚書甚急，廷臣相顧愕眙。

translations.literal: More than ten inner eunuchs urgently called for Minister Cui; the ministers looked at one another in shock.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen palace eunuchs called urgently for Minister Cui; the court officials exchanged stunned glances.

sentences.zh: 呈秀入見忠賢，密謀久之，語秘不得聞。

translations.literal: Chengxiu entered to see Zhongxian and plotted in secret for a long time; their words were secret and could not be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chengxiu went in to see Wei Zhongxian; they plotted together in secret for a long while, and no one heard what was said.

sentences.zh: 或言忠賢欲篡位，呈秀以時未可，止之也。

translations.literal: Some say Zhongxian wished to usurp the throne, and Chengxiu stopped him because the time was not yet right.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Wei Zhongxian meant to seize the throne, and Cui Chengxiu dissuaded him—the moment was not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，其黨知忠賢必敗，內相攜。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor acceded, his faction knew Zhongxian would surely fall and began to turn on one another within.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor took the throne, the eunuch faction knew Wei Zhongxian was doomed and began to fracture among themselves.

sentences.zh: 副都御史楊所修首請允呈秀守制，御史楊維垣、賈繼春相繼力攻，呈秀乞罷。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Suoxiu was first to request allowing Chengxiu to observe mourning; censors Yang Weiyuan and Jia Jichun successively attacked with force; Chengxiu begged dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Suoxiu was first to ask that Cui Chengxiu be allowed to leave office and observe mourning; Censors Yang Weiyuan and Jia Jichun pressed the attack in turn, and Cui Chengxiu begged to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝猶慰留。

translations.literal: The Emperor still comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still sought to comfort him and keep him at post.

sentences.zh: 章三上，溫旨令乘傳歸。

translations.literal: After three memorials, a warm edict ordered him to return home by official relay.
translations.idiomatic: After three memorials, a gracious edict ordered him home by relay horse.

sentences.zh: 已而言者劾呈秀及工部尚書吳淳夫、兵部尚書田吉、太常卿倪文煥、副都御史李夔龍，號稱「五虎」，宜肆市朝。

translations.literal: Then remonstrators impeached Chengxiu and Minister of Works Wu Chunfu, Minister of War Tian Ji, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Ni Wenhuan, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Kuilong, called the "Five Tigers," saying they should be dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Then remonstrators impeached Cui Chengxiu together with Minister of Works Wu Chunfu, Minister of War Tian Ji, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Ni Wenhuan, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Kuilong—the "Five Tigers"—and demanded they be torn apart in the public square.

sentences.zh: 詔逮治，籍其貲。

translations.literal: An edict ordered their arrest and prosecution and confiscation of their assets.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered their arrest and the seizure of their estates.

sentences.zh: 時忠賢已死，呈秀知不免，列姬妾，羅諸奇異珍寶，呼酒痛飲，盡一卮即擲壞之，飲已自縊。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongxian was already dead; Chengxiu knew he could not escape; he lined up his concubines, spread out various wondrous treasures, called for wine and drank heavily; after each cup he smashed it; when finished drinking he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was already dead; knowing there was no escape, Cui Chengxiu gathered his concubines, laid out his strangest treasures, called for wine and drank deep—each emptied cup he hurled aside and smashed—and when the wine was done he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 詔戮其屍，子鐸除名，弟凝秀遣戍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his corpse dismembered; his son Duo was struck from the rolls; his brother Ningxiu was sent into frontier exile.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his corpse torn apart in punishment; his son Duo was struck from the rolls; his brother Ningxiu was banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後定逆案，以呈秀為首。

translations.literal: Later, when the treason cases were settled, Chengxiu was listed first.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Treason Case was finalized, Cui Chengxiu stood at its head.

sentences.zh: 吳淳夫 倪文煥 田吉 李夔龍

translations.literal: Wu Chunfu, Ni Wenhuan, Tian Ji, Li Kuilong
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chunfu, Ni Wenhuan, Tian Ji, Li Kuilong

sentences.zh: 淳夫，晉江人。

translations.literal: Chunfu was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chunfu was a native of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官陜西僉事，以京察罷。

translations.literal: He served as Intendant in Shaanxi and was dismissed in the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Intendant in Shaanxi and was dismissed in the capital review.

sentences.zh: 五年夤緣起兵部郎中，與文煥、吉、夔龍並由呈秀進，為忠賢義子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, through pull he rose to Bureau Director in the Ministry of War; together with Wenhuan, Ji, and Kuilong he was advanced through Chengxiu and became Zhongxian's adopted sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianqi he wheedled his way to Bureau Director in the Ministry of War; he and Wenhuan, Ji, and Kuilong all rose through Cui Chengxiu and became Wei Zhongxian's adopted sons.

sentences.zh: 大學士馮銓釋褐十三年登宰輔，為忠賢所匿。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Feng Quan entered office from the jinshi after thirteen years and reached the chancellor's seat, but was concealed by Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Feng Quan had reached the chancellor's seat only thirteen years after taking his jinshi degree, yet Wei Zhongxian kept him in the shadows.

sentences.zh: 呈秀妒之，淳夫即為攻銓。

translations.literal: Chengxiu was jealous of him, and Chunfu thereupon attacked Quan on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chengxiu envied him, and Wu Chunfu attacked Feng Quan at his bidding.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，擢太僕少卿，視職方事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and attended to Personnel Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and put in charge of Personnel Bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 旋擢太僕卿，歷工部添註右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Director of the Imperial Stud and served as additionally appointed Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Director of the Imperial Stud and then additionally appointed Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 冒寧、錦及三殿功，累進工部尚書，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: Claiming credit for Ningxia, Jinzhou, and the three halls, he was promoted in succession to Minister of Works and made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For the Ningxia and Jinzhou campaigns and the three halls he rose in succession to Minister of Works and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 歲中六遷，至極品。

translations.literal: Six promotions within a year, reaching the highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: Six promotions within a single year—he reached the highest ranks.

sentences.zh: 倪文煥，江都人。

translations.literal: Ni Wenhuan was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Wenhuan was a native of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 由進士授行人，擢御史，巡視南城。

translations.literal: From jinshi he was appointed courier; promoted to censor, he inspected the southern capital ward.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his jinshi he was appointed a courier, then promoted to censor and assigned to inspect the southern capital ward.

sentences.zh: 山東多大猾，事發則走匿京師。

translations.literal: Shandong had many great rascals; when matters were exposed they would flee and hide in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong swarmed with great scoundrels who, once exposed, fled to hide in the capital.

sentences.zh: 參政王維章數牒文煥，文煥納其賄，反劾罷維章。

translations.literal: Assistant Administrator Wang Weizhang repeatedly petitioned Wenhuan; Wenhuan accepted bribes and in turn impeached and dismissed Weizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Administrator Wang Weizhang repeatedly memorialized Ni Wenhuan, who took bribes and impeached Weizhang in return, removing him from office.

sentences.zh: 嘗誤撻皇城守卒，為中官所糾，大懼，走謁呈秀求救，遂引入忠賢幕，為鷹犬。

translations.literal: Once he mistakenly beat a guard of the Imperial City and was impeached by eunuchs; greatly afraid, he ran to Chengxiu to beg rescue and was thereby brought into Zhongxian's entourage as a hawk and hound.
translations.idiomatic: Once he wrongly flogged an Imperial City guard and was impeached by palace eunuchs; terrified, he ran to Cui Chengxiu for rescue and was brought into Wei Zhongxian's circle as a trained attack dog.

sentences.zh: 首劾兵部侍郎李邦華，御史李日宣，吏部員外郎周順昌、林枝橋。

translations.literal: He was first to impeach Vice Minister of War Li Banghua, Censor Li Rixuan, and Department Vice Directors Zhou Shunchang and Lin Zhiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was first to impeach Vice Minister of War Li Banghua, Censor Li Rixuan, and Department Vice Directors Zhou Shunchang and Lin Zhiqiao.

sentences.zh: 再劾戶部侍郎孫居相、御史夏之令及故吏部尚書崔景榮、吏部尚書李宗延等數十人。

translations.literal: He again impeached Vice Minister of Revenue Sun Juxiang, Censor Xia Zhiling, former Minister of Personnel Cui Jingrong, Minister of Personnel Li Zongyan, and several dozen others.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached again: Vice Minister of Revenue Sun Juxiang, Censor Xia Zhiling, former Minister of Personnel Cui Jingrong, Minister of Personnel Li Zongyan, and dozens more.

sentences.zh: 輕者削奪，重者拷死。

translations.literal: The lighter cases were stripped of honors; the heavier were tortured to death.
translations.idiomatic: Some lost their rank; others were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 呈秀首頌忠賢，文煥即繼之。

translations.literal: Chengxiu was first to praise Zhongxian, and Wenhuan immediately followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Chengxiu led the praise of Wei Zhongxian, Ni Wenhuan followed at once.

sentences.zh: 出按畿輔，為忠賢建三祠。

translations.literal: Going out to inspect the capital region, he built three shrines for Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection tour in the capital region he built three shrines to Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 河南道缺掌印官，呈秀為懸缺待文煥，至越十餘人任之。

translations.literal: When the Henan Circuit lacked its seal-bearing officer, Chengxiu left the post vacant waiting for Wenhuan; more than ten others held the post in the interim.
translations.idiomatic: When the Henan Circuit post of seal-bearing censor fell vacant, Cui Chengxiu kept it open for Ni Wenhuan; more than ten others served in the role before him.

sentences.zh: 冒寧、錦、殿功，加太僕卿，掌道如故。

translations.literal: Claiming credit for Ningxia, Jinzhou, and the hall construction, he was made Director of the Imperial Stud while still managing the circuit as before.
translations.idiomatic: For Ningxia, Jinzhou, and the hall construction he was made Director of the Imperial Stud, still holding his circuit duties.

sentences.zh: 尋改太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，文煥懼，乞終養歸。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell, Wenhuan was afraid and begged to return home for permanent mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian fell, Ni Wenhuan panicked and begged leave to retire and care for his parents until their death.

sentences.zh: 田吉者，故城人。

translations.literal: Tian Ji was a native of Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji was a native of Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十八年廷對懷挾，罰三科，以縣佐錄用。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Wanli, he was caught with hidden notes at the palace examination; penalized three sessions, he was employed as a county assistant.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year of Wanli he was caught smuggling notes into the palace examination; barred for three rounds, he was taken on as a county assistant.

sentences.zh: 已，補試，由知縣歷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Later he passed the supplementary examination and rose from magistrate to Bureau Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after passing the supplementary examination, he rose from magistrate to Bureau Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，遷淮揚參議，取中旨，擢太常少卿，視職方事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year he was transferred to Assistant Administration Commissioner of Huai-Yang; by secret edict he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and attended to Personnel Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year he became Assistant Administration Commissioner of Huai-Yang; by secret edict he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and put over Personnel Bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年擢太常卿。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 未匝歲，連擢至兵部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed, he was promoted in succession to Minister of War and made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than a year he rose in succession to Minister of War and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 諸逆黨超擢，未有如吉者。

translations.literal: Among the treason faction's extraordinary promotions, none matched Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Among the traitor faction's meteoric rises, none matched Tian Ji.

sentences.zh: 李夔龍，福建南安人。

translations.literal: Li Kuilong was a native of Nan'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuilong was a native of Nan'an, Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由進士歷吏部主事，被劾罷去。

translations.literal: From jinshi he served as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his jinshi he rose to principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel but was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年夤緣復官，進郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi, through pull he was restored to office and promoted to Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianqi he wheedled his way back into office and was promoted to Bureau Director.

sentences.zh: 專承呈秀指，引用邪人以媚忠賢。

translations.literal: He exclusively carried out Chengxiu's directives, recommending wicked men to please Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He did only as Cui Chengxiu directed, advancing corrupt men to curry favor with Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 擢太常少卿，仍署選事。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he still handled appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while still overseeing appointments.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左僉都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三殿成，進左副都御史。

translations.literal: When the three halls were completed, he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the three halls were completed he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，淳夫、文煥、吉、夔龍，並以上林典簿樊維城、戶部員外郎王守履言，逮治論死。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded, Chunfu, Wenhuan, Ji, and Kuilong, together with Chief of the Imperial Park Bureau Fan Weicheng and Department Vice Director Wang Shoulü, who had spoken out, were arrested and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded, Chunfu, Wenhuan, Ji, and Kuilong were arrested and sentenced to death, together with Imperial Park Bureau chief Fan Weicheng and Revenue Department Vice Director Wang Shoulü, who had memorialized against them.

sentences.zh: 欽定逆案

translations.literal: The Treason Case as Determined by Imperial Command
translations.idiomatic: The Treason Case as Determined by Imperial Command

sentences.zh: 方忠賢敗時，莊烈帝納廷臣言，將定從逆案。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian had just fallen, the Chongzhen Emperor accepted the court ministers' advice and was about to settle the cases of those who followed the traitors.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian had just fallen, the Chongzhen Emperor heeded the court and set out to settle the cases of those who had followed the traitors.

sentences.zh: 大學士韓爌、李標、錢龍錫不欲廣搜樹怨，僅以四五十人上。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Han Kuang, Li Biao, and Qian Longxi did not wish to search broadly and sow resentment; they submitted only forty or fifty names.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Han Kuang, Li Biao, and Qian Longxi did not wish to hunt widely and sow fresh grudges; they submitted only forty or fifty names.

sentences.zh: 帝少之，令再議，又以數十人上。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered it too few and ordered reconsideration; again they submitted several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought the list too short and ordered another deliberation; again they submitted only several dozen.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，令以贊導、擁戴、頌美、諂附為目，且曰：「內侍同惡者亦當入。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased and ordered categories of assistance, support, praise, and flattery, saying: "Palace attendants who shared in the evil should also be included.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and ordered them to sort the guilty by abetting, rallying, praising, and fawning—and said: "Palace attendants who shared their wickedness must be included as well.

sentences.zh: 爌等以不知內侍對，帝曰：「豈皆不知，特畏任怨耳。」

translations.literal: Kuang and the others replied that they did not know the palace attendants; the Emperor said: "How could you all not know? You simply fear taking on resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang and the others answered that they did not know the palace attendants; the emperor said: "You all know perfectly well—you simply fear the blame.

sentences.zh: 閱日，召入便殿，案有布囊，盛章疏甚夥，指之曰：「此皆奸黨頌疏，可案名悉入。」

translations.literal: The next day he summoned them to the side hall; on the desk was a cloth sack holding a great many memorials; pointing to it he said: "These are all eulogies from the traitor faction; you may list the names and include them all.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned them to the side hall. On the desk lay a cloth sack crammed with memorials. Pointing to it he said: "These are all eulogies from the traitor faction—take every name and include them.

sentences.zh: 爌等知帝意不可回，乃曰：「臣等職在調旨，三尺法非所習。」

translations.literal: Kuang and the others knew the Emperor's intent could not be turned back and said: "Our duty is to draft rescripts; we are not versed in the law.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor's mind could not be changed, Han Kuang and the others said: "Our duty is to draft rescripts; we are not versed in penal law.

sentences.zh: 帝召吏部尚書王永光問之，永光以不習刑名對，乃詔刑部尚書喬允升、左都御史曹於汴同事，於是案名羅列無脫遺者。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang and asked; Yongguang replied he was not versed in penal affairs; thereupon he ordered Minister of Justice Qiao Yunsheng and Left Censor-in-Chief Cao Yubian to work together, and then the names were listed with none omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang, who likewise pleaded ignorance of penal matters; he then ordered Minister of Justice Qiao Yunsheng and Left Censor-in-Chief Cao Yubian to compile the cases together—and every name was listed, none escaped.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年三月上之，帝為詔書頒示天下。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Chongzhen it was submitted; the Emperor issued an edict proclaiming it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Chongzhen it was submitted; the emperor issued a proclamation to the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 首逆淩遲者二人：魏忠賢，客氏。

translations.literal: Two chief traitors to be dismembered: Wei Zhongxian and Madame Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief traitors sentenced to dismemberment: Wei Zhongxian and Madame Ke.

sentences.zh: 首逆同謀決不待時者六人：呈秀及魏良卿，客氏子都督侯國興，太監李永貞、李朝欽、劉若愚。

translations.literal: Six chief traitor conspirators to be immediately executed: Chengxiu and Wei Liangqing, Madame Ke's son the commander Hou Guoxing, and eunuchs Li Yongzhen, Li Chaoqin, and Liu Ruoyu.
translations.idiomatic: Six chief conspirators to be executed at once without delay: Cui Chengxiu and Wei Liangqing; Madame Ke's son, Commander Hou Guoxing; and the eunuchs Li Yongzhen, Li Chaoqin, and Liu Ruoyu.

sentences.zh: 交結近侍秋後處決者十九人：劉志選、梁夢環、倪文煥、田吉、劉詔、薛貞、吳淳夫、李夔龍、曹欽程，大理寺正許誌吉，順天府通判孫如冽，國子監生陸萬齡，豐城侯李承祚，都督田爾耕、許顯純、崔應元、楊寰、孫雲鶴、張體乾。

translations.literal: Nineteen who consorted with close attendants to be executed after autumn: Liu Zhixuan, Liang Menghuan, Ni Wenhuan, Tian Ji, Liu Zhao, Xue Zhen, Wu Chunfu, Li Kuilong, Cao Qincheng, Court of Judicial Review Director Xu Zhiji, Shuntian Prefecture Vice Prefect Sun Rulie, National University student Lu Wanling, Marquis of Fengcheng Li Chengzuo, and commanders Tian Ergeng, Xu Xianchun, Cui Yingyuan, Yang Huan, Sun Yunhe, and Zhang Tigan.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen who consorted with palace favorites, to be executed after autumn: Liu Zhixuan, Liang Menghuan, Ni Wenhuan, Tian Ji, Liu Zhao, Xue Zhen, Wu Chunfu, Li Kuilong, Cao Qincheng; Court of Judicial Review Director Xu Zhiji; Shuntian Vice Prefect Sun Rulie; National University student Lu Wanling; Marquis of Fengcheng Li Chengzuo; and Commanders Tian Ergeng, Xu Xianchun, Cui Yingyuan, Yang Huan, Sun Yunhe, and Zhang Tigan.

sentences.zh: 結交近侍次等充軍者十一人：魏廣微、周應秋、閻鳴泰、霍維華、徐大化、潘汝禎、李魯生、楊維垣、張訥，都督郭欽，孝陵衛指揮李之才。

translations.literal: Eleven who consorted with close attendants at the next rank to be sent into military exile: Wei Guangwei, Zhou Yingqiu, Yan Mingtai, Huo Weihua, Xu Dahua, Pan Ruzhen, Li Lusheng, Yang Weiyuan, Zhang Ne, Commander Guo Qin, and Xiaoling Guard Commander Li Zhicai.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven who consorted with palace favorites at the next rank, sentenced to military exile: Wei Guangwei, Zhou Yingqiu, Yan Mingtai, Huo Weihua, Xu Dahua, Pan Ruzhen, Li Lusheng, Yang Weiyuan, Zhang Ne, Commander Guo Qin, and Xiaoling Guard Commander Li Zhicai.

sentences.zh: 交結近侍又次等論徒三年輸贖為民者：大學士顧秉謙、馮銓、張瑞圖、來宗道，尚書王紹徽、郭允厚、張我續、曹爾禎、孟紹虞、馮嘉會、李春曄、邵輔忠、呂純如、徐兆魁、薛風翔、孫傑、楊夢袞、李養德、劉廷元、曹思誠，南京尚書範濟世、張樸，總督尚書黃運泰、郭尚友、李從心，巡撫尚書李精白等一百二十九人。

translations.literal: Those who consorted with close attendants at the rank below that, sentenced to three years' banishment commutable by ransom to commoner status: Grand Secretaries Gu Bingqian, Feng Quan, Zhang Ruitu, and Lai Zongdao; Ministers Wang Shaohui, Guo Yunhou, Zhang Woxu, Cao Erzhen, Meng Shaoyu, Feng Jiahui, Li Chunye, Shao Fuzhong, Lü Chunru, Xu Zhaokui, Xue Fengxiang, Sun Jie, Yang Menggun, Li Yangde, Liu Tingyuan, and Cao Sicheng; Nanjing Ministers Fan Jishi and Zhang Pu; Grand Coordinators Huang Yuntai, Guo Shangyou, and Li Congxin; Grand Secretary-Inspectors Li Jingbai, and one hundred twenty-nine others.
translations.idiomatic: Those who consorted with palace favorites at the rank below that, sentenced to three years' banishment commutable by ransom to commoner status: Grand Secretaries Gu Bingqian, Feng Quan, Zhang Ruitu, and Lai Zongdao; Ministers Wang Shaohui, Guo Yunhou, Zhang Woxu, Cao Erzhen, Meng Shaoyu, Feng Jiahui, Li Chunye, Shao Fuzhong, Lü Chunru, Xu Zhaokui, Xue Fengxiang, Sun Jie, Yang Menggun, Li Yangde, Liu Tingyuan, and Cao Sicheng; Nanjing Ministers Fan Jishi and Zhang Pu; Grand Coordinators Huang Yuntai, Guo Shangyou, and Li Congxin; Grand Secretary-Inspectors Li Jingbai; and one hundred twenty-nine others.

sentences.zh: 交結近侍減等革職閑住者，黃立極等四十四人。

translations.literal: Those who consorted with close attendants, reduced one grade and stripped of office to live in retirement: Huang Liji and forty-four others.
translations.idiomatic: Those who consorted with palace favorites, reduced one grade and stripped of office to live in retirement: Huang Liji and forty-four others.

sentences.zh: 忠賢親屬及內官黨附者又五十餘人。

translations.literal: Zhongxian's relatives and palace eunuch adherents numbered more than fifty others.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's kin and palace eunuch adherents numbered more than fifty besides.

sentences.zh: 案既定，其黨日謀更翻，王永光、溫體仁陰主之，帝持之堅，不能動。

translations.literal: Once the case was settled, his faction daily plotted to overturn it; Wang Yongguang and Wen Tiren secretly led this, but the Emperor held firm and they could not move him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the case was settled, the faction plotted daily to overturn it; Wang Yongguang and Wen Tiren led the effort in secret, but the emperor held firm and they could not budge him.

sentences.zh: 其後，張捷薦呂純如，被劾去。

translations.literal: Later, Zhang Jie recommended Lü Chunru and was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Jie recommended Lü Chunru and was impeached out of office.

sentences.zh: 唐世濟薦霍維華，福建巡按應喜臣薦部內閑住通政使周維京，罪至謫戍。

translations.literal: Tang Shiji recommended Huo Weihua; Fujian surveillance commissioner Ying Xichen recommended the idle Transmission Commissioner Zhou Weijing within his jurisdiction; the offense reached banishment to frontier service.
