translations.idiomatic: Tang Shiji recommended Huo Weihua; Fujian surveillance commissioner Ying Xichen recommended the idle Transmission Commissioner Zhou Weijing within his jurisdiction—and the offense earned them banishment to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其黨乃不敢言。

translations.literal: His faction then did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: The faction then dared not speak out.

sentences.zh: 福王時，阮大鋮冒定策功，起用，其案始翻。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, Ruan Dacheng falsely claimed credit for settling the succession and was restored to office; only then did the case begin to be overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Ruan Dacheng falsely claimed credit for settling the succession and was restored to office—and only then did the case begin to be overturned.

sentences.zh: 於是太僕少卿楊維垣、徐景濂，給事中虞廷陛、郭如暗，御史周昌晉、陳以瑞、徐復陽，編修吳孔嘉，參政虞大復輩相繼而起，國亡乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Yang Weiyuan and Xu Jinglian, Supervising Secretaries Yu Tingbi and Guo Ru'an, Censors Zhou Changjin, Chen Yirui, and Xu Fuyang, Compiler Wu Kongjia, and Administration Commissioner Yu Dafu and their kind rose in succession; only with the fall of the state did this cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Yang Weiyuan and Xu Jinglian, Supervising Secretaries Yu Tingbi and Guo Ru'an, Censors Zhou Changjin, Chen Yirui, and Xu Fuyang, Compiler Wu Kongjia, Administration Commissioner Yu Dafu, and their kind rose in succession—only the fall of the dynasty put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 劉志選

translations.literal: Liu Zhixuan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhixuan

sentences.zh: 劉志選，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhixuan was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhixuan was a native of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，與葉向高同舉進士。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he received the jinshi degree together with Ye Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he received the jinshi degree in the same year as Ye Xianggao.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，偕同官劉復初、李懋檜爭鄭貴妃、王恭妃冊封事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Justice and, together with colleagues Liu Fuchu and Li Maogui, contested the investiture of Noble Consort Zheng and Consort Wang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and, with colleagues Liu Fuchu and Li Maogui, joined the fight over the investiture of Noble Consort Zheng and Consort Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 後懋檜因給事中邵庶請禁諸曹言事，抗疏力爭，貶二秩。

translations.literal: Later Maogui, because Supervising Secretary Shao Shu petitioned to forbid the various offices from memorializing on affairs, submitted a defiant memorial arguing forcefully and was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Supervising Secretary Shao Shu petitioned to silence memorials from the various offices, Li Maogui submitted a bold counter-memorial and was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 志選言：「陛下謫懋檜，使人箝口結舌，蒙蔽耳目，非國家福也。」

translations.literal: Zhixuan said: "Your Majesty's demotion of Maogui makes men clamp mouths and tie tongues, blind ears and eyes—this is no blessing to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhixuan said, "Your Majesty's punishment of Maogui silences men's tongues and blinds their ears and eyes—this can bring the state no good."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫福寧州判官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted him to Assistant Magistrate of Funing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Funing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 稍遷合肥知縣，以大計罷歸，家居三十年。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to magistrate of Hefei; dismissed and sent home in the triennial evaluation, and lived at home for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to magistrate of Hefei, then dismissed in the triennial evaluation and sent home, where he lived in retirement for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 光宗、熹宗相繼立，諸建言得罪者盡起，志選獨以計典不獲與。

translations.literal: When Guangzong and Xizong succeeded to the throne in turn, all who had offended through memorializing were restored; Zhixuan alone failed to be included because of the evaluation record.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangzong and Xizong emperors succeeded in turn, every official punished for outspoken memorials was restored—Liu Zhixuan alone was passed over because of his evaluation record.

sentences.zh: 會向高赴召，道杭州，志選與遊宴彌月。

translations.literal: It happened that Xianggao was summoned on his way and passed through Hangzhou; Zhixuan feasted and toured with him for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye Xianggao was summoned to court and passed through Hangzhou, Liu Zhixuan joined him in feasting and sightseeing for a full month.

sentences.zh: 還朝，用為南京工部主事，進郎中，時已七十餘，嗜進彌銳，上疏追論「紅丸」，極詆孫慎行不道。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was appointed Principal Clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and promoted to Bureau Director; he was already over seventy, yet his craving for advancement grew ever sharper; he memorialized revisiting the "Red Pill" case and bitterly denounced Sun Shenxing as immoral.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made a principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and promoted to bureau director. Though already past seventy, his hunger for office grew keener still; he memorialized to reopen the Red Pill affair and savagely denounced Sun Shenxing as a man of no principle.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢喜，天啟五年九月召為尚寶少卿。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian was pleased; in the ninth month of Tianqi 5 he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was delighted, and in the ninth month of Tianqi 5 Liu Zhixuan was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Treasures.

sentences.zh: 在道，復力攻慎行，遂並及向高。

translations.literal: On the road he again attacked Shenxing forcefully, and thereby implicated Xianggao as well.
translations.idiomatic: While still on the road he renewed his assault on Sun Shenxing and extended the attack to Ye Xianggao as well.

sentences.zh: 忠賢益喜，出兩疏宣史館。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was all the more pleased and had both memorials published at the Historiographical Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was still more pleased and had both memorials circulated through the Historiographical Institute.

sentences.zh: 明年擢順天府丞。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Assistant Prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to assistant prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 冬十月遂上疏劾張國紀。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he submitted a memorial impeaching Zhang Guoji.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he submitted a memorial impeaching Zhang Guoji.

sentences.zh: 國紀者，後父也。

translations.literal: Guoji was the empress's father.
translations.idiomatic: Guoji was the empress's father.

sentences.zh: 忠賢忌後賢明，欲傾之。

translations.literal: Zhongxian envied the empress's wisdom and wished to topple her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian resented the empress's intelligence and wished to bring her down.

sentences.zh: 會有張匿名榜於厚載門者，列忠賢反狀，並其黨七十餘人。

translations.literal: It happened that an anonymous placard was posted at Houzai Gate listing Zhongxian's treasonous acts and naming more than seventy of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: An anonymous placard appeared at Houzai Gate listing Zhongxian's acts of treason and naming more than seventy of his followers.

sentences.zh: 忠賢疑出國紀及被逐諸人手。

translations.literal: Zhongxian suspected it came from Guoji and those who had been expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian suspected that Guoji and the men he had driven out were behind it.

sentences.zh: 邵輔忠、孫傑謀因此興大獄，盡殺東林諸人，而借國紀以搖中宮，事成則立魏良卿女為後，草一疏，募人上之。

translations.literal: Shao Fuzhong and Sun Jie plotted to use this to launch a major prosecution, kill all the Donglin men, and by means of Guoji shake the inner palace; once done they would install Wei Liangqing's daughter as empress; they drafted a memorial and recruited someone to submit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Fuzhong and Sun Jie plotted to use the incident to launch a great purge, wipe out the Donglin faction, and through Guoji shake the inner palace; if the plan succeeded they would install Wei Liangqing's daughter as empress. They drafted a memorial and sought someone to submit it.

sentences.zh: 諸人慮禍不敢承。

translations.literal: The others feared calamity and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The others feared the consequences and dared not take it on.

sentences.zh: 志選惑家人言，謂己老必先忠賢死，竟上之。

translations.literal: Zhixuan was misled by his family's words, thinking that because he was old he would certainly die before Zhongxian, and in the end submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhixuan, swayed by his family's counsel that he was old and would surely die before Zhongxian, submitted the memorial in the end.

sentences.zh: 極論國紀罪，而末言「毋令人訾及丹山之穴，藍田之種。」

translations.literal: He argued at length Guoji's crimes, and at the end said: "Let no one cast aspersions upon the cave of Dan Mountain or the seed of Lantian."
translations.idiomatic: He laid out Guoji's crimes at length and ended by saying, "Let no one speak ill of the cave of Dan Mountain or the seed of Lantian."

sentences.zh: 蓋前有死囚孫二言張後己所生，非國紀女也。

translations.literal: For previously there was a condemned man Sun Er who said the Zhang empress was born to someone else and was not Guoji's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: For a condemned man named Sun Er had earlier claimed that the Zhang empress was born to another and was not Guoji's daughter.

sentences.zh: 疏上，事叵測。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the affair was unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial reached the throne, the outcome was impossible to foretell.

sentences.zh: 帝伉儷情篤，但令國紀自新而已。

translations.literal: The emperor's affection for his consort was deep; he merely ordered Guoji to reform himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's devotion to his consort ran deep; he merely ordered Guoji to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 後為故司禮劉克敬所選，忠賢遷怒克敬，謫發鳳陽，縊殺之。

translations.literal: Later she had been chosen by the former Director of Ceremonial Liu Kejing; Zhongxian redirected his anger at Kejing, banished him to Fengyang, and had him strangled.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had been chosen through the former Director of Ceremonial Liu Kejing; Zhongxian turned his rage on Kejing, banished him to Fengyang, and had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，志選疏頌《要典》，言：「命德討罪，無微不彰，即堯、舜之放四兇，舉元、愷，何以加焉，洵遊、夏無能贊一詞者。」

translations.literal: Before long Zhixuan submitted a memorial praising The Essential Records, saying: "By command and virtue crimes were judged, nothing small left unrevealed—even Yao and Shun's banishment of the Four Evils and elevation of Yuan and Kai could add nothing; truly Ziyou and Xia could not offer a single word of praise."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Zhixuan submitted a memorial praising 《The Essential Records》, writing, "By imperial command and moral authority crimes were judged and no detail left hidden—even Yao and Shun's banishment of the Four Evils and elevation of Yuan and Kai could add nothing; truly even Ziyou and Xia could not have found a word of praise."

sentences.zh: 因力詆王之寀、孫慎行、楊漣、左光鬥，而極譽劉廷元、嶽駿聲、黃克纘、徐景濂、範濟世、賈繼春並及傅櫆、陳九疇。

translations.literal: He thereupon bitterly denounced Wang Zhicai, Sun Shenxing, Yang Lian, and Zuo Guangdou, while extravagantly praising Liu Tingyuan, Yue Junsheng, Huang Kezuan, Xu Jinglian, Fan Jishi, Jia Jichun, and also Fu Yi and Chen Jiuchou.
translations.idiomatic: He then savaged Wang Zhicai, Sun Shenxing, Yang Lian, and Zuo Guangdou while heaping praise on Liu Tingyuan, Yue Junsheng, Huang Kezuan, Xu Jinglian, Fan Jishi, Jia Jichun, Fu Yi, and Chen Jiuchou.

sentences.zh: 且言：「慷慨憂時，力障狂瀾於既倒者，魏廣微也，當還之揆席，以繼五臣之盛事。

translations.literal: He also said: "The man who generously grieved for the times and with all his strength held back the raging torrent already overturned is Wei Guangwei; he should be returned to the chancellor's seat to continue the grand enterprise of the Five Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "The man who grieved for the age and with all his strength held back the tide already turned is Wei Guangwei; he should be restored to the chancellor's seat to carry on the glory of the Five Worthies.

sentences.zh: 赤忠報國，弼成巨典於不日者，廠臣也，當增入簡端，以揚一德之休風。」

translations.literal: The man of red loyalty serving the state, who assisted in completing the great canon in no time, is the Depot Director; he should be added to the front of the imperial documents to proclaim the fine wind of unified virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The man whose loyal heart served the state and helped bring the great canon to completion in no time is the Depot Director; he should be named at the head of imperial documents to proclaim the virtue of unified rule."

sentences.zh: 又言：「之寀宜正典刑，慎行宜加謫戍。」

translations.literal: He further said: "Zhicai should receive proper capital punishment; Shenxing should be further demoted and sent to garrison duty."
translations.idiomatic: He further demanded that Wang Zhicai receive the full penalty of law and that Sun Shenxing be further demoted and sent to frontier garrison duty."

sentences.zh: 忠賢大悅，於是駿聲等超擢，之寀被逮，慎行遣戍，悉如志選言。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly pleased; thereupon Junsheng and others were promoted out of turn, Zhicai was arrested, Shenxing was sent to garrison exile—all exactly as Zhixuan said.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was overjoyed. Yue Junsheng and the others were promoted out of turn, Wang Zhicai was arrested, and Sun Shenxing was sent into exile—all exactly as Liu Zhixuan had asked.

sentences.zh: 七年擢右僉都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of Yangtze defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and placed in command of Yangtze defense.

sentences.zh: 其年，熹宗崩，忠賢敗，言官交劾，詔削籍。

translations.literal: That year Xizong died, Zhongxian fell, censorial officials impeached him in succession, and an edict struck him from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Xizong Emperor died, Zhongxian fell from power, censorial officials impeached Liu Zhixuan in a body, and an edict struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 後定逆案，律無傾搖國母文，坐子罵母律，與梁夢環並論死。

translations.literal: Later when the Treason Case was settled, the law had no provision for undermining the text regarding the State Mother; he was sentenced under the statute for a son reviling his mother, and together with Liang Menghuan was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Treason Case was later settled, the code contained no statute for undermining the empress dowager's honor; he was sentenced under the law against a son reviling his mother and, together with Liang Menghuan, condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 志選先自經。

translations.literal: Zhixuan hanged himself first.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhixuan hanged himself before the sentence could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 梁夢環 劉詔 邵輔忠 孫傑

translations.literal: Liang Menghuan, Liu Zhao, Shao Fuzhong, Sun Jie
translations.idiomatic: Liang Menghuan, Liu Zhao, Shao Fuzhong, Sun Jie

sentences.zh: 夢環，廣東順德人。

translations.literal: Menghuan was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Menghuan was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歷官御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through service as a censor.

sentences.zh: 父事忠賢，興汪文言獄，殺楊漣等。

translations.literal: He served Zhongxian as a father; he launched the Wang Wenyin case and killed Yang Lian and others.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Zhongxian as a father; he engineered the Wang Wenyin prosecution and helped bring about the deaths of Yang Lian and others.

sentences.zh: 出巡山海關，會寧遠敘功，崔呈秀不獲與，夢環力敘其賢勞，遂進侍郎。

translations.literal: On an inspection tour beyond Shanhaiguan, when Ningyuan achievements were being tallied and Cui Chengxiu was not included, Menghuan forcefully recounted Chengxiu's merits and labors, and Chengxiu was promoted to Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: While on inspection beyond Shanhaiguan, when honors for Ningyuan were being distributed and Cui Chengxiu was left out, Menghuan forcefully argued for Chengxiu's merit and service, and Chengxiu was promoted to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 劾熊廷弼乾沒軍資十七萬，廷弼已死，家益破。

translations.literal: He impeached Xiong Tingbi for embezzling 170,000 [taels of] military funds; Tingbi was already dead, and his household was ruined all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Xiong Tingbi for embezzling 170,000 taels of military funds; Tingbi was already dead, and his family was ruined still further.

sentences.zh: 志選之劾國紀也，忠賢意未逞。

translations.literal: When Zhixuan impeached Guoji, Zhongxian's intent had not been satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhixuan impeached Guoji, Zhongxian's purpose had not yet been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 夢環偵知之，七年二月馳疏極論國紀罪，且故詰「丹山、藍田」二語，冀傾後。

translations.literal: Menghuan learned of it; in the second month of the seventh year he hurriedly submitted a memorial arguing at length Guoji's crimes, and deliberately pressed the two phrases "Dan Mountain" and "Lantian," hoping to topple the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Menghuan learned of the affair and, in the second month of the seventh year, hurried in a memorial denouncing Guoji at length and deliberately pressing the phrases "Dan Mountain" and "Lantian," hoping to bring down the empress.

sentences.zh: 顧事重，忠賢亦不能驟行，而國紀竟勒還籍。

translations.literal: But the affair was weighty; Zhongxian likewise could not act abruptly, and yet Guoji was ultimately compelled to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was too grave for Zhongxian to move at once, yet Guoji was ultimately forced to return to his native place.

sentences.zh: 夢環建祠祀忠賢，三疏頌功德。

translations.literal: Menghuan built a shrine to worship Zhongxian and submitted three memorials extolling his merits and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Menghuan built a shrine to honor Zhongxian and submitted three memorials praising his merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 寧、錦之役，復稱忠賢「德被四方，勛高百代」，於是有安平之封，夢環擢太僕卿。

translations.literal: In the Ning and Jin campaigns he again praised Zhongxian as "virtue covering the four quarters, merit towering over a hundred generations"; thereupon came the enfeoffment as Duke of Anping, and Menghuan was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ningyuan and Jinzhou campaigns he again hailed Zhongxian as one "whose virtue covered the four quarters and whose merit towered over a hundred generations"; there followed the enfeoffment as Duke of Anping, and Menghuan was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 又劉詔者，杞縣人。

translations.literal: There was also Liu Zhao, a native of Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Liu Zhao, a native of Qixian.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十七年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-seventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授盧龍知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年超擢山東僉事。

translations.literal: In Tianqi 2 he was promoted out of turn to Administration Vice Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he was promoted out of turn to administration vice commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 七年代閻鳴泰總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he replaced Yan Mingtai as Grand Coordinator of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he replaced Yan Mingtai as grand coordinator of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Minister of War and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Minister of War and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 詔嗜利無恥，父事忠賢。

translations.literal: Zhao was greedy and shameless, serving Zhongxian as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao was greedy and without shame, treating Zhongxian as a father.

sentences.zh: 釋褐九年，驟至極品。

translations.literal: Nine years from first appointment to highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: Only nine years passed from his first appointment to the highest rank.

sentences.zh: 建四祠祀忠賢。

translations.literal: He built four shrines to worship Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He built four shrines to honor Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，僅罷官聽勘。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell he was merely dismissed pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian fell, Liu Zhao was merely dismissed pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 御史高弘圖言：「傾危社稷，搖動宮闈，如詔及劉志選、梁夢環三賊者，罪實浮於『五虎』『五彪』，而天討未加。

translations.literal: Censor Gao Hongtu said: "Those who undermined the altars of state and shook the inner palace—such villains as Zhao, Liu Zhixuan, and Liang Menghuan—their guilt in fact exceeds that of the 'Five Tigers' and 'Five Leopards,' yet Heaven's punishment has not been applied.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gao Hongtu said, "Men who endangered the altars of state and shook the inner palace—villains such as Liu Zhao, Liu Zhixuan, and Liang Menghuan—are in truth guiltier than the Five Tigers and Five Leopards, yet Heaven's judgment has not fallen on them.

sentences.zh: 且詔建祠薊州，迎忠賢像，五拜三稽首，呼九千歲。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhao built a shrine at Jizhou, welcomed Zhongxian's image, performed five bows and three kowtows, and cried 'Nine thousand years.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Liu Zhao built a shrine at Jizhou, welcomed Zhongxian's image, performed five bows and three kowtows, and cried, "Nine thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 及聞先帝彌留，詔即整兵三千，易置將領，用崔呈秀所親蕭惟中主郵騎，直接都門，此其意何為。」

translations.literal: And upon hearing the late emperor was dying, Zhao immediately assembled three thousand troops, replaced the commanders, and put Cui Chengxiu's protégé Xiao Weizhong in charge of the courier relays straight to the capital gates—what was his intent?"
translations.idiomatic: And when he heard that the late emperor lay dying, Liu Zhao at once assembled three thousand troops, replaced the commanders, and put Cui Chengxiu's protégé Xiao Weizhong in charge of the courier relays leading straight to the capital gates—what did he intend by this?"

sentences.zh: 由是三人皆被逮，論死。

translations.literal: Thereupon all three were arrested and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: On this account all three were arrested and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 邵輔忠，定海人。

translations.literal: Shao Fuzhong was a native of Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Fuzhong was a native of Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the twenty-third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 為工部郎中，首劾李三才貪險假橫四大罪。

translations.literal: As a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works he was first to impeach Li Sancai on four counts: greed, treachery, hypocrisy, and tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: As a bureau director in the Ministry of Works he was the first to impeach Li Sancai on four counts—greed, treachery, hypocrisy, and tyranny.

sentences.zh: 尋謝病去，久之起故官。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned citing illness; after a long while he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned citing illness; after a long interval he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年附忠賢，驟遷至兵部尚書，視侍郎事。

translations.literal: In Tianqi 5 he attached himself to Zhongxian and was suddenly promoted to Minister of War, handling Vice Minister duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 5 he attached himself to Zhongxian and was suddenly promoted to Minister of War, performing the duties of a vice minister.

sentences.zh: 諸奸黨攻擊正人，多其所主使。

translations.literal: Attacks on upright men by the various wicked faction members were largely at his instigation.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the faction's assaults on upright officials were instigated by him.

sentences.zh: 七年三月護桂王之藩衡州，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year he escorted the Prince of Gui to his fief at Hengzhou and was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he escorted the Prince of Gui to his fief at Hengzhou and was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 還朝，時事已變，移疾歸。

translations.literal: Returning to court, the times had already changed; he pleaded illness and went home.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court the political tide had already turned; he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 尋麗逆案，贖徒為民。

translations.literal: Soon he was named in the Treason Case, sentenced to banishment commutable to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named in the Treason Case and sentenced to banishment commutable to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 孫傑，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Sun Jie was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jie was a native of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 官刑科右給事中，以附忠賢劾劉一燝、周嘉謨，為清議所棄。

translations.literal: He served as Right Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; for attaching himself to Zhongxian and impeaching Liu Yihuan and Zhou Jiamo he was abandoned by pure opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Right Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; for siding with Zhongxian and impeaching Liu Yihuan and Zhou Jiamo he was cast out by respectable opinion.

sentences.zh: 出為江西參議，引疾歸。

translations.literal: He went out as Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi and cited illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as administration commissioner of Jiangxi and cited illness to return home.

sentences.zh: 忠賢召為大理丞，累擢工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhongxian summoned him as Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and promoted him cumulatively to Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian summoned him back as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and promoted him step by step to Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 大學士馮銓由李魯生、李蕃擁戴為首輔，素與崔呈秀璫。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Feng Quan, ushered into chief ministership by Li Lusheng and Li Fan, had long been connected with Cui Chengxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Feng Quan, installed as chief minister by Li Lusheng and Li Fan, had long been allied with Cui Chengxiu.

sentences.zh: 而傑與霍維華以呈秀最得忠賢歡，欲令入閣，謀之吳淳夫等，先擊去銓。

translations.literal: But Jie and Huo Weihua, because Chengxiu most won Zhongxian's favor, wished to have him enter the Grand Secretariat; they conspired with Wu Chunfu and others, first striking to remove Quan.
translations.idiomatic: But Sun Jie and Huo Weihua, seeing that Chengxiu enjoyed Zhongxian's favor above all others, wished to put him in the Grand Secretariat; they conspired with Wu Chunfu and others to strike first at Feng Quan.

sentences.zh: 又恐王紹徽為吏部，不肯推呈秀，令袁鯨疏攻紹徽，而龔萃肅上閣臣內外兼用疏以堅之。

translations.literal: They also feared that with Wang Shaohui as Minister of Personnel he would not recommend Chengxiu; they had Yuan Jing submit a memorial attacking Shaohui, while Gong Cuisu submitted a memorial on using inner and outer ministers together to strengthen the plan.
translations.idiomatic: They also feared that Wang Shaohui, as Minister of Personnel, would not recommend Chengxiu; they had Yuan Jing submit a memorial attacking Shaohui, while Gong Cuisu submitted a memorial urging that inner and outer ministers be used together to fix the plan.

sentences.zh: 自是，魯生、蕃與傑等分途，其黨日相輒矣。

translations.literal: From this Lusheng, Fan, and Jie and the others split paths, and their faction daily turned against one another.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Li Lusheng, Li Fan, Sun Jie, and the rest went their separate ways, and the faction daily turned on itself.

sentences.zh: 傑官亦至尚書，加少保。

translations.literal: Jie's office also reached Minister, with the additional title Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jie's rank also rose to minister, with the additional title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 忠賢誅，傑被劾罷，名麗逆案，贖徒三年。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian was executed Jie was impeached and dismissed, was named in the Treason Case, and was sentenced to three years' banishment commutable to ransom.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian was executed Sun Jie was impeached and dismissed, named in the Treason Case, and sentenced to three years' banishment commutable by ransom.

sentences.zh: 輔忠、傑本謀搖中宮，而事發於志選、夢環，故得輕論云。

translations.literal: Fuzhong and Jie had originally plotted to shake the inner palace, but since the affair erupted through Zhixuan and Menghuan they received lighter sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Fuzhong and Sun Jie had originally plotted to shake the inner palace, but because the affair broke through Liu Zhixuan and Liang Menghuan they received lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 曹欽程

translations.literal: Cao Qincheng
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qincheng

sentences.zh: 曹欽程，江西德化人。

translations.literal: Cao Qincheng was a native of Dehua in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qincheng was a native of Dehua in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授吳江知縣，贓汙狼籍，以淫刑博強項聲。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Wujiang; corruption was rampant; he won a reputation for toughness through cruel punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Wujiang, he plundered without restraint and built a reputation for ruthlessness through cruel punishments.

sentences.zh: 巡撫周起元劾之，貶秩，改順天教授，調國子助教。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhou Qiyuan impeached him; he was demoted in rank, changed to Instructor in Shuntian, and transferred to Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhou Qiyuan impeached him; he was demoted, reassigned as an instructor in Shuntian, and transferred to assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 諂附汪文言，得為工部主事。

translations.literal: He fawned upon Wang Wenyin and obtained the post of Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He fawned on Wang Wenyin and won appointment as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 及文言敗，欽程力擠之，由座主馮銓父事魏忠賢，為「十狗」之一。

translations.literal: When Wenyin fell, Qincheng forcefully pushed him out; through his patron-examiner Feng Quan he served Wei Zhongxian as a father and became one of the "Ten Dogs."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wenyin fell, Qincheng turned on him and drove him out; through his patron-examiner Feng Quan he treated Wei Zhongxian as a father and became one of the Ten Dogs.

sentences.zh: 銓欲害御史張慎言、周宗建，令李魯生草疏，屬欽程上之，因及李應升、黃尊素，而薦魯生及傅櫆、陳九疇、張訥、李蕃、李恒茂、梁夢環輩十餘人。

translations.literal: Quan wished to harm Censors Zhang Shenyan and Zhou Zongjian; he had Li Lusheng draft a memorial and entrusted Qincheng to submit it, thereby implicating Li Yingsheng and Huang Zunsu while recommending Lusheng and more than ten others including Fu Yi, Chen Jiuchou, Zhang Ne, Li Fan, Li Hengmao, and Liang Menghuan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan wished to destroy Censors Zhang Shenyan and Zhou Zongjian; he had Li Lusheng draft a memorial and entrusted Qincheng to submit it, thereby implicating Li Yingsheng and Huang Zunsu while recommending Li Lusheng and more than ten others, including Fu Yi, Chen Jiuchou, Zhang Ne, Li Fan, Li Hengmao, and Liang Menghuan.

sentences.zh: 慎言等四人並削籍。

translations.literal: Shenyan and the other three were all struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shenyan and the other three were all struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 欽程於群小中尤無恥，日夜走忠賢門，卑諂無所不至，同類頗羞稱之。

translations.literal: Among the petty men Qincheng was especially shameless; day and night he ran to Zhongxian's gate, fawning and groveling without limit; his fellows were quite ashamed to acknowledge him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the petty men Cao Qincheng was the most shameless; day and night he ran to Zhongxian's gate, groveling without limit, and even his fellows were ashamed to claim him.

sentences.zh: 欽程顧驕眾人以忠賢親己。

translations.literal: Qincheng however was proud before the crowd because Zhongxian favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qincheng swaggered before others because Zhongxian favored him.

sentences.zh: 給事中吳國華劾之，忠賢怒，除國華名，欽程益得誌。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wu Guohua impeached him; Zhongxian was angry and struck Wu Guohua from the rolls; Qincheng was all the more satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Secretary Wu Guohua impeached him, Zhongxian flew into a rage and struck Wu Guohua from the rolls; Qincheng was more pleased than ever.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊所修緣忠賢指，力薦其賢，遂由員外郎擢太僕少卿。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yang Suoxiu, at Zhongxian's direction, vigorously recommended his worth and he was thereupon promoted from Bureau Vice Director to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yang Suoxiu, acting on Zhongxian's orders, vigorously praised his talent, and Qincheng was promoted from bureau vice director to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 後忠賢亦厭之，六年正月為給事中潘士聞所劾。

translations.literal: Later Zhongxian also grew weary of him; in the first month of the sixth year he was impeached by Supervising Secretary Pan Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhongxian grew weary of him as well; in the first month of the sixth year he was impeached by Supervising Secretary Pan Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 忠賢責以敗群，削其籍。

translations.literal: Zhongxian rebuked him for ruining the faction and struck him from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian rebuked him for wrecking the faction and struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 瀕行猶頓首忠賢前曰：「君臣之義已絕，父子之恩難忘。」

translations.literal: On the verge of leaving he still kowtowed before Zhongxian and said: "The bond between monarch and minister is ended; the debt between father and son is hard to forget."
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave he still kowtowed before Zhongxian and said, "The bond between monarch and minister is ended, but the debt between father and son is hard to forget."

sentences.zh: 絮泣而去。

translations.literal: He went away weeping and babbling.
translations.idiomatic: He went away weeping and muttering.

sentences.zh: 忠賢誅，入逆案首等，論死。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian was executed he was placed in the first rank of the Treason Case and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian was executed Cao Qincheng was placed in the first rank of the Treason Case and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 系獄久之，家人不復饋食，欽程掠他囚餘食，日醉飽。

translations.literal: Imprisoned long, his family no longer brought food; Qincheng seized other prisoners' leftover food and each day drank and ate his fill.
translations.idiomatic: Held in prison for a long while, he received no more food from his family; Qincheng robbed other inmates of their scraps and spent his days drunk and gorged.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷京師，欽程首破獄出降。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took the capital, Qincheng was first to break the prison and come out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng seized the capital, Qincheng was the first to break open the jail and surrender.

sentences.zh: 自成敗，隨之西走，不知所終。

translations.literal: When Zicheng was defeated, he followed him fleeing west; his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng was routed, Qincheng fled west with him; nothing more is known of his fate.

sentences.zh: 福王時，定從賊案，欽程復列首等。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, when the cases of those who followed the rebels were settled, Qincheng was again ranked among the chief culprits.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, when the cases of those who had sided with the rebels were adjudicated, Qincheng was once again listed among the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 當忠賢盛時，其黨爭搏擊清流，獻諂希寵。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian was at the height of power, his partisans vied to attack the upright faction and offered flattery hoping for favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongxian's heyday, his followers competed to strike down the upright faction, fawning and scheming for imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 最著者，石三畏、張訥、盧承欽、門克新、劉徽、智鋌。

translations.literal: The most prominent were Shi Sanwei, Zhang Ne, Lu Chengqin, Men Kexin, Liu Hui, and Zhi Ting.
translations.idiomatic: The most notorious among them were Shi Sanwei, Zhang Ne, Lu Chengqin, Men Kexin, Liu Hui, and Zhi Ting.

sentences.zh: 石三畏 張訥 盧承欽 門克新 劉徽 智鋌

translations.literal: Shi Sanwei, Zhang Ne, Lu Chengqin, Men Kexin, Liu Hui, Zhi Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sanwei, Zhang Ne, Lu Chengqin, Men Kexin, Liu Hui, Zhi Ting.

sentences.zh: 三畏，交河人。

translations.literal: Sanwei was a native of Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: Sanwei was a native of Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 知文登、曹二縣，大著貪聲。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Wendeng and Cao counties and became widely known for greed.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Wendeng and Cao counties, he earned a notorious reputation for corruption.

sentences.zh: 以御史陳九疇薦，得行取。

translations.literal: Recommended by Censor Chen Jiuchou, he was selected for promotion from local office.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Censor Chen Jiuchou, he was selected for promotion from the provinces to the capital.

sentences.zh: 趙南星秉銓，出為王府長史。

translations.literal: When Zhao Nanxing held the Ministry of Personnel, Sanwei was posted out as chief secretary of a princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhao Nanxing controlled the Ministry of Personnel, Sanwei was sent out to serve as chief secretary of a princely household.

sentences.zh: 故事，外吏行取無為王官者，三畏以是大恨。

translations.literal: By precedent, local officials selected for promotion were never made princely household officials; Sanwei therefore nursed a deep hatred.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, local officials promoted to the capital were never assigned to princely households; Sanwei therefore bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 及忠賢得誌，三畏諂附之，遂授御史。

translations.literal: Once Zhongxian gained his wish, Sanwei fawned upon him and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian at last had his way, Sanwei attached himself with flattery and was made a censor.

sentences.zh: 首劾都給事中劉弘化護熊廷弼，太僕卿吳炯黨顧憲成，兩人獲嚴譴。

translations.literal: He was first to impeach Chief Supervising Secretary Liu Honghua for shielding Xiong Tingbi, and Grand Minister of the Stud Wu Jiong for factional ties with Gu Xiancheng; both received severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He opened by impeaching Chief Supervising Secretary Liu Honghua for protecting Xiong Tingbi, and Grand Minister of the Stud Wu Jiong for aligning with Gu Xiancheng; both were severely punished.

sentences.zh: 追論京察三變，力詆李三才、王圖、孫丕揚、曹於汴、湯兆京、王宗賢、顧憲成、胡忻、王元翰、王淑抃、趙南星、張問達、王允成、塗一榛、王象春等十五人，而薦喬應甲、徐兆魁等十三人。

translations.literal: He pursued the three rounds of Beijing inspection, fiercely denouncing Li Sancai, Wang Tu, Sun Piyang, Cao Yubian, Tang Zhaojing, Wang Zongxian, Gu Xiancheng, Hu Xin, Wang Yuanhan, Wang Shubian, Zhao Nanxing, Zhang Wenda, Wang Yuncheng, Tu Yizhen, and Wang Xiangchun—fifteen men in all—while recommending Qiao Yingjia, Xu Zhaokui, and twelve others.
translations.idiomatic: He revisited the three rounds of Beijing inspection, savaging Li Sancai, Wang Tu, Sun Piyang, Cao Yubian, Tang Zhaojing, Wang Zongxian, Gu Xiancheng, Hu Xin, Wang Yuanhan, Wang Shubian, Zhao Nanxing, Zhang Wenda, Wang Yuncheng, Tu Yizhen, and Wang Xiangchun—fifteen men in all—while recommending Qiao Yingjia, Xu Zhaokui, and a dozen others.

sentences.zh: 於是三才等生者除名，死者追奪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the living among Sancai and the rest were stripped of office; the dead were posthumously disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon those still living, including Sancai, were removed from office, and the dead were stripped of honors posthumously.

sentences.zh: 已，極論三案，請以其疏付史館，而劾禮部侍郎周炳謨、南京尚書沈儆炌、大理丞張廷拱，三人亦獲譴。

translations.literal: Later he argued forcefully over the three cases, asking that his memorial be sent to the historiographical office, and impeached Vice Minister of Rites Zhou Bingmo, Nanjing Minister Shen Jiaochang, and Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Tinggong; all three were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed hard on the three cases, requesting that his memorial be deposited in the historiographical office, and impeached Vice Minister of Rites Zhou Bingmo, Nanjing Minister Shen Jiaochang, and Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Tinggong; all three were censured.

sentences.zh: 三畏為忠賢「十孩兒」之一。

translations.literal: Sanwei was one of Zhongxian's "Ten Boys."
translations.idiomatic: Sanwei was one of Zhongxian's "Ten Boys."

sentences.zh: 又倚呈秀為薦主，鍛成楊、左之獄，咆哮特甚。

translations.literal: He also relied on Rui Xiang as his patron, forged the cases against Yang and Zuo, and was especially ferocious in his attacks.
translations.idiomatic: He also leaned on Rui Xiang as his patron, forged the cases against Yang and Zuo, and raged with particular savagery.

sentences.zh: 一日，赴戚畹宴，魏良卿在焉。

translations.literal: One day he attended a feast at a kinsman's of the empress; Wei Liangqing was present.
translations.idiomatic: One day he went to a banquet at a kinsman's of the empress, where Wei Liangqing was also in attendance.

sentences.zh: 三畏醉，誤令優人演《劉瑾酗酒》一劇。

translations.literal: Sanwei, drunk, mistakenly ordered actors to perform the play "Liu Jin Drunk."
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Sanwei mistakenly ordered the players to perform the play "Liu Jin Drunk."

sentences.zh: 忠賢聞，大怒，削籍歸。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian heard of it, he was greatly angered and had Sanwei stripped of office and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian heard of it and flew into a rage; Sanwei was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 忠賢殛，借忤璫名，起故官，為南京御史朱純所劾，罷去。

translations.literal: After Zhongxian was executed, Sanwei was restored to his former post on the pretext of having offended the eunuch faction; Censor-in-Chief Zhu Chun of Nanjing impeached him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongxian's execution, Sanwei was reinstated on the pretext that he had defied the eunuch faction; Censor-in-Chief Zhu Chun of Nanjing impeached him and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 訥，閬中人。

translations.literal: Ne was a native of Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ne was a native of Langzhong.

sentences.zh: 由行人擢御史，承忠賢指，首劾趙南星十大罪，並及御史王允成，吏部郎鄒維璉、程國祥、夏嘉遇。

translations.literal: Promoted from Courier to censor, following Zhongxian's lead he was first to impeach Zhao Nanxing on ten major crimes, also implicating Censor Wang Yuncheng and Section Chiefs Zou Weilian, Cheng Guoxiang, and Xia Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from Courier to censor, he followed Zhongxian's cue and was first to impeach Zhao Nanxing on ten capital crimes, also dragging in Censor Wang Yuncheng and Section Chiefs Zou Weilian, Cheng Guoxiang, and Xia Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大喜，立除南星等名，且令再奏。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly pleased; Nanxing and the others were immediately stripped of office, and Ne was ordered to submit further memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was delighted; Nanxing and the rest were at once removed from the rolls, and Ne was told to memorialize again.

sentences.zh: 乃羅織兵部侍郎李邦華，湖廣巡撫孫鼎相，舊給事中毛士龍、魏大中，光祿少卿史記事等十七人，誣以賄南星得官，諸人並獲罪。

translations.literal: He then fabricated charges against Vice Minister of War Li Banghua, Huguang Governor Sun Dingxiang, former Supervising Secretaries Mao Shilong and Wei Dazhong, and Vice Minister of the Imperial Household Shi Jishi—seventeen men in all—falsely claiming they had bribed Nanxing for their appointments; all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He then wove a net around Vice Minister of War Li Banghua, Huguang Governor Sun Dingxiang, former Supervising Secretaries Mao Shilong and Wei Dazhong, and Vice Minister of the Imperial Household Shi Jishi—seventeen men in all—accusing them of buying office from Nanxing; all were condemned.

sentences.zh: 尋請毀東林、關中、江右、徽州諸書院。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized to destroy the academies of the Donglin, Guanzhong, Jiangyou, and Huizhou factions.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he petitioned to raze the academies of the Donglin, Guanzhong, Jiangyou, and Huizhou factions.

sentences.zh: 痛詆鄒元標、馮從吾、余懋衡、孫慎行並及侍郎鄭三俊、畢懋良等，亦坐削奪。

translations.literal: He savagely denounced Zou Yuanbiao, Feng Congwu, Yu Maohui, and Sun Shensheng, also implicating Vice Ministers Zheng Sanjun and Bi Maoliang; they too were stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: He viciously attacked Zou Yuanbiao, Feng Congwu, Yu Maohui, and Sun Shensheng, and extended his charges to Vice Ministers Zheng Sanjun and Bi Maoliang; they too were stripped of honors.

sentences.zh: 復劾罷江西巡撫韓光祐。

translations.literal: He also impeached and had dismissed Han Guangyou, Governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He further impeached Han Guangyou, Governor of Jiangxi, and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 訥為忠賢鷹犬，前後搏擊用力多。

translations.literal: Ne was Zhongxian's hawk and hound; in repeated assaults he exerted himself greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Ne served as Zhongxian's hawk and hound, throwing himself into attack after attack.

sentences.zh: 忠賢深德之，用其兄太僕少卿樸至南京戶部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was deeply grateful and had Ne's elder brother, Vice Minister of the Stud Pu, promoted to Minister of Revenue in Nanjing with the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian repaid him handsomely, promoting Ne's elder brother Pu from Vice Minister of the Stud to Minister of Revenue in Nanjing and adding the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 樸官宣大總督，為忠賢建四祠。

translations.literal: Pu, as Grand Coordinator of Xuanhua, built four shrines for Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Coordinator of Xuanhua, Pu erected four shrines to Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並入逆案。

translations.literal: Both brothers were included in the treason cases.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers were entered in the treason cases.

sentences.zh: 承欽，餘姚人。

translations.literal: Chengqin was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqin was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 由中書舍人擢御史，首劾罷戶部侍郎孫居相等，因言：「東林自顧憲成、李三才、趙南星而外，如王圖、高攀龍等謂之副帥，曹於汴、湯兆京、史記事、魏大中、袁化中謂之『先鋒』，丁元薦、沈正宗、李樸、賀烺謂之『敢死軍人』，孫丕揚、鄒元標謂之『土木魔神。』

translations.literal: Promoted from Central Drafting Clerk to censor, he was first to impeach and have dismissed Vice Minister of Revenue Sun Juxiang and others, then said: "Apart from Gu Xiancheng, Li Sancai, and Zhao Nanxing, the Donglin faction counts Wang Tu and Gao Panlong as its deputy commanders, Cao Yubian, Tang Zhaojing, Shi Jishi, Wei Dazhong, and Yuan Huazhong as its 'vanguard,' Ding Yuanjian, Shen Zhengzong, Li Pu, and He Lang as its 'suicide troops,' and Sun Piyang and Zou Yuanbiao as its 'earth-and-wood demons.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from Central Drafting Clerk to censor, he opened by impeaching Vice Minister of Revenue Sun Juxiang and others out of office, then declared: "Beyond Gu Xiancheng, Li Sancai, and Zhao Nanxing, the Donglin counts Wang Tu and Gao Panlong as its deputy chiefs, Cao Yubian, Tang Zhaojing, Shi Jishi, Wei Dazhong, and Yuan Huazhong as its 'shock troops,' Ding Yuanjian, Shen Zhengzong, Li Pu, and He Lang as its 'suicide soldiers,' and Sun Piyang and Zou Yuanbiao as its 'demons of earth and timber.

sentences.zh: 請以黨人姓名、罪狀榜示海內。」

translations.literal: He requested that the names and crimes of the faction members be posted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the names and offenses of the faction be published across the empire.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大喜，敕所司刊籍，凡黨人已罪未罪者，悉編名其中。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was delighted and ordered the relevant offices to print a register; everyone among the faction already condemned or not yet condemned was entered by name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was overjoyed and commanded the offices to compile and print a register; every faction member, whether already punished or not, was entered by name.

sentences.zh: 承欽官至太僕少卿卒。

translations.literal: Chengqin rose to Vice Minister of the Stud and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqin reached the post of Vice Minister of the Stud and died in office.

sentences.zh: 克新，汝陽人。

translations.literal: Kexin was a native of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kexin was a native of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 由青州推官擢御史，劾右庶子葉燦、光祿卿錢春、按察使張光縉倚傍門戶，且請速誅熊廷弼。

translations.literal: Promoted from investigating prefect of Qingzhou to censor, he impeached Right Companion Reader Ye Can, Grand Minister of the Household Qian Chun, and Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Guangjin for leaning on factional patronage, and also called for swift execution of Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from investigating prefect of Qingzhou to censor, he impeached Right Companion Reader Ye Can, Grand Minister of the Household Qian Chun, and Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Guangjin for sheltering behind factional patronage, and demanded that Xiong Tingbi be put to death at once.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大喜，立傳旨行刑。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was delighted and immediately issued an imperial order for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was delighted and at once transmitted an order for execution.

sentences.zh: 以閣臣固爭，乃令俟秋後，而除燦等名。

translations.literal: Because grand secretaries firmly objected, the sentence was deferred until autumn, and Ye Can and the others were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries protested vigorously, so execution was postponed until autumn, and Ye Can and the others were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 御史吳裕中，廷弼姻也，憤曰：「廷弼已死人，何必疏促。」

translations.literal: Censor Wu Yuzhong, a relative by marriage of Tingbi, said in anger: "Tingbi is already dead—why press for execution in a memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Yuzhong, who was related to Tingbi by marriage, said in fury: "Tingbi is already dead—why urge his execution in a memorial?"

sentences.zh: 與克新絕，逆黨由此銜之。

translations.literal: He broke with Kexin, and the faction henceforth bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with Kexin, and the faction thereafter nursed a grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 廷弼之禍，大學士丁紹軾有力焉。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ding Shaozhi had a significant hand in Tingbi's downfall.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ding Shaozhi had done much to bring about Tingbi's ruin.

sentences.zh: 馮銓因使人嗾裕中劾紹軾，而先報忠賢曰：「裕中必為廷弼報仇。」

translations.literal: Feng Quan therefore had someone incite Yuzhong to impeach Shaozhi, and first told Zhongxian: "Yuzhong will surely avenge Tingbi."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan therefore had a man goad Yuzhong into impeaching Shaozhi, and told Zhongxian in advance: "Yuzhong is sure to avenge Tingbi."

sentences.zh: 裕中疏上，遂命於午門杖之百，舁至家死。

translations.literal: When Yuzhong's memorial arrived, he was ordered beaten one hundred strokes at the Meridian Gate and died being carried home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzhong's memorial reached the throne, he was ordered flogged one hundred strokes at the Meridian Gate and died on the litter being carried home.

sentences.zh: 魏廣微將謝政，克新言：「廣微砥柱狂瀾，厥功甚偉，宜錫之溫綸，優以禮數。」

translations.literal: Wei Guangwei was about to retire from office; Kexin said: "Guangwei stood like a pillar against the raging flood—his merit was great; he should be granted a warm edict and honored with full ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangwei was preparing to leave office; Kexin said: "Guangwei stood like a pillar against the raging flood—his service was magnificent; he should be sent a gracious edict and honored with full ceremony."

sentences.zh: 以是稍失忠賢意。

translations.literal: For this he slightly lost Zhongxian's favor.
translations.idiomatic: For this he fell somewhat from Zhongxian's favor.

sentences.zh: 太倉人孫文豸，與同里武進士顧同寅嘗客廷弼所。

translations.literal: Sun Wenzhi of Taicang and his fellow townsman, military jinshi Gu Tongyin, had once been guests at Tingbi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wenzhi of Taicang and his fellow townsman, military jinshi Gu Tongyin, had once lodged with Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 廷弼死，文豸為詩誄之，同寅題尺牘亦有追惜語，為邏卒所獲。

translations.literal: After Tingbi died, Wenzhi composed an elegy for him and Tongyin wrote words of mourning on a letter; both were seized by border patrols.
translations.idiomatic: After Tingbi's death, Wenzhi wrote an elegy for him and Tongyin inscribed words of mourning on a letter; both were caught by border patrols.

sentences.zh: 克新遽以誹謗聞，兩人遂棄市，連及同郡編修陳仁錫、故修撰文震孟，並削籍。

translations.literal: Kexin immediately reported them for slander; both were executed in the marketplace, and Compiler Chen Renxi of the same prefecture and former Compiler Wen Zhenmeng were also stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Kexin at once reported them for slander; both were executed in the marketplace, and Compiler Chen Renxi of the same prefecture and former Compiler Wen Zhenmeng were stripped of office as well.

sentences.zh: 克新尋巡按山東，崇禎初，引疾去。

translations.literal: Kexin soon went as touring censor to Shandong; at the start of Chongzhen's reign he resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Kexin soon toured Shandong as censor; at the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 徽，清苑人。

translations.literal: Hui was a native of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a native of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 由臨淮知縣擢御史。

translations.literal: Promoted from magistrate of Linhuai to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from magistrate of Linhuai to censor.

sentences.zh: 陳朝輔劾馮銓，徽出疏繼之，且曰：「臣與銓同鄉，痛惡群小之誤銓，不忍銓坐失燕、趙本色。」

translations.literal: When Chen Chaofu impeached Feng Quan, Hui submitted a follow-up memorial saying: "I am a fellow townsman of Quan's; I loathe the petty men who have led Quan astray and cannot bear to see Quan lose the true character of Yan and Zhao through their fault."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Chaofu impeached Feng Quan, Hui followed with a memorial of his own, saying: "I am Quan's fellow townsman; I hate the petty men who have misled him and cannot bear to see Quan stripped of the true mettle of Yan and Zhao on their account."

sentences.zh: 聞者笑之。

translations.literal: Those who heard it laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it laughed.

sentences.zh: 出督遼餉，乾沒不貲。

translations.literal: Sent out to oversee Liaodong funds, he embezzled without measure.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to oversee Liaodong supplies, he embezzled on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 初，梁夢環巡關，誣熊廷弼侵盜軍貲十七萬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liang Menghuan inspected the passes, he had falsely charged Xiong Tingbi with embezzling 170,000 taels of military funds.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liang Menghuan inspected the frontier passes, he had falsely accused Xiong Tingbi of embezzling 170,000 taels of military funds.

sentences.zh: 徽言：「廷弼原領帑金三十萬，茫無所歸。

translations.literal: Hui said: "Tingbi originally received 300,000 taels from the treasury, yet they vanished without trace.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: "Tingbi originally received 300,000 taels from the treasury, yet they vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 其家貲不下百萬，而僅以十七萬還公家，何以申國法？」

translations.literal: His household wealth was no less than a million, yet he returned only 170,000 to the state—how can this satisfy the law of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: His family fortune was no less than a million, yet he returned only 170,000 to the state—how can this satisfy the law of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 因誣給事中劉弘化、毛士龍，御史樊尚燝、房可壯贓賄事。

translations.literal: He then falsely charged Supervising Secretaries Liu Honghua and Mao Shilong and Censors Fan Shangcan and Fang Kezhuang with bribery.
translations.idiomatic: He then fabricated charges of bribery against Supervising Secretaries Liu Honghua and Mao Shilong and Censors Fan Shangcan and Fang Kezhuang.

sentences.zh: 忠賢喜，削弘化等籍，敕所司徵廷弼贓。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was pleased; Honghua and the others were stripped of office, and the offices were ordered to recover Tingbi's illicit gains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was pleased; Honghua and the others were removed from the rolls, and the offices were ordered to recover Tingbi's ill-gotten gains.

sentences.zh: 尋加徽太僕少卿，先後頌忠賢至十一疏。

translations.literal: Hui was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Stud and in eleven memorials successively praised Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was soon made Vice Minister of the Stud and across eleven memorials successively extolled Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，被劾回籍。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell, Hui was impeached and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian fell, Hui was impeached and sent back to his native place.

sentences.zh: 鋌，元氏人。

translations.literal: Ting was a native of Yuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was a native of Yuanshi.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試，受業趙南星門，授知縣。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination, studied under Zhao Nanxing, and was appointed magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination, studied under Zhao Nanxing, and served as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 由魏廣微通於忠賢，得擢御史，遂疏詆南星為元惡。

translations.literal: Through Wei Guangwei he gained access to Zhongxian, was promoted to censor, and memorialized denouncing Nanxing as the chief villain.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wei Guangwei he reached Zhongxian, was raised to censor, and memorialized denouncing Nanxing as the arch-villain.

sentences.zh: 先後劾罷禮部侍郎徐光啟等。

translations.literal: In succession he impeached and had dismissed Vice Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi and others.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he impeached and removed Vice Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi and others from office.

sentences.zh: 鋌以乙榜起家，欲得忠賢歡，搏擊彌銳。

translations.literal: Ting, having entered office through the provincial examination, sought Zhongxian's favor all the more keenly and attacked with ever greater sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Ting, having risen through the provincial examination rather than the palace degree, courted Zhongxian's favor all the more eagerly and struck with ever greater ferocity.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大喜，加太僕少卿，以憂歸。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly pleased and promoted him to Vice Minister of the Stud; he then returned home on grounds of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was delighted and made him Vice Minister of the Stud; he then went home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，禮部主事喬若雯劾鋌及陳九疇、張訥為魏廣微爪牙，詔奪職。

translations.literal: At the start of Chongzhen's reign, Section Chief Qiao Ruowen impeached Ting together with Chen Jiuchou and Zhang Ne as Wei Guangwei's claws and fangs; an edict stripped them of office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, Section Chief Qiao Ruowen impeached Ting together with Chen Jiuchou and Zhang Ne as Wei Guangwei's claws and fangs; an edict removed them from office.

sentences.zh: 後與三畏、訥、承欽、克新、徽並入逆案，訥遣戍，三畏等論徒。

translations.literal: Later Ting, together with Sanwei, Ne, Chengqin, Kexin, and Hui, was entered in the treason cases; Ne was sent into exile, and Sanwei and the others were sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ting, together with Sanwei, Ne, Chengqin, Kexin, and Hui, was entered in the treason cases; Ne was banished to frontier service, and Sanwei and the others were sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 當忠賢橫時，宵小希進幹寵，皆陷善類以自媒。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian held sway, petty men hoping for advancement and favor all destroyed the good to recommend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongxian ruled unchecked, petty men scheming for promotion and favor destroyed the upright to advance themselves.

sentences.zh: 始所擊皆東林也，其後凡所欲去者，悉誣以東林而逐之。

translations.literal: At first those they struck were all Donglin men; afterward whoever they wished removed was falsely labeled Donglin and driven out.
translations.idiomatic: At first their targets were all Donglin men; afterward anyone they wished gone was falsely branded a Donglin partisan and driven out.

sentences.zh: 自四年十月迄熹宗崩，斃詔獄者十餘人，下獄謫戍者數十人，削奪者三百餘人，他革職貶黜者不可勝計。

translations.literal: From the tenth month of the fourth year until the Xizong Emperor's death, more than ten died in the Imperial Prison, several tens were imprisoned or banished to frontier service, more than three hundred were stripped of rank, and those merely dismissed or demoted were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From the tenth month of the fourth year until the Xizong Emperor's death, more than ten perished in the Imperial Prison, several tens were jailed or sent into exile, more than three hundred were stripped of honors, and those merely dismissed or demoted were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 王紹徽

translations.literal: Wang Shaohui
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaohui

sentences.zh: 王紹徽，咸寧人，尚書用賓從孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Shaohui was a native of Xianning and a grandnephew of Minister Wang Yongbin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaohui was a native of Xianning and a grandnephew of Minister Wang Yongbin.

sentences.zh: 舉萬曆二十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 26.

sentences.zh: 授鄒平知縣，擢戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Zouping, he was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Zouping, he was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 居官強執，頗以清操聞。

translations.literal: In office he was forceful and obstinate and was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was forceful and unyielding and enjoyed a reputation for clean conduct.

sentences.zh: 湯賓尹號召黨與，圖柄用。

translations.literal: Tang Binyin rallied his faction and plotted to seize power.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Binyin rallied his faction and plotted to seize power.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書孫丕揚以紹徽其門生，用年例出為山東參議，紹徽辭疾不就。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Sun Piyang, because Shaohui was his student, posted him out by seniority as Assistant Administrator of Shandong; Shaohui declined on grounds of illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Sun Piyang, because Shaohui was his protégé, transferred him out by seniority to Assistant Administrator of Shandong; Shaohui pleaded illness and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 泰昌時，起通政參議，遷太僕少卿，被劾引疾。

translations.literal: Under Taichang he was recalled as Assistant Director of the Office of Transmission, promoted to Vice Minister of the Stud, impeached, and resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taichang he was recalled as Assistant Director of the Office of Transmission, promoted to Vice Minister of the Stud, impeached, and resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋以拾遺罷。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed for a remonstrance offense.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed for a remonstrance offense.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年冬，魏忠賢既逐去左光鬥，即召紹徽代為左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Tianqi, after Wei Zhongxian had driven out Zuo Guangdou, Shaohui was summoned to replace him as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Tianqi 4, after Wei Zhongxian had driven out Zuo Guangdou, Shaohui was summoned to replace him as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 明年六月進左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the following year he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋進戶部侍郎，督倉場，甫視事，改左都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue to oversee the granaries; scarcely had he taken office when he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of Revenue to oversee the granaries; he had barely assumed the post when he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十二月拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 忠賢為從子良卿求世封，紹徽即為奏請良卿封伯。

translations.literal: Zhongxian sought a hereditary enfeoffment for his nephew Liangqing; Shaohui immediately memorialized requesting that Liangqing be enfeoffed as a count.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian sought a hereditary title for his nephew Liangqing; Shaohui at once memorialized asking that Liangqing be enfeoffed as a count.

sentences.zh: 請推崇其三世，紹徽亦議如其言。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian asked that honors be extended to three generations of his family, Shaohui also agreed as requested.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian asked that honors be extended to three generations of his line, Shaohui likewise endorsed the request.

sentences.zh: 至忠賢遣內臣出鎮，紹徽乃偕同官陳四不可。

translations.literal: Only when Zhongxian dispatched inner eunuchs to command the armies did Shaohui join his colleagues in memorializing that this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Zhongxian sent palace eunuchs to command the armies did Shaohui join his colleagues in memorializing that this must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 王恭廠、朝天宮並災，紹徽言誅罰過多。

translations.literal: When the Wang Gongchang Arsenal and Chaotian Palace both suffered disasters, Shaohui said punishments and executions had grown excessive.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wang Gongchang Arsenal and Chaotian Palace both suffered disasters, Shaohui said that punishments and executions had grown excessive.

sentences.zh: 忤忠賢意，得譙讓。

translations.literal: This displeased Zhongxian, and Shaohui was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: This offended Zhongxian, and Shaohui was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 已復上言：「四方多事，九邊缺餉，難免催科，乞定分數，寬年限，以緩急之宜付撫按。

translations.literal: Later he memorialized again: "Affairs are troubled on every side; the nine frontiers lack funds, and tax collection cannot be avoided—I beg that fixed quotas and extended deadlines be set, leaving the balance of urgency and ease to the governors and censors.
translations.idiomatic: He later memorialized again: "Trouble presses on every side; the nine frontiers lack funds, and tax collection cannot be avoided—I beg that fixed quotas and extended deadlines be set, leaving governors and censors to judge what is urgent and what may wait.

sentences.zh: 正殿既成，兩殿宜緩，請敕工部裁省織造、瓷器諸冗費，用佐大工。

translations.literal: Now that the main hall is finished, work on the two secondary halls should be slowed; I beg that the Ministry of Works be ordered to cut redundant expenses for weaving, porcelain, and the like to help fund the great project.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the main hall is finished, work on the two secondary halls should be slowed; I beg that the Ministry of Works be ordered to cut redundant expenses for weaving, porcelain, and the like to help fund the great project.

sentences.zh: 奸黨削除已盡，恐藏禍蓄怨，反受中傷。

translations.literal: The wicked faction has already been purged to the last man; I fear that hidden resentments may yet bring slander in return.
translations.idiomatic: The wicked faction has already been purged to the last man; I fear that hidden resentments may yet bring slander in return.

sentences.zh: 逮系重刑，加於封疆、顯過、三案巨奸，則人心悅服，餘宜少寬貸。」

translations.literal: If heavy punishment and arrest are reserved for frontier crimes, conspicuous offenses, and the great villains of the three cases, the hearts of the people will be satisfied; the rest should be treated with greater leniency."
translations.idiomatic: If heavy punishment and arrest are reserved for frontier crimes, conspicuous offenses, and the great villains of the three cases, the people will be satisfied; the rest should be treated with greater leniency."

sentences.zh: 復忤忠賢意。

translations.literal: This again displeased Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: This again offended Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 初，紹徽在萬曆朝，素以排擊東林為其黨所推，故忠賢首用居要地。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Wanli reign, Shaohui had long been promoted by his faction for attacking the Donglin, and so Zhongxian first put him in a key post.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wanli era on, Wang Shaohui had made his name attacking the Donglin, and his faction had backed him for it; Wei Zhongxian therefore placed him first among his appointments to positions of real power.

sentences.zh: 紹徽仿民間《水滸傳》，編東林一百八人為《點將錄》，獻之，令按名黜汰，以是益為忠賢所喜。

translations.literal: Shaohui, imitating the popular Water Margin, compiled the Donglin's 108 men into a Roll of Commanders, presented it, and had them dismissed by name; for this Zhongxian delighted in him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohui took the popular Water Margin as his model, listed 108 Donglin men in a Roll of Commanders, and presented it with orders to purge them by name. Wei Zhongxian was pleased beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 既而奸黨轉盛，後進者求速化，妒諸人妨己，擬次第逐之。

translations.literal: Before long the evil faction grew stronger; newcomers sought quick advancement, resented those who stood in their way, and planned to drive them out one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the wicked faction swelled; latecomers hungry for rapid promotion resented anyone who blocked their path and plotted to remove them in turn.

sentences.zh: 孫傑乃謀使崔呈秀入閣，先擊去紹徽，令御史袁鯨、張文熙詆紹徽朋比。

translations.literal: Sun Jie then plotted to bring Cui Chengxiu into the Grand Secretariat, first removing Shaohui by having censors Yuan Jing and Zhang Wenxi denounce Shaohui for factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jie then schemed to install Cui Chengxiu in the Grand Secretariat. First he had to remove Shaohui, and set Censors Yuan Jing and Zhang Wenxi to denounce him for clique-making.

sentences.zh: 鯨再疏列其鬻官穢狀，遂落紹徽職，而以周應秋代。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized again, listing his sale-of-offices corruption; Shaohui was dismissed and Zhou Yingqiu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jing memorialized again, cataloguing Shaohui's bribery and corruption in office sales; Shaohui was stripped of his post and Zhou Yingqiu took his place.

sentences.zh: 逆案既定，紹徽削籍論徒。

translations.literal: When the treason cases were settled, Shaohui was struck from the rolls and sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: When the treason cases were settled, Shaohui was removed from the register and sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 周應秋

translations.literal: Zhou Yingqiu
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yingqiu

sentences.zh: 應秋，金壇人。

translations.literal: Yingqiu was a native of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yingqiu was a native of Jintan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi during the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination during the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官工部侍郎，生平無持操。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Works; in life he held to no principles.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Works, yet in life he stood for nothing.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年避東林謝病去。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi he pleaded illness and left office to avoid the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianqi he pleaded illness and quit office to keep clear of the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，魏忠賢起為南京刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: The next winter Wei Zhongxian had him recalled as Left Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter Wei Zhongxian recalled him as Left Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 五年召拜刑部添註尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned and appointed adjunct Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned and appointed adjunct Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時忠賢廣樹私人，悉餌以顯爵，故兩京大僚多添註。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongxian planted his men widely, baiting them all with high titles, so many senior officials in both capitals were adjunct appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was then planting his own men everywhere, luring them with glittering titles, and many senior posts in both capitals were filled by adjunct appointees.

sentences.zh: 尋改左都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 家善烹飪，每魏良卿過，進豚蹄留飲，良卿大歡，時號「煨蹄總憲」。

translations.literal: At home he was skilled in cookery; whenever Wei Liangqing came visiting, he would serve braised pig's trotters and keep him to drink. Liangqing was delighted, and people called him the "Commissioner of Braised Trotters."
translations.idiomatic: He was a gifted cook at home; whenever Wei Liangqing called, he would serve braised pig's trotters and keep him drinking. Liangqing was delighted, and people nicknamed him the "Commissioner of Braised Trotters."

sentences.zh: 明年七月代紹徽為吏部尚書，與文選郎李夔龍鬻官分賄。

translations.literal: The next July he replaced Shaohui as Minister of Personnel and, with Bureau Director Li Kuilong, sold offices and split the bribes.
translations.idiomatic: The following July he replaced Shaohui as Minister of Personnel and, with Bureau Director Li Kuilong, sold offices and divided the spoils.

sentences.zh: 清流未盡逐者，應秋毛舉細故，削奪無虛日。

translations.literal: For upright officials not yet fully purged, Yingqiu seized on petty pretexts; not a day passed without demotions and confiscations.
translations.idiomatic: For upright men not yet fully driven out, Yingqiu hunted up trivial offenses; scarcely a day passed without demotion or confiscation.

sentences.zh: 忠賢門下有「十狗」，應秋其首也。

translations.literal: Among Zhongxian's followers were the "Ten Dogs," and Yingqiu was their chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's inner circle included the "Ten Dogs," and Yingqiu was their leader.

sentences.zh: 冒三殿功，屢加太子太師。

translations.literal: He claimed credit for the three halls and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed merit for the three halls and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，楊漣等拷死，應秋夜半叩戶，語其館客曰：「天眼開，楊漣、左光鬥死矣。」

translations.literal: When Yang Lian and the others were beaten to death in interrogation, Yingqiu knocked at his door at midnight and said to a guest in his house, "Heaven's eye is open—Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou are dead."
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian and the others were tortured to death, Yingqiu knocked at his door in the dead of night and told a house guest, "Heaven's eye has opened—Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou are dead."

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，被劾歸。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded, he was impeached and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was impeached and sent home.

sentences.zh: 已，入逆案，遣戍死。

translations.literal: Later he was included in the treason cases, exiled, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was later listed in the treason cases, exiled, and died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 弟維持。

translations.literal: His younger brother Weichi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhou Weichi.

sentences.zh: 天啟中為御史，請刊黨籍，盡毀天下書院。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he served as a censor, requesting that faction registers be published and all academies in the realm destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he served as a censor, petitioning that faction registers be published and every academy in the empire torn down.

sentences.zh: 俄劾兵部尚書趙彥等，並削籍。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Minister of War Zhao Yan and others, and they were all struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached Minister of War Zhao Yan and others, and they were all struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 以兄應秋在位，引嫌歸。

translations.literal: Because his brother Yingqiu held office, he withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest.
translations.idiomatic: Because his brother Yingqiu still held office, he withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起按浙江，被劾罷。

translations.literal: Early in Chongzhen he was revived to inspect Zhejiang, impeached, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was recalled to inspect Zhejiang, impeached, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並麗逆案。

translations.literal: Both brothers were listed in the treason cases.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers were named in the treason cases.

sentences.zh: 霍維華

translations.literal: Huo Weihua
translations.idiomatic: Huo Weihua

sentences.zh: 霍維華，東光人。

translations.literal: Huo Weihua was a native of Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Weihua was a native of Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 除金壇知縣，徵授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Jintan, then summoned as supervising secretary of the Military Affairs Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jintan, then summoned as supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年六月，中官王安當掌司禮監印，辭疾居外邸，冀得溫旨即視事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianqi, palace eunuch Wang An was to take charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial seal; he pleaded illness and stayed at an outer residence, hoping for a gracious edict before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianqi 1, the palace eunuch Wang An was to take charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial seal. He pleaded illness and remained at an outer residence, hoping a warm edict would let him assume duty at once.

sentences.zh: 安與魏忠賢有隙，閹人陸藎臣者，維華內弟也，偵知之以告。

translations.literal: An and Wei Zhongxian were at odds; the eunuch Lu Genchen was Weihua's brother-in-law, discovered this, and told him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang An and Wei Zhongxian were at odds. The eunuch Lu Genchen, Weihua's brother-in-law, learned of it and informed him.

sentences.zh: 維華故與忠賢同郡交好，遂乘機劾安，忠賢輒矯旨殺之。

translations.literal: Weihua had long been on good terms with Zhongxian as a fellow townsman; he seized the chance to impeach An, and Zhongxian forged an edict and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Weihua had long been on friendly terms with Zhongxian as a fellow townsman. He seized the moment to impeach Wang An, and Zhongxian forged an edict and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 劉一燝、周嘉謨咸惡維華，用年例出為陜西僉事。

translations.literal: Liu Yipao and Zhou Jiamo both hated Weihua; by seniority rule he was sent out as Assistant Commissioner in Shaanxi.
