translations.idiomatic: Liu Yipao and Zhou Jiamo both detested Weihua and, invoking the seniority rule, had him sent out as Assistant Commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 其同官孫傑言，維華三月兵垣無過失，一燝、嘉謨仰王安鼻息，故擯於外。

translations.literal: His colleague Sun Jie said that in three months in the military office Weihua had committed no fault, but Yipao and Jiamo lived by Wang An's breath and therefore sidelined him.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Sun Jie argued that Weihua had done nothing wrong in three months on the military desk, but Yipao and Jiamo lived at Wang An's whim and therefore pushed him out.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大喜，立逐兩人，而維華亦以外艱歸。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly pleased, immediately drove out both men, and Weihua also returned home for a parent's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was delighted and immediately drove out both men; Weihua, for his part, went home to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，朝事大變，南京御史呂鵬雲以外轉請告。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year court affairs changed greatly; Nanjing Censor Lu Pengyun requested leave after transfer outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year the court turned sharply; Nanjing Censor Lu Pengyun, transferred outside the capital, requested leave.

sentences.zh: 忠賢傳旨令與被察徐大化、年例外轉孫傑俱擢京卿，維華及王誌道、郭興治、徐景濂、賈繼春、楊維垣並復故官。

translations.literal: Zhongxian transmitted an edict promoting Xu Dahua, who had failed inspection, Sun Jie, transferred outside by seniority rule, and all to capital ministerial posts; Weihua, Wang Zhidao, Guo Xingzhi, Xu Jinglian, Jia Jichun, and Yang Weiyuan were all restored to their former offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian transmitted an edict promoting Xu Dahua, who had failed inspection, Sun Jie, transferred outside by seniority rule, and others to capital ministerial posts; Weihua, Wang Zhidao, Guo Xingzhi, Xu Jinglian, Jia Jichun, and Yang Weiyuan were all restored to their former offices.

sentences.zh: 維華得刑科。

translations.literal: Weihua received the Military Affairs supervising secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Weihua was given the Military Affairs supervising secretariat.

sentences.zh: 諸為趙南星斥者，競起用事。

translations.literal: Those whom Zhao Nanxing had expelled competed to return to power.
translations.idiomatic: Men whom Zhao Nanxing had driven out scrambled to take power again.

sentences.zh: 維華益銳意攻東林，劾罷御史劉璞、南京御史塗世業、黃公輔、萬言揚。

translations.literal: Weihua pressed his attack on the Donglin all the harder, impeaching and dismissing Censor Liu Pu, Nanjing Censor Tu Shiye, Huang Gongfu, and Wan Yanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Weihua redoubled his assault on the Donglin, impeaching and dismissing Censor Liu Pu, Nanjing Censor Tu Shiye, Huang Gongfu, and Wan Yanyang.

sentences.zh: 追論三案，痛詆劉一燝、韓爌、孫慎行、張問達、周嘉謨、王之寀、楊漣、左光鬥，而譽範濟世、王誌道、汪慶百、劉廷元、徐景濂、郭如楚、張捷、唐嗣美、嶽駿聲、曾道唯。

translations.literal: He reopened debate on the Three Cases, bitterly denouncing Liu Yipao, Han Kuang, Sun Shenxing, Zhang Wenda, Zhou Jiamo, Wang Zhichao, Yang Lian, and Zuo Guangdou, while praising Fan Jishi, Wang Zhidao, Wang Qingbai, Liu Tingyuan, Xu Jinglian, Guo Ruchu, Zhang Jie, Tang Simei, Yue Junsheng, and Zeng Daowei.
translations.idiomatic: He reopened the Three Cases, savaging Liu Yipao, Han Kuang, Sun Shenxing, Zhang Wenda, Zhou Jiamo, Wang Zhichao, Yang Lian, and Zuo Guangdou while praising Fan Jishi, Wang Zhidao, Wang Qingbai, Liu Tingyuan, Xu Jinglian, Guo Ruchu, Zhang Jie, Tang Simei, Yue Junsheng, and Zeng Daowei.

sentences.zh: 請改《光宗實錄》，宣其疏史館。

translations.literal: He requested revision of the Veritable Records of Emperor Guangzong and had his memorial publicized at the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to rewrite the Veritable Records of Emperor Guangzong and had his memorial circulated at the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 忠賢立傳旨削一燝等五人籍，逮之寀，免李可灼戍，擢濟世巡撫、誌道等京卿，嗣美以下悉起用，實錄更撰，而以閣臣言免一燝等罪。

translations.literal: Zhongxian transmitted an edict stripping Yipao and four others from the register, arresting Wang Zhichao, exempting Li Kezhuo from exile, promoting Jishi to grand coordinator and Zhidao and others to capital posts, restoring Simei and those below, and ordering the Veritable Records rewritten; yet by the Grand Secretaries' plea Yipao and the others were spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian transmitted an edict stripping Yipao and four others from the register, arresting Wang Zhichao, exempting Li Kezhuo from exile, promoting Fan Jishi to grand coordinator and Wang Zhidao and others to capital posts, restoring Tang Simei and those below, and ordering the Veritable Records rewritten—yet the Grand Secretaries interceded and Yipao and the rest were spared.

sentences.zh: 尋言，總督張我續宜罪，尚書趙彥宜去，御史方震孺不宜逮，韓敬宜復官，湯賓尹宜雪。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that Governor Zhang Woxu should be punished, Minister Zhao Yan should leave office, Censor Fang Zhenru should not be arrested, Han Jing should be restored, and Tang Binyin should be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he memorialized that Governor Zhang Woxu should be punished, Minister Zhao Yan removed, Censor Fang Zhenru left unarrested, Han Jing restored to office, and Tang Binyin exonerated.

sentences.zh: 忤忠賢意，傳旨譙責之。

translations.literal: This ran counter to Zhongxian's intent, and an edict rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: This crossed Wei Zhongxian's wishes, and an edict rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 五年冬擢太僕少卿。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 明年擢本寺卿。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Director of the same ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 尋擢兵部右侍郎，署部事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and acted as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and directed the ministry in the minister's stead.

sentences.zh: 每陳奏，必頌忠賢。

translations.literal: In every memorial he praised Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Every memorial he submitted sang Wei Zhongxian's praises.

sentences.zh: 七年，延綏奏捷，進右都御史，蔭子錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, with victory reported in Yan-sui, he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and his son ennobled as a thousand-household of the Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after victory was reported in Yan-sui, he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and his son ennobled as a thousand-household of the Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 寧、錦敘功，進兵部尚書，視侍郎事，蔭子如之。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed for Ningyuan and Jinzhou, he was promoted to Minister of War while still serving as vice minister, and his son was ennobled likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were granted for Ningyuan and Jinzhou, he was promoted to Minister of War while still serving as vice minister, and his son received the same ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 俄敘三殿功，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon, for merit in the three halls, he was made Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, for merit in the three halls, he was made Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 維華性憸邪，與崔呈秀為忠賢謀主。

translations.literal: Weihua was by nature sly and wicked; with Cui Chengxiu he served as Zhongxian's chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Weihua was sly and corrupt by nature; with Cui Chengxiu he served as Wei Zhongxian's chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 所親為近侍，宮禁事皆預知，因進仙方靈露飲。

translations.literal: Those close to him were palace attendants; he knew palace affairs in advance and presented an immortal elixir called Spirit-Dew Drink.
translations.idiomatic: His intimates were inner attendants; he learned palace affairs before they happened and presented an elixir called Spirit-Dew Drink.

sentences.zh: 帝初甚甘之，已漸厭。

translations.literal: At first the emperor greatly enjoyed it, but gradually he grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor drank it with relish, but in time he tired of it.

sentences.zh: 及得疾，體腫，忠賢頗以咎維華。

translations.literal: When he fell ill and his body swelled, Zhongxian largely blamed Weihua.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill and his body swelled, Zhongxian largely blamed Weihua.

sentences.zh: 維華甚懼，而慮有後患，欲先自貳於忠賢，乃力辭寧、錦恩命，讓功袁崇煥，乞以己蔭授之。

translations.literal: Weihua was greatly afraid and, fearing future trouble, wished to break with Zhongxian first; he forcefully declined the honors from Ningyuan and Jinzhou, yielded the credit to Yuan Chonghuan, and begged that his own ennoblement be conferred on Yuan instead.
translations.idiomatic: Weihua was terrified. Fearing what might follow, he tried to break with Zhongxian first: he forcefully declined the honors from Ningyuan and Jinzhou, yielded the credit to Yuan Chonghuan, and begged that his own ennoblement be transferred to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 忠賢覺其意，降旨頗厲。

translations.literal: Zhongxian saw his intent and issued a harsh edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian saw through him and issued a stern edict.

sentences.zh: 無何，熹宗崩，忠賢敗，維華與楊維垣等彌縫百方。

translations.literal: Before long the Xizong Emperor died, Zhongxian fell, and Weihua, with Yang Weiyuan, patched things over by every means.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xizong Emperor died, Zhongxian fell, and Weihua, with Yang Weiyuan, patched over his record by every means they could.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，以兵部尚書協理戎政。

translations.literal: That October he served as Minister of War assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That October he served as Minister of War with charge over military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，附璫者多罷去，維華自如。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen reign began, many who had clung to the eunuch faction were dismissed, yet Weihua remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen reign began, many who had clung to the eunuch faction were cast out, yet Weihua held on as before.

sentences.zh: 遼東督師王之臣免，代者袁崇煥未至，維華謀行邊自固。

translations.literal: Liaodong commander-in-chief Wang Zhichen was removed; his successor Yuan Chonghuan had not yet arrived, and Weihua planned a tour of the border to secure his position.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong commander-in-chief Wang Zhichen was removed; his successor Yuan Chonghuan had not yet arrived, and Weihua planned a border tour to shore up his position.

sentences.zh: 帝已可之，給事中顏繼祖極論其罪，言「維華狡人也，璫熾則借璫，璫敗則攻璫。

translations.literal: The emperor had already approved, but Supervising Secretary Yan Jizu argued his crimes at length, saying, "Weihua is a crafty man—when the eunuchs flourish he borrows them; when they fall he attacks them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already assented, but Supervising Secretary Yan Jizu laid out his crimes at length: "Weihua is a crafty man—when the eunuchs are ascendant he rides their power; when they fall he turns on them.

sentences.zh: 擊楊、左者，維華也。

translations.literal: The man who struck at Yang and Zuo was Weihua.
translations.idiomatic: The man who struck down Yang and Zuo was Weihua.

sentences.zh: 楊、左逮，而陽為救者，亦維華也。

translations.literal: When Yang and Zuo were arrested, the one who pretended to save them was also Weihua.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang and Zuo were seized, the man who feigned rescue was also Weihua.

sentences.zh: 以一給事中，三年躐至尚書，無敘不及，有賚必加，即維華亦難以自解。」

translations.literal: From a supervising secretary to minister in three years—every promotion he received, every gift conferred—even Weihua cannot explain himself."
translations.idiomatic: From supervising secretary to minister in three years—every leap in rank, every gift from the throne—even Weihua cannot account for himself."

sentences.zh: 乃寢前命。

translations.literal: The previous order was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier order was set aside.

sentences.zh: 頃之，言者踵至，維華乃引退。

translations.literal: Before long accusers followed one after another, and Weihua withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long accusers came in waves, and Weihua resigned.

sentences.zh: 逆案既定，維華戍徐州，氣勢猶盛。

translations.literal: When the treason cases were settled, Weihua was exiled to Xuzhou, yet his bearing remained proud.
translations.idiomatic: When the treason cases were settled, Weihua was exiled to Xuzhou, yet he carried himself as proudly as ever.

sentences.zh: 七年，駱馬湖淤，維華言於治河尚書劉榮嗣，請自宿遷抵徐州，穿渠二百餘里，引黃河水通漕，冀敘功復職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Luoma Lake silted up; Weihua spoke to River Works Minister Liu Rongsi, requesting a canal of more than two hundred li from Suqian to Xuzhou to channel Yellow River water into the grain transport, hoping merit would restore him to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Luoma Lake silted up; Weihua proposed to River Works Minister Liu Rongsi a canal of more than two hundred li from Suqian to Xuzhou to draw Yellow River water into the grain route, hoping the work would win him restoration.

sentences.zh: 榮嗣然其計，費金錢五十餘萬，工不成，下獄論死，維華意乃沮。

translations.literal: Rongsi approved the plan; more than five hundred thousand taels were spent, the work failed, he was imprisoned and sentenced to death, and Weihua's hopes were dashed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rongsi approved the plan. More than five hundred thousand taels were spent, the work failed, Rongsi was imprisoned and sentenced to death, and Weihua's hopes collapsed.

sentences.zh: 九年，邊事急，都御史唐世濟薦維華邊才，至，下獄遣戍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, with border affairs urgent, Censor-in-Chief Tang Shiji recommended Weihua for border talent; when he arrived he was imprisoned and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, with the frontier in crisis, Censor-in-Chief Tang Shiji recommended Weihua as a border expert; upon arrival he was thrown into prison and sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 維華遂憂憤死。

translations.literal: Weihua thereupon died of grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Weihua died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 福王時，楊維坦翻逆案，為維華等訟冤，章下吏部。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, Yang Weiyuan overturned the treason cases and petitioned to clear Weihua and others; the memorial was sent to the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Yang Weiyuan reopened the treason cases and petitioned to vindicate Weihua and others; the memorial went to the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尚書張捷重述三朝舊事，力稱維華等忠，追賜恤典。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Jie rehearsed old affairs of three reigns and strongly declared Weihua and the others loyal; posthumous honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Jie rehearsed the old scandals of three reigns and declared Weihua and the others loyal men; posthumous honors followed.

sentences.zh: 贈蔭祭葬謚全者，維華及劉廷元、呂純如、楊所修、徐紹吉、徐景濂六人。

translations.literal: Those granted posthumous office, ennoblement, sacrifices, burial, and a full epithet were Weihua, Liu Tingyuan, Lu Chunru, Yang Suoxiu, Xu Shaoji, and Xu Jinglian—six men in all.
translations.idiomatic: Those granted posthumous office, ennoblement, sacrifices, burial, and a full posthumous title were Weihua, Liu Tingyuan, Lu Chunru, Yang Suoxiu, Xu Shaoji, and Xu Jinglian—six men in all.

sentences.zh: 贈蔭祭葬不予謚者，徐大化、範濟世二人。

translations.literal: Those granted posthumous office, ennoblement, sacrifices, and burial but no epithet were Xu Dahua and Fan Jishi—two men.
translations.idiomatic: Those granted posthumous office, ennoblement, sacrifices, and burial but no posthumous title were Xu Dahua and Fan Jishi—two men.

sentences.zh: 贈官祭葬者，徐揚先、劉廷宣、嶽駿聲三人。

translations.literal: Those granted posthumous office and burial honors were Xu Yangxian, Liu Tingxuan, and Yue Junsheng—three men.
translations.idiomatic: Those granted posthumous office and burial honors were Xu Yangxian, Liu Tingxuan, and Yue Junsheng—three men.

sentences.zh: 復官不賜恤者，王紹徽、徐兆魁、喬應甲三人。

translations.literal: Those restored to office without condolence honors were Wang Shaohui, Xu Zhaokui, and Qiao Yingjia—three men.
translations.idiomatic: Those restored to office without condolence honors were Wang Shaohui, Xu Zhaokui, and Qiao Yingjia—three men.

sentences.zh: 他若王德完、黃克纘、王永光、章光嶽、徐鼎臣、徐卿伯、陸澄源，名不麗逆案，而為清議所抑者，亦賜恤有差。

translations.literal: Others such as Wang Dewan, Huang Kezuan, Wang Yongguang, Zhang Guangyue, Xu Dingchen, Xu Qingbo, and Lu Chengyuan, though not listed in the treason cases, had been suppressed by upright opinion; they too received honors in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Others—Wang Dewan, Huang Kezuan, Wang Yongguang, Zhang Guangyue, Xu Dingchen, Xu Qingbo, and Lu Chengyuan—though not named in the treason cases, had been held down by upright opinion; they too received honors in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 徐大化

translations.literal: Xu Dahua
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dahua

sentences.zh: 徐大化，會稽人，家京師。

translations.literal: Xu Dahua was a native of Kuaiji; his family lived in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dahua was a native of Kuaiji, though his family lived in the capital.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士改御史，以京察貶官，再起再貶，至工部主事。

translations.literal: From Hanlin academician he was transferred to censor; demoted in the capital inspection, revived and demoted again, he fell to secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin academician he was transferred to censor; demoted in the capital inspection, revived and demoted again, he sank to secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 孫丕揚典京察，坐不謹落職。

translations.literal: When Sun Piyang conducted the capital inspection, he was dismissed for inattention.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Piyang conducted the capital inspection, Dahua was dismissed for inattention.

sentences.zh: 故事，大計斥退官無復起者。

translations.literal: By precedent, officials expelled in the grand review were never restored.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, officials expelled in the grand review were never restored to office.

sentences.zh: 萬曆末，群邪用事，文選郎陸卿榮破例起之。

translations.literal: Late in Wanli, with wicked men in power, Bureau Director Lu Qingrong broke precedent and revived him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wanli, with wicked men holding sway, Bureau Director Lu Qingrong broke precedent and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，屢遷刑部員外郎，結魏忠賢、劉朝，為之謀主。

translations.literal: Early in Tianqi he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, joined Wei Zhongxian and Liu Chao, and served as their chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he rose repeatedly to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, allied with Wei Zhongxian and Liu Chao, and became their chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 給事中周朝瑞劾其奸貪，御史張新詔抉其閨房之隱，大化頗愧沮。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhou Chaorui impeached him for wicked greed; Censor Zhang Xinzhao exposed secrets of his bedchamber; Dahua was ashamed and discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhou Chaorui impeached him for wicked greed; Censor Zhang Xinzhao laid bare secrets of his private life; Dahua was shamed and disheartened.

sentences.zh: 已，承要人指，力詆熊廷弼。

translations.literal: Then, at the direction of powerful men, he fiercely denounced Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Then, at the bidding of powerful men, he savaged Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 及廷弼入關，又請速誅，與朝瑞相訐，尚書王紀劾罷之。

translations.literal: When Tingbi entered the pass, he again requested swift execution, quarreled with Chaorui, and Minister Wang Ji impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong Tingbi entered the pass, Dahua again demanded swift execution, quarreled with Zhou Chaorui, and Minister Wang Ji impeached and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 尋復罹察典，削職。

translations.literal: Soon he again fell in the inspection cycle and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again failed the inspection cycle and was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，中旨起大理丞，益與魏廣微比，助忠賢為虐。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year an imperial order revived him as Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review; he drew closer to Wei Guangwei and helped Zhongxian in his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year an imperial order revived him as Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review; he grew closer to Wei Guangwei and helped Zhongxian in his cruelties.

sentences.zh: 疏薦邵輔忠、姚宗文、陸卿榮、郭鞏等十三人，即召用。

translations.literal: He memorialized recommending Shao Fuzhong, Yao Zongwen, Lu Qingrong, Guo Gong, and thirteen others in all, and they were immediately summoned.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized recommending Shao Fuzhong, Yao Zongwen, Lu Qingrong, Guo Gong, and thirteen others in all; they were summoned at once.

sentences.zh: 俄遷少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 左僉都御史楊漣等之下獄也，大化獻策於忠賢曰：「彼但坐移宮罪，則無贓可指。

translations.literal: When Left Assistant Censor Yang Lian and the others were imprisoned, Dahua offered a stratagem to Zhongxian, saying, "If they sit only on the Palace Shift charge, no corruption can be cited.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Assistant Censor Yang Lian and the others were thrown into prison, Dahua offered Zhongxian a stratagem: "If they are charged only with the Palace Shift offense, no graft can be pinned on them.

sentences.zh: 若坐納楊鎬、熊廷弼賄，則封疆事重，殺之有名。」

translations.literal: If they are charged with accepting bribes from Yang Hao and Xiong Tingbi, border affairs are weighty matters, and killing them will have a name.
translations.idiomatic: Charge them with taking bribes from Yang Hao and Xiong Tingbi, and the weight of frontier affairs will give the executions a righteous name.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大悅，從之，由是諸人皆不免。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly pleased and followed his advice; thereby none of the men escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was delighted and took his advice—and none of the prisoners escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 尋進左副都御史，歷工部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and served in turn as Left and Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 皇極殿成，加尚書，貪恣無忌，忠賢亦厭之。

translations.literal: When the Huangji Hall was completed he was made Minister; greedy and unrestrained, Zhongxian too grew weary of him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huangji Hall was completed he was made Minister; his greed knew no bounds, and even Zhongxian grew weary of him.

sentences.zh: 七年四月挪移金錢事發，遂勒閑住。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year the misappropriation of funds was exposed, and he was forced into retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventh year his embezzlement came to light, and he was compelled to retire.

sentences.zh: 後入逆案，戍死。

translations.literal: Later he was entered in the treason cases, exiled, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was later listed in the treason cases, banished to frontier service, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 李蕃 李魯生 李恆茂

translations.literal: Li Fan, Li Lusheng, Li Hengmao
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, Li Lusheng, Li Hengmao

sentences.zh: 李蕃，日照人。

translations.literal: Li Fan was a native of Rizhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan was a native of Rizhao.

sentences.zh: 與李魯生皆萬曆四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He and Li Lusheng both passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Lusheng both received their jinshi degrees in the forty-first year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 蕃由廬江知縣入為御史，魯生亦方居垣中，皆為魏忠賢心腹。

translations.literal: Fan entered the Censorate from magistrate of Lujiang; Lusheng too was then serving in the Censorate—they were both Wei Zhongxian's trusted agents.
translations.idiomatic: Fan entered the Censorate from his post as magistrate of Lujiang; Lusheng too was then serving there—both were trusted agents of Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 孫承宗請入朝，蕃以王敦、李懷光為比，承宗遂還鎮。

translations.literal: When Sun Chengzong requested to enter court, Fan compared him to Wang Dun and Li Huai Guang; Chengzong thereupon returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Chengzong asked to come to court, Fan likened him to Wang Dun and Li Huai Guang; Chengzong thereupon returned to his frontier post.

sentences.zh: 朱國禎當國，不為忠賢所喜，蕃希指劾去之。

translations.literal: Zhu Guozhen was directing state affairs and was disliked by Zhongxian; Fan read his intent and impeached him out of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guozhen was directing state affairs and had fallen out of Zhongxian's favor; Fan divined his intent and impeached him from office.

sentences.zh: 同官排擊忠良，多其代草。

translations.literal: In joint attacks on upright men by fellow censors, he drafted many of the memorials for them.
translations.idiomatic: When his colleagues joined in driving out upright officials, he drafted many of their memorials.

sentences.zh: 始與魯生諂事魏廣微，廣微敗，改事馮銓，銓寵衰，又改事崔呈秀，時號兩人為四姓奴。

translations.literal: At first he and Lusheng fawned on Wei Guangwei; when Guangwei fell, they switched to Feng Quan, and when Quan's favor waned, switched again to Cui Chengxiu—people of the time called the two of them "slaves of four surnames."
translations.idiomatic: At first he and Lusheng fawned on Wei Guangwei; when Guangwei fell they transferred their loyalty to Feng Quan, and when Quan's star faded they attached themselves to Cui Chengxiu—people of the time called the pair "slaves of four surnames."

sentences.zh: 出督畿輔學政，建祠天津、河間、真定，呼忠賢九千歲。

translations.literal: Sent out to supervise education in the capital region, he built shrines at Tianjin, Hejian, and Zhending and cried to Zhongxian, "Nine thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Sent out to supervise education in the capital region, he built shrines at Tianjin, Hejian, and Zhending and hailed Zhongxian as "Nine Thousand Years."

sentences.zh: 加太僕卿，視御史事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Imperial Studs while retaining censorial duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Imperial Studs while continuing to perform censorial duties.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，被劾罷。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell, he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian fell, he was impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 魯生，沾化人，知邢臺、邯鄲、儀封、祥符四縣。

translations.literal: Lusheng was a native of Zhanhua and served as magistrate of four counties: Xingtai, Handan, Yifeng, and Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Lusheng was a native of Zhanhua and had served as magistrate of Xingtai, Handan, Yifeng, and Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 擢兵科給事中，由座主廣微通於忠賢，卑汙奸險，常參密謀。

translations.literal: Promoted to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, through his chief examiner Guangwei he gained access to Zhongxian—base, filthy, treacherous, he often took part in secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he gained access to Zhongxian through his chief examiner Guangwei—base, corrupt, and treacherous, he was often party to secret plots.

sentences.zh: 周起元劾朱童蒙，魯生希忠賢指，攻罷起元。

translations.literal: When Zhou Qiyuan impeached Zhu Tongmeng, Lusheng read Zhongxian's intent and attacked until Qiyuan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Qiyuan impeached Zhu Tongmeng, Lusheng divined Zhongxian's wishes and attacked until Qiyuan was driven from office.

sentences.zh: 時中旨頻出，朝端以為憂。

translations.literal: At the time direct orders from the inner court issued frequently, and the court viewed this with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Direct edicts from the inner court were issuing with growing frequency, and the court looked on with alarm.

sentences.zh: 魯生獨上言：「執中者帝，用中者王，旨不從中出而誰出？」

translations.literal: Lusheng alone memorialized: "He who holds the center is the emperor; he who wields the center is the king—if edicts do not issue from the center, from whom do they issue?
translations.idiomatic: Lusheng alone memorialized: "He who holds the center is the emperor; he who applies the center is the king—if edicts do not come from the center, from whom should they come?

sentences.zh: 舉朝大駭。

translations.literal: The whole court was horrified.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court was appalled.

sentences.zh: 內閣缺人，詔舉老成幹濟者。

translations.literal: When the Grand Secretariat lacked personnel, an edict called for recommendations of seasoned and capable men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Secretariat had vacancies, an edict called for nominations of seasoned and capable men.

sentences.zh: 馮銓資淺，年未及四十，魯生、蕃欲令入閣。

translations.literal: Feng Quan's qualifications were shallow and he was not yet forty; Lusheng and Fan wanted to put him in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan's credentials were thin and he was not yet forty, yet Lusheng and Fan wanted to install him in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 魯生遂上言：「成即為老，而非必老乎年。

translations.literal: Lusheng then memorialized: "Seasoned means mature in conduct, not necessarily mature in years.
translations.idiomatic: Lusheng then memorialized: "To be seasoned is to be mature in conduct—not necessarily mature in years.

sentences.zh: 幹乃稱濟，而即有濟於國。」

translations.literal: Capable is what makes one useful—and that is what benefits the state.
translations.idiomatic: To be capable is to be useful—and that is what truly benefits the state.

sentences.zh: 銓果柄用。

translations.literal: Quan was indeed granted power.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was duly given power.

sentences.zh: 時有「十孩兒」之號，魯生其一也。

translations.literal: At the time there was the title "Ten Boys"; Lusheng was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were called the "Ten Boys," and Lusheng was one of them.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦阮大鋮、陳爾翼、張素養、李嵩、張捷輩十一人，悉其私黨。

translations.literal: He once recommended eleven men including Ruan Dacheng, Chen Eryi, Zhang Suyang, Li Song, and Zhang Jie—all his private faction.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended eleven men—Ruan Dacheng, Chen Eryi, Zhang Suyang, Li Song, Zhang Jie, and others—all members of his private faction.

sentences.zh: 疏詆家居大學士韓爌，削其籍。

translations.literal: In a memorial he slandered Han Kuang, Grand Secretary at home on leave, and had him struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he vilified Han Kuang, the Grand Secretary then at home on leave, and had him struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 主事呂下問治徽州吳養春獄，株累者數百家，知府石萬程不能堪，棄官去。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Lü Xiawen handled the Wu Yangchun case in Huizhou; hundreds of families were implicated, and Prefect Shi Wancheng could not endure it and abandoned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Lü Xiawen handled the Wu Yangchun case in Huizhou; hundreds of families were swept up in it, and Prefect Shi Wancheng could bear it no longer and resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 魯生反劾罷萬程。

translations.literal: Lusheng instead impeached and dismissed Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lusheng turned around and impeached Wancheng out of office.

sentences.zh: 遷左給事中，典試湖廣，發策詬楊漣，因歷詆屈原、宋玉等。

translations.literal: Promoted to Left Supervising Secretary, he served as chief examiner for Huguang and in the examination questions reviled Yang Lian, going on to malign Qu Yuan, Song Yu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Supervising Secretary, he served as chief examiner for Huguang and set examination questions denouncing Yang Lian, then went on to revile Qu Yuan, Song Yu, and others.

sentences.zh: 冒寧、錦功，進太僕少卿。

translations.literal: Claiming merit from the Ningyuan and Jinzhou campaigns, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Studs.
translations.idiomatic: By falsely claiming credit for the Ningyuan and Jinzhou campaigns, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Studs.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，魯生知禍及，疏請免漣等追贓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne, Lusheng knew retribution was coming and memorialized asking that the demands for restitution against Lian and the others be waived.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, Lusheng knew the reckoning was near and memorialized asking that the demand for restitution from Lian and the others be dropped.

sentences.zh: 給事中汪始亨、顏繼祖，御史張三謨交章發其奸，始罷去。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Wang Shiheng and Yan Jizu and censor Zhang Sanmo submitted successive memorials exposing his treachery, and he was finally dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Wang Shiheng and Yan Jizu and censor Zhang Sanmo submitted a barrage of memorials exposing his crimes, and he was finally dismissed.

sentences.zh: 御史汪應元再劾之，乃削籍。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Yingyuan impeached him again, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Yingyuan impeached him again, and he was struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 又有李恒茂者，邢臺人。

translations.literal: There was also Li Hengmao, a native of Xingtai.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Li Hengmao, a native of Xingtai.

sentences.zh: 為禮科給事中，薦呈秀復官，與深相得。

translations.literal: As supervising secretary of the Bureau of Rites, he recommended Chengxiu's restoration to office and was on intimate terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: As supervising secretary of the Bureau of Rites, he recommended Chengxiu's restoration to office and was on the closest terms with him.

sentences.zh: 劾罷侍郎扶克儉、太僕少卿孫之益、太常少卿莊欽鄰，皆不附忠賢者也。

translations.literal: He impeached and dismissed Vice Minister Fu Kejian, Vice Director of the Imperial Studs Sun Zhiyi, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhuang Qinlin—all men who would not attach themselves to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and removed Vice Minister Fu Kejian, Vice Director of the Imperial Studs Sun Zhiyi, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhuang Qinlin—all men who refused to attach themselves to Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 恒茂、魯生、蕃日走吏、兵二部，交通請托，時人為之語曰：「官要起，問三李。」

translations.literal: Hengmao, Lusheng, and Fan daily frequented the Ministries of Personnel and War, trading favors and solicitations; people of the time had a saying: "If you want an appointment, ask the Three Lis.
translations.idiomatic: Hengmao, Lusheng, and Fan daily haunted the Ministries of Personnel and War, trading favors and pulling strings; people had a saying: "If you want an appointment, ask the Three Lis.

sentences.zh: 後忽與呈秀交惡，削籍歸。

translations.literal: Later he suddenly fell out with Chengxiu, was struck from the rolls, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he suddenly broke with Chengxiu, was struck from the register, and went home.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，起故官，為御史鄒毓祚劾罷。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell, he was restored to his former post but was impeached and dismissed by censor Zou Yuzuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian fell, he was restored to his former post, only to be impeached and dismissed by censor Zou Yuzuo.

sentences.zh: 逆案既定。

translations.literal: When the treason cases were settled,
translations.idiomatic: When the treason cases were settled,

sentences.zh: 魯生遣戍，蕃、恒茂贖徒為民。

translations.literal: Lusheng was sent into exile; Fan and Hengmao redeemed their penal servitude and became commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Lusheng was banished to frontier service; Fan and Hengmao redeemed their sentences and returned to common life.

sentences.zh: 閻鳴泰

translations.literal: Yan Mingtai
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mingtai

sentences.zh: 閻鳴泰，清苑人。

translations.literal: Yan Mingtai was a native of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mingtai was a native of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination during Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree during the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事，屢遷遼東參政，拾遺被劾罷歸。

translations.literal: Appointed secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, he rose repeatedly to Administer of Liaodong; after submitting a remonstrance he was impeached and dismissed home.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, he rose repeatedly to Administer of Liaodong; after submitting a remonstrance he was impeached and sent home.

sentences.zh: 久之，起僉事，分巡遼海。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was revived as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner to oversee Liaohai.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner with responsibility for Liaohai.

sentences.zh: 開原既失，經略熊廷弼遣撫沈陽，半道慟哭而返。

translations.literal: Once Kaiyuan was lost, Commissioner Xiong Tingbi sent the Grand Coordinator to Shenyang; Mingtai turned back halfway, weeping bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan fell, Military Commissioner Xiong Tingbi dispatched the Grand Coordinator toward Shenyang; Mingtai turned back halfway along the road, weeping bitterly.

sentences.zh: 尋托疾謝歸。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and resigned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he pleaded illness and resigned to go home.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，起故官，監軍山海關。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was revived to his former post to oversee troops at Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was restored to his former post to oversee troops at Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 旋進副使，受知孫承宗，屢疏推薦，而鳴泰實無才略，工諂佞，以虛詞罔上而已。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Vice Commissioner, he won Sun Chengzong's trust and was repeatedly recommended in memorials—but Mingtai in truth had no talent for strategy; he was skilled at flattery and deceit and nothing more than empty words to mislead his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon promoted to Vice Commissioner, he won Sun Chengzong's favor and was repeatedly recommended in memorials—yet Mingtai in truth had no gift for strategy; he was adept at flattery and deceit, offering nothing but empty words to mislead his superiors.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，廷推鳴泰遼東經略，會承宗自請督師，乃擢右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month the court deliberation proposed Mingtai as Liaodong military commissioner; as Chengzong himself requested supreme command, Mingtai was instead promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the eighth month the court deliberation proposed Mingtai as Liaodong military commissioner; but as Chengzong himself requested supreme command, Mingtai was instead promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 自王化貞棄地後，巡撫罷不設。

translations.literal: Since Wang Huazhen abandoned the territory, the post of Grand Coordinator had been abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Huazhen had abandoned the territory, the post of Grand Coordinator had been left unfilled.

sentences.zh: 至是承宗以重臣當關，事權獨操，鳴泰不能有所為。

translations.literal: Now Chengzong held the pass as a senior minister with sole authority; Mingtai could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chengzong held the pass as a senior minister with sole command of affairs; Mingtai could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 明年五月復移疾去，家居三年。

translations.literal: The next year in the fifth month he again pleaded illness and left; he lived at home for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The following year in the fifth month he again pleaded illness and withdrew; he remained at home for three years.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢竊柄，鳴泰潛結之，用御史智鋌薦，召為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian usurped power, Mingtai secretly allied with him; through censor Zhi Ting's recommendation he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian seized power, Mingtai secretly allied with him; through censor Zhi Ting's recommendation he was summoned back as Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，寧遠告警，畿輔震驚。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year the alarm from Ningyuan shook the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year news of danger at Ningyuan sent shock through the capital region.

sentences.zh: 內閣顧秉謙等以順天巡撫吳中偉非禦侮才，薦鳴泰代之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Gu Bingqian and others held that Wu Zhongwei, Grand Coordinator of Shuntian, lacked the talent to repel invasion and recommended Mingtai to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Gu Bingqian and others judged that Wu Zhongwei, Grand Coordinator of Shuntian, lacked the talent to repel invasion and recommended Mingtai to replace him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，代王之臣總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Wang Zhichen as supreme commander of Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Wang Zhichen as supreme commander of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 寧遠敘功，進本部尚書。

translations.literal: Merit from Ningyuan was recorded and he was promoted to Minister of the same ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When merit from Ningyuan was recorded, he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 以繕修山海關城，進太子太傅。

translations.literal: For repairing the walls of Shanhaiguan, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For overseeing repairs to the walls of Shanhaiguan, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，協理戎政。

translations.literal: Soon recalled to court, he coordinated military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon recalled to court, he was put in charge of coordinating military affairs.

sentences.zh: 敘錦州功，加少保。

translations.literal: For the merit at Jinzhou he was given the title Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When credit for Jinzhou was recorded, he was given the title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 三殿成，加少師兼太子太師。

translations.literal: When the three halls were completed, he was made Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the three main halls were completed, he was made Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 熹宗崩，代崔呈秀為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong died, he replaced Cui Chengxiu as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong died, he replaced Cui Chengxiu as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 鳴泰由忠賢再起，專事諂諛。

translations.literal: Mingtai had been restored through Zhongxian and devoted himself entirely to flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Mingtai had been restored through Zhongxian's patronage and devoted himself entirely to flattery.

sentences.zh: 每陳邊事，必頌功德，於薊、遼建生祠，多至七所。

translations.literal: Whenever he discussed border affairs he always praised Zhongxian's merits and virtues; in Ji and Liaodong he built living shrines—as many as seven.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of border affairs he always extolled Zhongxian's merit and virtue; in Ji and Liaodong he built living shrines to him—as many as seven.

sentences.zh: 其頌忠賢，有「民心依歸，即天心向順」語，聞者咋舌。

translations.literal: In praising Zhongxian he used phrases such as "When the people's hearts turn to him, that is Heaven's will turning in favor"—listeners clicked their tongues in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: In praising Zhongxian he wrote that "when the people's hearts turn to him, Heaven's will turns in accord"—listeners were left speechless with astonishment.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，為言者劾罷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was impeached and dismissed by memorialists.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Chongzhen reign he was impeached and driven from office by memorialists.

sentences.zh: 後麗逆案，遣戍死。

translations.literal: Later, listed in the treason cases, he was banished and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was later listed in the treason cases, banished to frontier service, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 生祠之建

translations.literal: The Building of Living Shrines
translations.idiomatic: The Building of Living Shrines

sentences.zh: 生祠之建，始於潘汝禎。

translations.literal: The building of living shrines began with Pan Ruzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The building of living shrines began with Pan Ruzhen.

sentences.zh: 汝禎巡撫浙江，徇機戶請，建祠西湖。

translations.literal: Ruzhen, as Grand Coordinator of Zhejiang, indulged the request of machine households and built a shrine at West Lake.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Coordinator of Zhejiang, Ruzhen indulged a petition from local workshop operators and built a shrine at West Lake.

sentences.zh: 六年六月疏聞於朝，詔賜名「普德」。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year the memorial reached court and an edict granted the name "Pude."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year the memorial reached court, and an edict bestowed the name "Pude."

sentences.zh: 自是，諸方效尤，幾遍天下。

translations.literal: From this, every region imitated the example, until the practice spread nearly across the whole empire.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every region followed suit, until the practice had spread nearly across the entire empire.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，孝陵衛指揮李之才建之南京。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month, Li Zhicai, commander of the Xiaoling Guard, built one in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the tenth month, Li Zhicai, commander of the Xiaoling Guard, built one in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，宣大總督張樸、宣府巡撫秦士文、宣大巡按張素養建之宣府、大同，應天巡撫毛一鷺、巡按王珙建之虎丘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, Xuan-Da Governor Zhang Pu, Xuanfu Grand Coordinator Qin Shiwen, and Xuan-Da touring censor Zhang Suyang built them at Xuanfu and Datong; Yingtian Grand Coordinator Mao Yilu and touring censor Wang Gong built one at Tiger Hill.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, Xuan-Da Governor Zhang Pu, Xuanfu Grand Coordinator Qin Shiwen, and Xuan-Da touring censor Zhang Suyang built shrines at Xuanfu and Datong; Yingtian Grand Coordinator Mao Yilu and touring censor Wang Gong built one at Tiger Hill.

sentences.zh: 二月，鳴泰與順天巡撫劉詔、巡按倪文煥建之景忠山，宣大總督樸、大同巡撫王點、巡按素養又建之大同。

translations.literal: In the second month, Mingtai together with Shuntian Grand Coordinator Liu Zhao and touring censor Ni Wenhuan built one at Jingzhong Mountain; Xuan-Da Governor Pu, Datong Grand Coordinator Wang Dian, and touring censor Suyang built another at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Mingtai together with Shuntian Grand Coordinator Liu Zhao and touring censor Ni Wenhuan built one at Jingzhong Mountain; Xuan-Da Governor Pu, Datong Grand Coordinator Wang Dian, and touring censor Suyang built another at Datong.

sentences.zh: 三月，鳴泰與詔、文煥，巡按御史梁夢環建之西協密雲丫髻山，又建之昌平、通州，太僕寺卿何宗聖建之房山。

translations.literal: In the third month, Mingtai together with Zhao and Wenhuan and touring censor Liang Menghuan built one at Yajishan in western Miyun; others were built at Changping and Tongzhou, and Director of the Imperial Studs He Zongsheng built one at Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Mingtai together with Zhao and Wenhuan and touring censor Liang Menghuan built one at Yajishan in western Miyun; others followed at Changping and Tongzhou, and Director of the Imperial Studs He Zongsheng built one at Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 四月，鳴泰與巡撫袁崇煥又建之寧前，宣大總督樸、山西巡撫曹爾禎、巡按劉弘光又建之五臺山，庶吉士李若琳建之蕃育署，工部郎中曾國禎建之盧溝橋。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Mingtai and Grand Coordinator Yuan Chonghuan built one in the Ning-Qian region; Xuan-Da Governor Pu, Shanxi Grand Coordinator Cao Erzhen, and touring censor Liu Hongguang built one at Mount Wutai; Hanlin academician Li Ruolin built one at the Fanyu Office, and Bureau Director Zeng Guozhen built one at Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Mingtai and Grand Coordinator Yuan Chonghuan built one in the Ning-Qian region; Xuan-Da Governor Pu, Shanxi Grand Coordinator Cao Erzhen, and touring censor Liu Hongguang built one at Mount Wutai; Hanlin academician Li Ruolin built one at the Fanyu Office, and Bureau Director Zeng Guozhen built one at Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 五月，通政司經歷孫如冽、順天府尹李春茂建之宣武門外，巡撫朱童蒙建之延綏，巡視五城御史黃憲卿、王大年、汪若極、張樞、智鋌等建之順天，戶部主事張化愚建之崇文門，武清侯李誠銘建之藥王廟，保定侯梁世勛建之五軍營大教場，登萊巡撫李嵩、山東巡撫李精白建之蓬萊閣、寧海院，督餉尚書黃運泰，保定巡撫張鳳翼、提督學政李蕃、順天巡按文煥建之河間、天津，河南巡撫郭增光、巡按鮑奇謨建之開封，上林監丞張永祚建之良牧、嘉蔬、林衡三署，博平侯郭振明等建之都督府、錦衣衛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Secretariat clerk Sun Rulie and Shuntian prefect Li Chunmao built one outside Xuanwu Gate; Grand Coordinator Zhu Tongmeng built one in Yansui; the five-city touring censors Huang Xianqing, Wang Danian, Wang Ruoji, Zhang Shu, and Zhi Ting built one in Shuntian; Revenue secretary Zhang Huayu built one at Chongwen Gate; Marquis Li Chengming built one at the Medicine King Temple; Marquis Liang Shixun built one at the Five Armies Grand Drill Ground; Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Li Song and Shandong Grand Coordinator Li Jingbai built them at Penglai Pavilion and Ninghai Courtyard; Grain Transport Minister Huang Yuntai, Baoding Grand Coordinator Zhang Fengyi, Education Intendant Li Fan, and Shuntian touring censor Wenhuan built them at Hejian and Tianjin; Henan Grand Coordinator Guo Zengguang and touring censor Bao Qimo built one at Kaifeng; Upper Forest supervisor Zhang Yongzuo built them at the three offices of Livestock, Fine Vegetables, and Forestry; Marquis Guo Zhenming and others built them at the Chief Military Commission and the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Secretariat clerk Sun Rulie and Shuntian prefect Li Chunmao built one outside Xuanwu Gate; Grand Coordinator Zhu Tongmeng built one in Yansui; the five-city touring censors Huang Xianqing, Wang Danian, Wang Ruoji, Zhang Shu, and Zhi Ting built one in Shuntian; Revenue secretary Zhang Huayu built one at Chongwen Gate; Marquis Li Chengming built one at the Medicine King Temple; Marquis Liang Shixun built one at the Five Armies Grand Drill Ground; Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Li Song and Shandong Grand Coordinator Li Jingbai built shrines at Penglai Pavilion and Ninghai Courtyard; Grain Transport Minister Huang Yuntai, Baoding Grand Coordinator Zhang Fengyi, Education Intendant Li Fan, and Shuntian touring censor Wenhuan built them at Hejian and Tianjin; Henan Grand Coordinator Guo Zengguang and touring censor Bao Qimo built one at Kaifeng; Upper Forest supervisor Zhang Yongzuo built them at the Livestock, Fine Vegetables, and Forestry offices; Marquis Guo Zhenming and others built them at the Chief Military Commission and the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 六月，總漕尚書郭尚友建之淮安。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Grain Transport Minister Guo Shangyou built one at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Grain Transport Minister Guo Shangyou built one at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 是月，順天巡按盧承欽、山東巡按黃憲卿、順天巡按卓邁，七月，長蘆巡鹽龔萃肅、淮揚巡鹽許其孝、應天巡按宋禎漢、陜西巡按莊謙，各建之所部。

translations.literal: That month, Shuntian touring censor Lu Chengqin, Shandong touring censor Huang Xianqing, and Shuntian touring censor Zhuo Mai; in the seventh month, Changlu salt censor Gong Cuisu, Huai-Yang salt censor Xu Qixiao, Yingtian touring censor Song Zhenhan, and Shaanxi touring censor Zhuang Qian—each built one in his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Shuntian touring censor Lu Chengqin, Shandong touring censor Huang Xianqing, and Shuntian touring censor Zhuo Mai; in the seventh month, Changlu salt censor Gong Cuisu, Huai-Yang salt censor Xu Qixiao, Yingtian touring censor Song Zhenhan, and Shaanxi touring censor Zhuang Qian—each built one within his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 八月，總河李從心、總漕尚友、山東巡撫精白、巡按黃憲卿、巡漕何可及建之濟寧，湖廣巡撫姚宗文、鄖陽撫治梁應澤、湖廣巡按溫臯謨建之武昌、承天、均州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Grand Canal Director Li Congxin, Grain Transport Minister Shangyou, Shandong Grand Coordinator Jingbai, touring censor Huang Xianqing, and grain-transport censor He Keji built one at Jining; Huguang Grand Coordinator Yao Zongwen, Yunyang pacification commissioner Liang Yingze, and Huguang touring censor Wen Gaomo built them at Wuchang, Chengtian, and Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Grand Canal Director Li Congxin, Grain Transport Minister Shangyou, Shandong Grand Coordinator Jingbai, touring censor Huang Xianqing, and grain-transport censor He Keji built one at Jining; Huguang Grand Coordinator Yao Zongwen, Yunyang pacification commissioner Liang Yingze, and Huguang touring censor Wen Gaomo built shrines at Wuchang, Chengtian, and Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 三邊總督史永安。

translations.literal: Three-front supreme commander Shi Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Three-front supreme commander Shi Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 陜西巡撫胡廷晏，巡按謙、袁鯨建之固原太白山。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Hu Tingyan and touring censors Qian and Yuan Jing built at Mount Taibai near Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Hu Tingyan and touring censors Qian and Yuan Jing built one at Mount Taibai near Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 楚王華奎建之高觀山。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Hua Kui built at Mount Gaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chu Hua Kui built one at Mount Gaoguan.

sentences.zh: 山西巡撫牟誌夔，巡按李燦然、劉弘光建之河東。

translations.literal: Shanxi Grand Coordinator Mou Zhikui and touring censors Li Ranran and Liu Hongguang built in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi Grand Coordinator Mou Zhikui and touring censors Li Ranran and Liu Hongguang built one in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 每一祠之費，多者數十萬，少者數萬，剝民財，侵公帑，伐樹木無算。

translations.literal: The cost of each shrine ran to hundreds of thousands at most and tens of thousands at least, stripping the people's wealth, encroaching on public funds, and felling trees beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Each shrine cost as much as several hundred thousand taels and no less than tens of thousands, stripping the people's wealth, draining the public coffers, and felling trees beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 開封之建祠也，至毀民舍二千餘間，創宮殿九楹，儀如帝者。

translations.literal: When the shrine was built at Kaifeng, more than two thousand commoners' dwellings were demolished, a palace of nine bays was erected, and the rites were like those of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the shrine was built at Kaifeng, more than two thousand commoners' homes were torn down, a palace of nine bays was raised, and the ceremonial arrangements rivaled those reserved for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 參政周鏘、祥符知縣季寓庸恣為之，巡撫增光俯首而已。

translations.literal: Administer Zhou Qiang and Xiangfu magistrate Ji Yuyong carried it out unrestrained; Grand Coordinator Zengguang only bowed his head in acquiescence.
translations.idiomatic: Administer Zhou Qiang and Xiangfu magistrate Ji Yuyong carried it out without restraint; Grand Coordinator Zengguang merely bowed his head and let them have their way.

sentences.zh: 鏘與魏良卿善，祠成，熹宗已崩，猶抵書良卿，為忠賢設滲金像。

translations.literal: Qiang was on good terms with Wei Liangqing; when the shrine was completed—Emperor Xizong had already died—he still sent a letter to Liangqing arranging a mercury-gilded golden image for Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang was on friendly terms with Wei Liangqing; when the shrine was finished—Emperor Xizong had already died—he still wrote to Liangqing to commission a mercury-gilded golden image of Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 而都城數十里間，祠宇相望。

translations.literal: Within several tens of li of the capital, shrines stood within sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Within several tens of li of the capital, shrines stood one within sight of the next.

sentences.zh: 有建之內城東街者，工部郎中葉憲祖竊嘆曰：「此天子幸辟雍道也，土偶能起立乎！」

translations.literal: One was built on East Street inside the inner city; Bureau Director Ye Xianzu sighed privately: "This is the road the Son of Heaven takes when visiting the Imperial Academy—can a clay figure stand up for him?
translations.idiomatic: One was built on East Street inside the inner city; Bureau Director Ye Xianzu sighed to himself: "This is the road the Son of Heaven takes when visiting the Imperial Academy—can a clay idol rise to receive him?

sentences.zh: 忠賢聞，即削其籍。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian heard of it, he immediately had Xianzu struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian heard of it, he immediately had Xianzu struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 上林一苑，至建四祠。

translations.literal: In the Upper Forest alone, four shrines were built.
translations.idiomatic: In the Upper Forest preserve alone, four shrines were built.

sentences.zh: 童蒙建祠延綏，用琉璃瓦。

translations.literal: Tongmeng built a shrine in Yansui using glazed roof tiles.
translations.idiomatic: Tongmeng built a shrine in Yansui roofed with glazed tiles.

sentences.zh: 詔建祠薊州，金像用冕旒。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a shrine built at Jizhou; the gilded statue was given a crown and tassels.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a shrine built at Jizhou, its gilded statue crowned with the regalia of an emperor.

sentences.zh: 幾疏詞揄揚，一如頌聖，稱以「堯天帝德，至聖至神。」

translations.literal: Memorial after memorial praised him in language no different from hymns to the sage-emperor, calling him "Yao's heavenly virtue—most holy, most divine."
translations.idiomatic: Memorial after memorial praised him in the tones of imperial panegyric, calling him "Yao's heavenly virtue—most holy, most divine."

sentences.zh: 而閣臣輒以駢語褒答，中外若響應。

translations.literal: And the Grand Secretaries would answer in parallel prose, inside and outside the court echoing as one.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretaries answered in polished parallel prose, and inside and outside the court the chorus rang as one.

sentences.zh: 運泰迎忠賢像，五拜三稽首，率文武將吏列班階下，拜稽首如初。

translations.literal: Yuntai received Zhongxian's image with five bows and three prostrations, leading civil and military officers to line up below the steps and bow and prostrate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yuntai received Zhongxian's image with five bows and three prostrations, then led civil and military officers to rank themselves below the steps and bow and prostrate in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 已，詣像前，祝稱某事賴九千歲扶植，稽首謝。

translations.literal: Then he went before the image, prayed that such-and-such a matter had relied on the Nine Thousand Years' support, and prostrated in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went before the image, declared that such-and-such a matter had owed everything to the Nine Thousand Years' patronage, and prostrated in thanks.

sentences.zh: 某月荷九千歲拔擢，又稽首謝。

translations.literal: In such-and-such a month he had been favored with promotion by the Nine Thousand Years; again he prostrated in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In such-and-such a month he had been raised in rank by the Nine Thousand Years; again he prostrated in thanks.

sentences.zh: 還就班，復稽首如初禮。

translations.literal: He returned to his place in the ranks and again prostrated as at the first rite.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his place in the ranks and prostrated once more as at the opening ceremony.

sentences.zh: 運泰請以遊擊一人守祠，後建祠者必守。

translations.literal: Yuntai requested that one mobile-detachment commander guard the shrine; thereafter every shrine-builder had to post a guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuntai requested that a mobile-detachment commander be posted to guard the shrine; thereafter every man who built a shrine had to do the same.

sentences.zh: 其孝等方建祠揚州，將上梁，而熹宗哀詔至，既哭臨，釋缞易吉，相率往拜。

translations.literal: Xu Qixiao and others were just building a shrine at Yangzhou and were about to raise the ridge beam when the Xizong Emperor's mourning edict arrived; after weeping at the announcement they shed their mourning garb for auspicious dress and went in a body to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qixiao and others were raising a shrine at Yangzhou and were about to perform the ridge-beam ceremony when the Xizong Emperor's mourning edict arrived; after the public lament they cast off hemp for bright dress and went in a body to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 監生陸萬齡至謂：「孔子作《春秋》，忠賢作《要典》。

translations.literal: Supervising student Lu Wanling even said: "Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals; Zhongxian wrote the Essential Canon.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising student Lu Wanling even declared: "Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals; Zhongxian wrote the Essential Canon.

sentences.zh: 孔子誅少正卯，忠賢誅東林。

translations.literal: Confucius executed Shao Zhengmao; Zhongxian executed the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius executed Shao Zhengmao; Zhongxian destroyed the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 宜建祠國學西，與先聖並尊。」

translations.literal: A shrine should be built west of the Imperial Academy and he should be honored equally with the Sage."
translations.idiomatic: A shrine should be built west of the Imperial Academy, and he should be honored on a par with the Sage."

sentences.zh: 司業朱之俊輒為舉行，會熹宗崩，乃止。

translations.literal: Vice Rector Zhu Zhijun immediately set about carrying this out, but when the Xizong Emperor died the plan was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Rector Zhu Zhijun immediately set the plan in motion, but when the Xizong Emperor died it was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 而華奎、誠銘輩，以藩王之尊，戚畹之貴，亦獻諂希恩，祝厘恐後。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Hua Kui, Cheng Ming, and their like—by the dignity of princes of the blood and the eminence of imperial in-laws—also offered flattery hoping for favor, vying to be first in blessing rites.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Prince Hua Kui, Cheng Ming, and their like—by the dignity of princes of the blood and the eminence of imperial in-laws—also fawned for imperial favor, scrambling to be first at the blessing rites.

sentences.zh: 最後，巡撫楊邦憲建祠南昌，毀周、程三賢祠，益其地，鬻淡臺滅明祠，曳其像碎之。

translations.literal: Last of all, Grand Coordinator Yang Bangxian built a shrine at Nanchang, demolished the shrine to the three sages Zhou and Cheng, enlarged the site, sold off the shrine to Dantai Mieming, dragged out its image and smashed it.
translations.idiomatic: Last of all, Grand Coordinator Yang Bangxian built a shrine at Nanchang, tore down the shrine to the sages Zhou and Cheng, expanded the grounds, sold the shrine of Dantai Mieming, dragged out its image, and smashed it.

sentences.zh: 比疏至，熹宗已崩，莊烈帝且閱且笑。

translations.literal: By the time the memorial arrived, the Xizong Emperor was already dead; the Chongzhen Emperor read it with a smile.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the memorial arrived, the Xizong Emperor was already dead; the Chongzhen Emperor read it and smiled.

sentences.zh: 忠賢覺其意，具疏偽辭，帝輒報允。

translations.literal: Zhongxian sensed his meaning and submitted a memorial with feigned refusal; the emperor at once approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian read his mind and submitted a memorial with a show of declining; the emperor at once assented.

sentences.zh: 無何，忠賢誅，諸祠悉廢，凡建祠者概入逆案雲。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongxian was executed, all the shrines were abolished, and every man who had built one was swept into the treason cases.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhongxian was executed, every such shrine was torn down, and every man who had built one was swept into the treason cases.

sentences.zh: 賈繼春

translations.literal: Jia Jichun
translations.idiomatic: Jia Jichun

sentences.zh: 賈繼春，新鄉人。

translations.literal: Jia Jichun was a native of Xinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Jichun was a native of Xinxiang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 歷知臨汾、任丘二縣，入為御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Linfen and Renqiu, then entered the capital as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Linfen and Renqiu, then entered the capital as a censor.

sentences.zh: 李選侍移噦鸞宮，一時頗逼迫，然故無恙也。

translations.literal: When Consort-select Li was moved from Qianqing Palace, the moment was quite coercive, yet in the end no harm was done.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort-select Li was moved from Qianqing Palace, the moment was harsh enough, yet in the end no harm came of it.

sentences.zh: 繼春聽流言，上書內閣方從哲等，略言：「新君禦極，首導以違忤先皇，逼逐庶母，通國痛心。

translations.literal: Jichun listened to rumor and memorialized the Grand Secretariat and Fang Congzhe and the rest, saying in summary: "The new ruler has just ascended the throne, yet is first led to defy the late emperor and drive out his stepmother—the whole realm is heartsick.
translations.idiomatic: Jichun listened to rumor and memorialized the Grand Secretariat and Fang Congzhe and the rest, saying in summary: "The new ruler has just ascended the throne, yet is first led to defy the late emperor and drive out his stepmother—the whole realm is heartsick.

sentences.zh: 昔孝宗不問昭德，先皇優遇鄭妃，何不輔上取法？

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Xiaozong did not question Lady Zhao's virtue, and the late emperor treated Consort Zheng with favor—why not counsel the emperor to take that as his model?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong once spared Lady Zhao any inquisition, and the late emperor treated Consort Zheng with favor—why not counsel the throne to follow that example?

sentences.zh: 且先皇彌留，面以選侍諭諸臣，而玉體未寒，愛妾莫保。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the late emperor lay at the point of death he spoke face to face with the ministers about the Consort-select, yet before his jade body had cooled his beloved concubine could not be protected.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the late emperor lay dying he spoke face to face with his ministers about the Consort-select, yet before his body had even cooled his beloved concubine could not be protected.

sentences.zh: 忝為臣子，夫獨何心。」

translations.literal: We disgrace ourselves as his subjects—what hearts do we bear?"
translations.idiomatic: We disgrace ourselves as his subjects—what hearts can we claim?"

sentences.zh: 給事中周朝瑞駁之，繼春再揭，謂「選侍雉經，皇八妹入井」，至稱選侍為未亡人。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhou Chaorui rebutted him; Jichun submitted again, saying "the Consort-select hanged herself and the emperor's eighth sister threw herself into a well," going so far as to call the Consort-select a widow.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhou Chaorui rebutted him; Jichun submitted again, claiming "the Consort-select tried to hang herself and the emperor's eighth sister threw herself into a well," going so far as to call the Consort-select a widow.

sentences.zh: 楊漣乃上移宮始末疏，謂：「宸宮未定，先帝之社稷為重，則平日之寵愛為輕。

translations.literal: Yang Lian thereupon submitted a memorial on the whole course of the Palace Shift, saying: "While the imperial residence was unsettled, the late emperor's altars of soil and grain were the weightier concern, and his daily favor the lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lian thereupon submitted a memorial recounting the whole Palace Shift affair, saying: "While the imperial residence was unsettled, the late emperor's altars of soil and grain were the weightier concern, and his daily favor the lighter.

sentences.zh: 及宸居已安，既盡臣子防危之忠，即當體聖主如天之度。

translations.literal: Once the imperial residence was secure, having done all a subject could to ward off peril, one should then embody the sage ruler's heaven-like magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial residence was secure, having done all a subject could to ward off peril, one should then embody the sage ruler's heaven-like magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 臣所以請移宮者如此。

translations.literal: This was why your subject asked for the move.
translations.idiomatic: That is why your subject asked for the move.

sentences.zh: 而蜚語謂選侍踉蹌徒跣，屢欲自裁，皇妹失所投井。

translations.literal: Yet rumor says the Consort-select staggered about barefoot, repeatedly tried to take her life, and the emperor's sister, lost and desperate, cast herself into a well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rumor says the Consort-select staggered about barefoot, repeatedly tried to take her life, and the emperor's sister, lost and desperate, cast herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 恐釀今日之疑端，流為他年之實事。」

translations.literal: I fear this will brew today's suspicions into tomorrow's accepted facts."
translations.idiomatic: I fear this will brew today's suspicions into tomorrow's accepted facts."

sentences.zh: 帝於是宣敕數百言，極言選侍無狀，嚴責廷臣黨庇。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict of several hundred words, declaring at length the Consort-select's misconduct and sternly rebuking the court for shielding her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon issued an edict of several hundred words, declaring at length the Consort-select's misconduct and sternly rebuking the court for shielding her.

sentences.zh: 時繼春出按江西，便道旋裏，馳疏自明上書之故，中有「威福大權，莫聽中涓旁落」語。

translations.literal: At the time Jichun was on inspection tour in Jiangxi; he took a detour home and hurried in a memorial explaining why he had written, including the phrase "the great power of favor and punishment must not be allowed to fall to palace eunuchs on the side."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jichun was on inspection tour in Jiangxi; he took a detour home and hurried in a memorial explaining why he had written, including the phrase "the great power of favor and punishment must not be allowed to fall to palace eunuchs on the side."

sentences.zh: 王安激帝怒，嚴旨切責，令陳狀。

translations.literal: Wang An stirred the emperor to anger; a stern edict sharply rebuked him and ordered a full statement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang An stirred the emperor to fury; a stern edict sharply rebuked him and ordered a full statement.

sentences.zh: 於是御史張慎言、高弘圖連章為求寬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censors Zhang Shenyan and Gao Hongtu submitted memorial after memorial asking leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Censors Zhang Shenyan and Gao Hongtu submitted memorial after memorial asking leniency.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，下廷臣雜議。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier still and referred the matter to the court for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still and referred the matter to the court for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書周嘉謨等言：「臣等意陛下篤念聖母，不能忘選侍。

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Jiamo and the rest said: "We thought Your Majesty deeply cherished the Empress Dowager and could not forget the Consort-select.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Jiamo and the rest said: "We thought Your Majesty deeply cherished the Empress Dowager and could not forget the Consort-select.

sentences.zh: 及誦敕諭，知聖心自體恤。

translations.literal: When we read the edict, we knew the sacred heart already showed compassion of its own.
translations.idiomatic: When we read the edict, we knew the sacred heart already showed compassion of its own.

sentences.zh: 而繼春誤聽風聞，慎言等又連疏瀆奏。

translations.literal: Jichun wrongly listened to rumor, and Shenyan and the rest again submitted repeated memorials in disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: Jichun wrongly listened to rumor, and Shenyan and the rest again submitted repeated memorials in disrespect.

sentences.zh: 然意本無他，罪當宥。」

translations.literal: Yet their intent was otherwise blameless; the offense should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Yet their intent was otherwise blameless; the offense should be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 未報。

translations.literal: No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: No reply came.

sentences.zh: 御史王大年、張捷、周宗建、劉廷宣，給事中王誌道、倪思輝等交章論救，給事、御史復合詞為請，諸閣臣又於講筵救之，乃停慎言、弘圖、大年俸，宥誌道等。

translations.literal: Censors Wang Danian, Zhang Jie, Zhou Zongjian, and Liu Tingxuan, and Supervising Secretaries Wang Zhidao and Ni Sihui and others submitted memorials in turn pleading for mercy; the supervising secretaries and censors jointly petitioned again, and the Grand Secretaries also interceded at the lecture audience—only then were Shenyan, Hongtu, and Danian suspended from salary, while Zhidao and the rest were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Wang Danian, Zhang Jie, Zhou Zongjian, and Liu Tingxuan, and Supervising Secretaries Wang Zhidao and Ni Sihui and others submitted memorials in turn pleading for mercy; the supervising secretaries and censors jointly petitioned again, and the Grand Secretaries also interceded at the lecture audience—only then were Shenyan, Hongtu, and Danian suspended from salary, while Zhidao and the rest were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 既而繼春回奏，詞甚哀，且隱「雉經、入井」二語。

translations.literal: Before long Jichun submitted his reply memorial; the language was very plaintive, and he concealed the two phrases "hanged herself" and "threw herself into a well."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jichun submitted his reply memorial; the language was very plaintive, and he concealed the two phrases "hanged herself" and "threw herself into a well."

sentences.zh: 帝嚴旨窮詰，令再陳。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a stern edict pressing him to the limit and ordered him to state the matter again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a stern edict pressing him to the limit and ordered him to state the matter again.

sentences.zh: 嘉謨等復力救，帝不許。

translations.literal: Jiamo and the rest again pleaded forcefully for mercy; the emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jiamo and the rest again pleaded forcefully for mercy; the emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 繼春益窘，惶恐引罪，言得之風聞。

translations.literal: Jichun grew all the more cornered, confessed in fear and accepted guilt, saying he had heard it on rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Jichun grew all the more cornered, confessed in fear and accepted guilt, saying he had heard it on rumor.

sentences.zh: 乃除名永錮，時天啟元年四月也。

translations.literal: He was struck from the register and permanently imprisoned; this was in the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck from the register and permanently imprisoned; this was in the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 其後言者屢請召還，帝皆不納。

translations.literal: Afterward memorialists repeatedly asked that he be recalled; the emperor never assented.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward memorialists repeatedly asked that he be recalled; the emperor never assented.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，魏忠賢既逐楊漣等，即以中旨召復官。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year, after Wei Zhongxian had driven out Yang Lian and the rest, he recalled Jichun to office by secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year, after Wei Zhongxian had driven out Yang Lian and the rest, he recalled Jichun to office by secret edict.

sentences.zh: 至則重述移宮事，極言：「漣與左光鬥目無先皇，罪不容死。

translations.literal: On arrival he rehearsed the Palace Shift affair at length, declaring: "Lian and Zuo Guangdou looked on the late emperor with contempt; their crime brooked no death.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he rehearsed the Palace Shift affair at length, declaring: "Lian and Zuo Guangdou looked on the late emperor with contempt; their crime brooked no death.

sentences.zh: 且漣因傅櫆發汪文言事，知禍及，故上劾內疏，先發制人，天地祖宗所必殛。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Lian, through Fu Kai, exposed the Wang Wenyan affair and knew disaster was coming, he submitted an impeachment memorial from within the palace first, striking before being struck—an offense Heaven, Earth, and the imperial ancestors would surely smite.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Lian, through Fu Kai, exposed the Wang Wenyan affair and knew disaster was coming, he submitted an impeachment memorial from within the palace first, striking before being struck—an offense Heaven, Earth, and the imperial ancestors would surely smite.

sentences.zh: 而止坐納賄結黨，則漣等當死之罪未大暴天下。

translations.literal: Yet to charge them only with taking bribes and forming factions would leave their capital crimes not fully exposed to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to charge them only with taking bribes and forming factions would leave their capital crimes not fully exposed to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 宜速定爰書布中外，昭史冊，使後世知朝廷之罪漣等以不道無人臣禮也。」

translations.literal: The written verdict should quickly be fixed and published at home and abroad, inscribed in the histories, so that later ages will know the court condemned Lian and the rest for treason and breach of a subject's rites."
translations.idiomatic: The written verdict should quickly be fixed and published at home and abroad, inscribed in the histories, so that later ages will know the court condemned Lian and the rest for treason and breach of a subject's rites."

sentences.zh: 疏娓娓數百言，且請用楊所修言，亟修《三朝要典》，忠賢大喜。

translations.literal: The memorial ran on eloquently for several hundred words; he also asked that Yang Suoxiu's words be adopted and the Three Reigns Essential Canon be compiled at once—Zhongxian was delighted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran on eloquently for several hundred words; he also asked that Yang Suoxiu's words be adopted and the Three Reigns Essential Canon be compiled at once—Zhongxian was delighted.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，繼春方督學南畿，知忠賢必敗，馳疏劾崔呈秀及尚書田吉、順天巡撫單明詡、副都御史李夔龍，群小始自貳。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded, Jichun was supervising education in the Southern Capital region; knowing Zhongxian must fall, he hurried in a memorial impeaching Cui Chengxiu and Ministers Tian Ji, Grand Coordinator of Shuntian Shan Mingxu, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Kuilong—only then did the petty men begin to waver.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded, Jichun was supervising education in the Southern Capital region; knowing Zhongxian must fall, he hurried in a memorial impeaching Cui Chengxiu and Ministers Tian Ji, Grand Coordinator of Shuntian Shan Mingxu, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Kuilong—only then did the petty men begin to waver.

sentences.zh: 旋由太常少卿進左僉都御史，與霍維華輩力扼正人。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted from Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and, with Huo Weihua and their like, strove to suppress upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted from Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and, with Huo Weihua and their like, strove to suppress upright men.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元五月，給事中劉斯球極言其反覆善幻，乃自引歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Chongzhen, Supervising Secretary Liu Siqiu denounced him at length for fickleness and deceit; he thereupon withdrew on his own.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Chongzhen, Supervising Secretary Liu Siqiu denounced him at length for fickleness and deceit; he thereupon withdrew on his own.

sentences.zh: 已，楊漣子之易疏訐之，詔削籍。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Lian's son Zhiyi submitted a memorial denouncing him, and an edict struck him from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Lian's son Zhiyi submitted a memorial denouncing him, and an edict struck him from the register.

sentences.zh: 初，繼春以移宮事詆漣結王安圖封拜，後見公議直漣，畏漣向用，俯首乞和，聲言疏非己意。

translations.literal: At first, over the Palace Shift affair Jichun had slandered Lian for colluding with Wang An to win titles and rewards; later, seeing public opinion vindicate Lian, fearing Lian might return to favor, he bowed his head and sued for peace, claiming the memorial had not expressed his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: At first, over the Palace Shift affair Jichun had slandered Lian for colluding with Wang An to win titles and rewards; later, seeing public opinion vindicate Lian, fearing Lian might return to favor, he bowed his head and sued for peace, claiming the memorial had not expressed his own intent.

sentences.zh: 還朝則極詆漣。

translations.literal: Back at court he savaged Lian all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he savaged Lian all the more.

sentences.zh: 及忠賢殛，又極譽高弘圖之救漣，且薦韓爌、倪元璐，以求容於清議。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian was executed, he in turn lavishly praised Gao Hongtu for saving Lian and even recommended Han Kuang and Ni Yuanlu, seeking acceptance among the upright.
